Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verses 1–5:

This surah is Madani.

The discussion of the basmalah has already been presented.

{1} As for the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah) at the beginning of the surah, the safest course regarding them is to refrain from speculating about their meaning without any textual basis, while affirming with certainty that Allah, exalted is He, did not send them down in vain, but for a wisdom we do not know.

{2} His saying: {That is the Book}; i.e., this great Book, which is the Book in reality, encompassing what the books of the earlier and later generations do not encompass of great knowledge and clear truth; {there is no doubt in it}: there is no doubt in it and no uncertainty in any respect. The negation of doubt about it implies its opposite, for the opposite of doubt and uncertainty is certainty. Thus this Book encompasses the knowledge of certainty (ʿilm al-yaqin), which removes uncertainty and doubt.

This is a beneficial principle: a negation intended as praise must necessarily include its opposite, which is perfection, because negation is an absence, and pure absence contains no praise. Since it encompasses certainty, and guidance is attained only through certainty, He said: {a guidance for the God-conscious}. Guidance (al-huda) is that by which one is guided away from misguidance and dubious matters, and that by which one is guided to walk the beneficial paths.

He said {guidance} and omitted the object, so He did not say: guidance to such-and-such benefit or to such-and-such thing; this is to intend generality, and that it is guidance for all the interests of both abodes. It guides the servants in the matters of the principles of religion (usul) and its branches (furu'), and it clarifies the truth from falsehood and the sound from the weak, and it shows them how to walk the paths beneficial to them in their worldly life and their hereafter. In another place He said: {guidance for mankind}, generalizing; and in this place and elsewhere: {guidance for the God-conscious}, because in itself it is guidance for all people. The wretched did not raise their heads to it, nor did they accept Allah's guidance, so the proof was established against them, and they did not benefit from it because of their wretchedness.

As for the God-conscious (al-muttaqun), who brought the greatest cause for attaining guidance, which is taqwa, whose reality is taking as a shield against the displeasure and punishment of Allah by complying with His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, they were guided by it and benefited to the utmost extent. Allah, exalted is He, said: {O you who believe, if you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion} (Qur'an 8:29). Thus the God-conscious are those who benefit from the Qur'anic verses and the cosmic signs.

Guidance is of two kinds: guidance of clarification (hidayat al-bayan) and guidance of divine enabling (hidayat al-tawfiq). The God-conscious obtained both guidances, while others did not obtain the guidance of enabling, and guidance of clarification without enabling to act upon it is not complete true guidance.

Then He described the God-conscious by their beliefs, their inner acts and their outer acts, since taqwa encompasses these, so He said:

{3} {Who believe in the unseen}. The reality of faith is complete affirmation of what the messengers have reported, implying submission of the limbs. The concern is not with faith in things perceived by the senses, for by that a Muslim is not distinguished from a disbeliever. The concern is with faith in the unseen which we have not seen or witnessed, and we believe in it only on the report of Allah and the report of His Messenger.

This is the faith by which the Muslim is distinguished from the disbeliever, because it is pure affirmation of Allah and His messengers. The believer believes in everything Allah has reported or His Messenger has reported, whether he witnessed it or not, and whether his intellect comprehends it or not. This contrasts with the heretics (al-zanadiqah) who deny the unseen matters, because their deficient and negligent minds have not been guided to them, so they denied what they did not encompass in knowledge; thus their minds became corrupt and their judgments confused, while the minds of the believers who affirm and are guided by Allah's guidance were purified.

Included in faith in the unseen is belief in everything Allah has reported of unseen matters, past and future, the conditions of the hereafter, the realities of Allah's attributes and their modalities, and what the messengers have reported of that. They believe in Allah's attributes and their existence, and are certain of them, even if they do not comprehend their modality.

Then He said: {and establish prayer}. He did not say "perform prayer" or "carry out prayer", because mere performance of its outward form is not sufficient. Establishing prayer is establishing it outwardly, by completing its pillars, obligatory elements and conditions, and establishing it inwardly, by establishing its spirit, which is presence of the heart in it and reflection on what one says and does in it. This is the prayer of which Allah said: {Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing} (Qur'an 29:45), and it is the prayer for which reward is recorded; the servant has from his prayer only what he understands of it. It includes both its obligatory and voluntary forms.

Then He said: {and from what We have provided them, they spend}. This includes obligatory expenditures, such as zakah, maintenance of wives, relatives and slaves, and the like, and recommended expenditures in all avenues of good. He did not mention the recipient because of the multiplicity of its causes and the variety of its recipients, and because spending as such is an act of drawing near to Allah. He used "min" (some of), which indicates partiality, to alert them that He only asks of them a small part of their wealth, which does not harm or burden them, but rather they benefit from spending it, and their brothers benefit from it. In His saying {We have provided them} is an indication that this wealth in your hands is not acquired by your own strength and ownership, but is the provision of Allah, which He has bestowed upon you and favoured you with. Just as He has bestowed favour upon you and preferred you over many of His servants, so thank Him by giving out part of what He has bestowed upon you, and show solidarity with your needy brothers.

Allah frequently combines prayer and zakah in the Qur'an, because prayer includes sincerity toward the One worshipped, and zakah and spending include kindness to His servants. The sign of a servant's happiness is his sincerity toward the One worshipped and his striving to benefit creation, just as the sign of a servant's wretchedness is the absence of these two matters in him, so there is neither sincerity nor kindness.

{4} Then He said: {And who believe in what has been revealed to you}, which is the Qur'an and the Sunnah. Allah, exalted is He, said: {And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom} (Qur'an 4:113). The God-conscious believe in all that the Messenger brought and do not differentiate among what was revealed to him, believing in part of it and disbelieving in part of it, either by denying it or by interpreting it contrary to the intent of Allah and His Messenger, as those innovators do who interpret the texts that contradict their views, with the result of not affirming their meaning even though they affirm their wording; thus they have not believed in them with true belief. His saying {and what was revealed before you} encompasses belief in all the earlier books, and belief in the books entails belief in the messengers and in what they contained, especially the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms. This is the distinctive feature of the believers: they believe in all the heavenly books and all the messengers, and do not differentiate between any of them.

Then He said: {and of the Hereafter they are certain}. The Hereafter is the name for what comes after death. He singled it out for mention after the general statement because belief in the Last Day is one of the pillars of faith, and because it is the greatest incentive to desire, fear and action. Certainty (al-yaqin) is complete knowledge, in which there is no slightest doubt, which necessitates action.

{5} {Those} i.e., those described by these praiseworthy attributes {are upon guidance from their Lord}, i.e., upon a great guidance; because the indefiniteness (in hudan) indicates magnification. What guidance is greater than those mentioned attributes, which encompass sound belief and upright deeds? Is not guidance in reality their guidance, and whatever opposes it is misguidance? He used "ʿala" (upon) in this place, which indicates elevation, and for misguidance He uses "fi" (in), as in His saying: {And indeed, either we or you are upon guidance or in clear misguidance} (Qur'an 34:24), because the possessor of guidance is elevated and raised by it, while the possessor of misguidance is immersed in it and despised.

Then He said: {And those are the successful}. Success (al-falah) is attaining what is sought and being saved from what is feared. He restricted success to them, because there is no path to success except by following their way; whatever lies outside that path are paths of wretchedness, ruin and loss, which lead their travellers to destruction. For this reason, having mentioned the attributes of the truly faithful, He mentioned the attributes of the disbelievers who openly display their disbelief and oppose the Messenger, saying:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verses 1–5:

This surah is Madani.

The discussion of the basmalah has already been presented.

{1} As for the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah) at the beginning of the surah, the safest course regarding them is to refrain from speculating about their meaning without any textual basis, while affirming with certainty that Allah, exalted is He, did not send them down in vain, but for a wisdom we do not know.

{2} His saying: {That is the Book}; i.e., this great Book, which is the Book in reality, encompassing what the books of the earlier and later generations do not encompass of great knowledge and clear truth; {there is no doubt in it}: there is no doubt in it and no uncertainty in any respect. The negation of doubt about it implies its opposite, for the opposite of doubt and uncertainty is certainty. Thus this Book encompasses the knowledge of certainty (ʿilm al-yaqin), which removes uncertainty and doubt.

This is a beneficial principle: a negation intended as praise must necessarily include its opposite, which is perfection, because negation is an absence, and pure absence contains no praise. Since it encompasses certainty, and guidance is attained only through certainty, He said: {a guidance for the God-conscious}. Guidance (al-huda) is that by which one is guided away from misguidance and dubious matters, and that by which one is guided to walk the beneficial paths.

He said {guidance} and omitted the object, so He did not say: guidance to such-and-such benefit or to such-and-such thing; this is to intend generality, and that it is guidance for all the interests of both abodes. It guides the servants in the matters of the principles of religion (usul) and its branches (furu'), and it clarifies the truth from falsehood and the sound from the weak, and it shows them how to walk the paths beneficial to them in their worldly life and their hereafter. In another place He said: {guidance for mankind}, generalizing; and in this place and elsewhere: {guidance for the God-conscious}, because in itself it is guidance for all people. The wretched did not raise their heads to it, nor did they accept Allah's guidance, so the proof was established against them, and they did not benefit from it because of their wretchedness.

As for the God-conscious (al-muttaqun), who brought the greatest cause for attaining guidance, which is taqwa, whose reality is taking as a shield against the displeasure and punishment of Allah by complying with His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, they were guided by it and benefited to the utmost extent. Allah, exalted is He, said: {O you who believe, if you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion} (Qur'an 8:29). Thus the God-conscious are those who benefit from the Qur'anic verses and the cosmic signs.

Guidance is of two kinds: guidance of clarification (hidayat al-bayan) and guidance of divine enabling (hidayat al-tawfiq). The God-conscious obtained both guidances, while others did not obtain the guidance of enabling, and guidance of clarification without enabling to act upon it is not complete true guidance.

Then He described the God-conscious by their beliefs, their inner acts and their outer acts, since taqwa encompasses these, so He said:

{3} {Who believe in the unseen}. The reality of faith is complete affirmation of what the messengers have reported, implying submission of the limbs. The concern is not with faith in things perceived by the senses, for by that a Muslim is not distinguished from a disbeliever. This is the faith by which the Muslim is distinguished from the disbeliever, because it is pure affirmation of Allah and His messengers. The believer believes in everything Allah has reported or His Messenger has reported, whether he witnessed it or not, and whether his intellect comprehends it or not. This contrasts with the heretics (al-zanadiqah) who deny the unseen matters, because their deficient and negligent minds have not been guided to them, so they denied what they did not encompass in knowledge; thus their minds became corrupt and their judgments confused, while the minds of the believers who affirm and are guided by Allah's guidance were purified.

Included in faith in the unseen is belief in everything Allah has reported of unseen matters, past and future, the conditions of the hereafter, the realities of Allah's attributes and their modalities, and what the messengers have reported of that. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 6–7:

{6} God, exalted is He, informs that {Indeed, those who disbelieve}, meaning: those who have attributed disbelief to themselves and been dyed by it, so that it became an enduring description of them, which no deterrent restrains them from and no admonition has effect upon them, that they persist in their disbelief. Thus it is the same for them {whether you warn them or do not warn them, they will not believe}.
The reality of disbelief (kufr) is denial of what the Messenger brought, or denial of part of it. These disbelievers are not benefited by the call except that the proof is established against them. It seems that in this there is a cutting off of the hope of the Messenger ﷺ in their belief, and that you should not grieve over them, nor should your soul go away in regret for them.

Then he mentioned the barriers that prevent them from faith, saying:

{7} {God has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing}; that is, He has stamped them with a stamp that faith does not enter and does not penetrate, so they do not comprehend what benefits them and do not hear what would be of use to them. {And over their eyes is a covering}; that is, a veil and a cover and wrappings that prevent them from the sight that would benefit them. These paths of knowledge and good have been closed off to them, so there is no hope in them and no good to be expected from them. They were only prevented from that and the doors of faith were shut off from them because of their disbelief, their denial, and their obstinacy after the truth had become clear to them, as God, exalted is He, said: {And We turn their hearts and their eyes, just as they did not believe in it the first time}.
This is an immediate punishment. Then he mentioned the deferred punishment, saying: {And for them is a great punishment}, which is the punishment of the Fire and the continuous, perpetual wrath of the Almighty.

Then God, exalted is He, said in describing the hypocrites, whose outward appearance is Islam and whose inward is disbelief:

Then God, exalted is He, said in describing the hypocrites, whose outward appearance is Islam and whose inward is disbelief:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verses 8–10:

{8–9} Know that hypocrisy (nifaq) is the display of good and the concealment of evil, and this definition includes both doctrinal hypocrisy (al-nifaq al-i'tiqadi) and practical hypocrisy (al-nifaq al-amali). Practical hypocrisy is like what the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned in his saying: "The sign of the hypocrite is three: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks it; and when he is entrusted, he betrays." In another narration: "and when he disputes, he is treacherous."

As for doctrinal hypocrisy, which takes one outside the circle of Islam, it is what Allah described the hypocrites with in this surah and elsewhere. Hypocrisy did not exist before the Prophet's (ﷺ) migration from Makkah to Madinah, nor after the migration, until the battle of Badr took place and Allah granted victory and honour to the believers. Then those in Madinah who had not embraced Islam were humbled, so some of them showed Islam out of fear and deception, so that their blood would be spared and their property kept safe. Thus they were among the Muslims outwardly, while in reality they were not of them.

It is from Allah's kindness to the believers that He exposed their conditions and described them with attributes by which they could be distinguished, so that the believers would not be deceived by them, and so that they would also be restrained from many of their wickedness. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The hypocrites fear that a surah will be revealed about them, informing them of what is in their hearts.﴾ Then Allah described them by the root of hypocrisy, saying: ﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers.﴾ They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts, so Allah refuted them by His saying: ﴿but they are not believers﴾, because true faith is that in which the heart and the tongue agree. This is only deception of Allah and of His believing servants. Deception (khida'ah) means that the deceiver shows the one he deceives something while concealing its opposite, so that he may attain his aim from the one he deceives. These hypocrites followed this course with Allah and His servants, yet their deception returned upon themselves. This is one of the wonders, for a deceiver either achieves his deception and attains his aim, or he is neither helped nor harmed. But these hypocrites' deception returned upon themselves, as though they were doing their scheming only to destroy and harm themselves, for Allah is not harmed at all by their deception, and the believing servants are not harmed at all by their plotting. So the believers are not harmed by the hypocrites showing faith; their property is thereby kept safe and their blood spared, while their plotting recoils upon their own necks. They obtain thereby disgrace and exposure in this world, and a constant grief because of the strength and victory the believers attain. Then in the Hereafter they will have a painful, agonizing and afflicting punishment because of their lying, disbelief and wickedness, while they, through their ignorance and folly, are not aware of this.

{10} As for His saying: ﴿in their hearts is a disease﴾, the disease here means the disease of doubt, doubts (shubuhat) and hypocrisy. The heart may be afflicted by two diseases that take it out of its soundness and balance: the disease of false doubts and the disease of destructive desires. Disbelief, hypocrisy, doubts and innovations (bid'ah) all come from the disease of doubts, while fornication, love of indecencies and sins, and committing them come from the disease of desires, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So the one in whose heart is a disease will covet﴾, meaning the desire for fornication. Whoever is spared from these two diseases attains certainty, faith and patience against every sin, and so he dwells in the garments of well-being.

As for His saying about the hypocrites: ﴿in their hearts is a disease, so Allah increased their disease﴾, it shows His wisdom in decreeing sins upon the sinners, and that it is because of their previous sins: He tests them with subsequent sins that necessitate their punishments. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights away, as they did not believe in it the first time﴾, and He said: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾, and He said: ﴿As for those in whose hearts is a disease, it adds to their filth to their filth﴾. Thus the reward of a sin is a sin after it, just as among the reward of a good deed is a good deed after it. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah increases those who are guided in guidance﴾.

For there is no greater corruption than that of one who disbelieves in the signs of Allah, turns others away from the way of Allah, deceives Allah and His friends, allies himself with those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger, and yet claims that this is reform. Acting [in sin] on the earth is corruption because it is a cause of the corruption of what is on the face of the earth of grains, fruits, trees and plants, through the blights that arise from it, which are caused by sins. Moreover, reform on the earth is that it be cultivated with the obedience of Allah and belief in Him. For this reason Allah created the creatures, settled them on the earth, and bestowed provisions upon them, so that they might be helped by them in obeying and worshipping Him. When the opposite is done upon it, it becomes striving in corruption upon it and ruining it from that for which it was created.

{11} That is: when these hypocrites are forbidden from corrupting the earth, which means acting in disbelief and sin, and among it revealing the inner secrets of the believers to their enemy and allying themselves with the disbelievers, they say: ﴿We are only reformers﴾. Thus they combined acting corruptly on the earth with asserting that it is not corruption but reform, inverting the realities and combining the doing of falsehood with believing it to be truth. Their offence is greater than that of one who commits sins while believing them to be forbidden, for the latter is closer to safety and more hopeful of his returning. And since their saying ﴿We are only reformers﴾ confines reform to their own side, and implies that the believers are not people of reform, Allah turned their claim back upon them by His saying:

{12} ﴿Verily, they are the corrupters﴾. For there is no greater corruption than that of one who disbelieves in the signs of Allah, turns others away from the way of Allah, deceives Allah and His friends, allies himself with those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger, and yet claims that this is reform. So is there any corruption beyond this corruption? ﴿But they do not perceive﴾ with a knowledge that benefits them, although they have indeed known this with a knowledge by which the proof of Allah is established against them. Acting [in sin] on the earth is corruption because it is a cause of the corruption of what is on the face of the earth of grains, fruits, trees and plants, through the blights that arise from it, which are caused by sins. Moreover, reform on the earth is that it be cultivated with the obedience of Allah and belief in Him. For this reason Allah created the creatures, settled them on the earth, and bestowed provisions upon them, so that they might be helped by them in obeying and worshipping Him. When the opposite is done upon it, it becomes striving in corruption upon it and ruining it from that for which it was created.

{13} That is: when it is said to the hypocrites, "Believe as the people have believed," meaning like the faith of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them), which is belief in the heart and on the tongue, they say, in their false assumption: "Shall we believe as the foolish have believed?" By "the foolish" they mean—may Allah disfigure them—the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them), because they assume that their foolishness required them to have faith, to abandon their homelands, and to oppose the disbelievers, whereas reason, in their view, requires the opposite of that. Thus they attributed foolishness to them, and implicit in this is that they themselves are the wise, possessors of intellect and sound judgment. Allah rejected this from them and informed that they are, in reality, the foolish ones, because the true meaning of foolishness is a person's ignorance of his own best interests and his striving toward what harms him, and this description applies to them [and is true of them], just as reason and sound judgment are a person's knowledge of his own best interests, his striving toward what benefits him, and his avoidance of what harms him, and this description applies to the Companions and the believers. So the criterion is by attributes and proof, not by bare claims and empty words.

{14} This is from their saying with their tongues what is not in their hearts. When they gathered with the believers, they showed that they were on their way and that they were with them. But when they went alone to their shayatin (satans) — that is, their chiefs and leaders in evil — they said: "Indeed we are with you in reality; we are only mocking the believers by showing them that we are on their way." Such is their inner and outer condition. "And the evil plotting does not encompass anyone except its own people."

{15} He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah mocks them and extends them in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾ This is a recompense for them for their mockery of His servants. Among His mockery of them is that He made attractive to them the wretchedness and the wicked states they were in, until they thought they were with the believers, since Allah had not empowered the believers over them. And among His mockery of them on the Day of Resurrection is that He gives them a apparent light along with the believers; when the believers walk by their light, the light of the hypocrites is extinguished, and they remain in darkness after the light, bewildered. How great is the despair after hope! ﴿They will call out to them, "Were we not with you?" They will say, "Yes, but you led yourselves into temptation, waited, doubted..."﴾ — the verse.

His saying ﴿wayamudduhum﴾ means: He increases them. ﴿Fi tughyanihim﴾ means: in their transgression, that is, their immorality and disbelief. ﴿Ya'mahun﴾ means: they are bewildered and hesitant. This is from His mockery of them, may He be exalted.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 16:

{16} "Those" — that is, the hypocrites described with those attributes — "are the ones who have bought misguidance in exchange for guidance" — that is, they desired misguidance with the desire of a buyer for a commodity, for whose sake he expends precious wealth. This is one of the finest of examples, for it made misguidance, which is the ultimate evil, like a commodity, and made guidance, which is the ultimate good, like the price. So they gave up guidance, desiring to turn away from it, in exchange for misguidance, desiring it. Thus is their trade; how wretched is the trade, and thus is their transaction; how wretched is the transaction.

If one who gives a dinar in exchange for a dirham is a loser, how much more so one who gives a jewel and takes a dirham in return? How much more so one who gives up guidance in exchange for misguidance, chooses wretchedness over happiness, and desires the lowest of matters while abandoning the highest. His trade has not profited; rather he has suffered the greatest loss in it. "Those are the ones who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, that is the clear loss." And His saying: {and they were not guided} is a confirmation of their misguidance and that they gained nothing of guidance. These are their ugly attributes. Then He mentioned their likeness, which reveals them completely, saying:

{17} That is: their likeness, matching their condition, is like the one who kindled a fire. He was in great darkness and in severe need of fire, so he kindled it from another, for it was not stored with him but came from outside him. When the fire lit up what was around him, he saw the place he was in and the dangers in it, and he felt secure and benefited from that fire, and his eye was comforted by it, and he thought he was able to control it. While he was thus, suddenly God took away its light; the light departed from him and joy departed with it, and he remained in the great darkness and the scorching fire. Its brightness went away and its burning remained. So he remained in multiple darknesses: the darkness of night, the darkness of the clouds, the darkness of the rain, and the darkness that comes after the light. How, then, is the state of this described person? Likewise, these hypocrites kindled the fire of faith from the believers, though it was not a quality of theirs, so they were illuminated by it temporarily and benefited. Thereby their blood was protected, their property was safe, and they attained a kind of security in this world. While they were thus, death suddenly overtook them; it stripped them of benefiting from that light, and there came upon them every worry, grief and punishment. There came upon them the darkness of the grave, the darkness of disbelief, the darkness of hypocrisy, and the darkness of sins in their various kinds, and after that the darkness of the Fire, and what an evil abode. Hence God, exalted is He, said about them:

{18} {Deaf}; that is, from hearing good, {dumb}, that is, from speaking it, {blind}, from seeing the truth. {So they will not return}; because they abandoned the truth after they had known it, so they do not return to it. This is unlike one who abandons the truth out of ignorance and misguidance, for he is not reasoned with, and he is closer to returning than they are.

{19} Then God, exalted is He, said: {Or like a rainstorm from the sky}; that is, like the possessor of a rainstorm, which is the rain that pours down, that is, descends in abundance, {in which are darknesses}: the darkness of night, the darkness of the clouds, and the darkness of the rain; and in it {thunder}, which is the sound heard from the clouds; and in it {lightning}, which is the shining flash seen from the clouds.

{20} {Whenever it lights up for them}, the lightning in those darknesses, {they walk in it; and when it becomes dark for them, they stand still}; that is, they halt. Thus is the state of the hypocrites when they hear the Qur'an, its commands and prohibitions, its promise and its warning: they put their fingers in their ears and turn away from its command and prohibition, its promise and its warning. Its warning frightens them, and its promises disturb them, so they turn away from them as much as they can, and they dislike them, like the dislike of the possessor of the rainstorm who hears the thunder and puts his fingers in his ears out of fear of death. This one may well attain safety, but as for the hypocrites, how can they attain safety, when He, exalted is He, encompasses them in power and knowledge, so they cannot escape Him or overcome Him? Rather, He records their deeds against them and recompenses them for them with the fullest recompense.

Since they were afflicted with deafness, dumbness and inner blindness, and the paths of faith were blocked for them, God, exalted is He, said: {And if God willed, He could take away their hearing and their sight}; that is, the sensory ones. In this is a warning and admonition to them of worldly punishment, so that they might beware and refrain from some of their evil and hypocrisy. {Indeed God is over all things competent}; so nothing can overpower Him, and from His power is that when He wills a thing, He does it without any preventer or opponent.

In this verse and similar ones is a refutation of the Qadariyya, who say that their actions are not included within God's power, exalted is He, because their actions are among the things included in His saying: {Indeed God is over all things competent}.

{21} This is a general address to all of mankind, with a general command, which is worship (ʿibādah) in its comprehensive sense: complying with God's commands, avoiding His prohibitions, and affirming His reports as true. Exalted is He, Who commanded them with that for which He created them. He said, Exalted is He: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me﴾. Then He cited, as proof of the obligation to worship Him alone, that He is your Lord, who nurtured you with various kinds of blessings, created you after non-existence, and created those before you.

{22} He bestowed upon you blessings, both apparent and hidden. He made the earth for you a bed (firāsh) on which you settle, and from which you benefit through buildings, agriculture, plowing, and traveling from place to place, along with other aspects of benefit from it. He made the sky a canopy for your dwelling and deposited in it benefits that are among your necessities and needs, such as the sun, the moon, and the stars. ﴿And He sent down water from the sky﴾. The word "sky" (samāʾ) refers to whatever is above you; therefore the exegetes said: the intended meaning of "sky" here is the clouds, from which He, Exalted is He, sent down water, ﴿and brought forth thereby fruits﴾, such as grains and fruits from date palms, fruit trees, crops, and others, ﴿as a provision for you﴾, by which you are provided for, sustained, kept alive, and enjoy. ﴿So do not set up rivals (andād) to God﴾, meaning: equals and peers (ashbāh wa-naẓāʾir) from among created beings, so that you worship them as you worship God, and love them as you love Him, while they are like you: created, provided for, and managed, owning not an atom's weight in the earth or in the heaven, and neither benefiting you nor harming. ﴿And you know﴾ that God has no partner and no equal, neither in creation, provision, and management, nor in divinity and perfection. So how do you worship other gods besides Him while you know this? This is among the most wondrous of wonders and the most foolish of follies.

This verse combines the command to worship God alone, the prohibition of worshipping anything other than Him, and the clear rational proof for the obligation to worship Him alone and the invalidity of worshipping others. This is the mention of Lordship monotheism (tawḥīd al-rubūbiyyah), which entails His singularity in creation, provision, and management. So when every person acknowledges that He has no partner in these, then likewise let there be acknowledgment that God has no partner in His worship. This is the clearest rational proof of the oneness of the Creator, Exalted is He, and the invalidity of association (shirk).

As for His saying ﴿so that you may be God-fearing (laʿallakum tattaqūn)﴾: it may mean that if you worship God alone, you will thereby guard yourselves against His wrath and punishment, because you have brought the cause that repels them. It may also mean that if you worship God, you become among the God-fearing (muttaqūn) who are described by piety (taqwā). Both meanings are sound, and they are mutually entailing. Whoever performs worship completely is among the God-fearing, and whoever is among the God-fearing obtains deliverance from God's punishment and wrath.

{23} This is a rational proof of the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him) and of the soundness of what he brought. He says: ﴿And if you are in doubt﴾, O you who oppose the Messenger, reject his call, and claim that he is a liar, ﴿concerning what We have sent down upon Our servant﴾, whether it is true or otherwise. Here is a matter on which the decision between you and him can be made fairly: he is a human being like you, not of another kind, and you know him since he grew up among you. He cannot write or read, yet he brought you a Book that he claimed was from Allah. You said that he had fabricated it and invented it. If the matter is as you say, then ﴿bring a surah like it﴾, and seek help from whomever among your helpers and witnesses you are able to. This is an easy matter for you, especially since you are people of eloquence and oratory, and have great enmity toward the Messenger. If you bring a surah like it, then it is as you claim. But if you do not bring a surah like it and you utterly fail [﴿and you will never bring a surah like it﴾, but this challenge is made in fairness and as a concession to you], then this is a great sign and a clear, manifest proof of his truthfulness and the truthfulness of what he brought. It becomes binding upon you to follow him and to guard yourselves against the Fire, whose heat and severity are immense, ﴿whose fuel is men and stones﴾. It is not like the fire of this world, which is kindled only with wood. This described Fire is prepared and readied ﴿for the disbelievers﴾ in Allah and His messengers. So beware of disbelief in His Messenger after it has become clear to you that he is the Messenger of Allah.

{24} This verse and similar ones are called the verse of challenge (al-tahaddi), which is the rendering of creation incapable of bringing anything like this Qur'an or of opposing it in any way. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were helpers to one another﴾.
How could a creature made of dust have speech like the speech of the Lord of lords? Or how could the poor one, deficient in every respect, bring speech like the speech of the Perfect One, who possesses absolute perfection and boundless independence in every respect? This is not within possibility or within human capacity. Everyone who has even a little taste and knowledge of the kinds of speech, when he weighs this [great] Qur'an against the speech of other eloquent people, will see the great difference.
In His saying ﴿And if you are in doubt﴾, and to the end of the verse, there is evidence that the one who may be hoped to be guided from error is the doubter who is perplexed, who has not known the truth from falsehood. Such a person, when the truth is made clear to him, is worthy of following it, if he is sincere in seeking the truth. As for the obstinate one who knows the truth and abandons it, his return is not possible, because he has abandoned the truth after it became clear to him. He did not abandon it out of ignorance, so there is no remedy for him. Likewise the doubter who is not sincere in seeking the truth, but turns away and does not strive in the search; such a person, in most cases, will not be granted success.
In describing the Messenger as a servant (ʿabd) in this great station, there is evidence that the greatest of his attributes (may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him) is his fulfillment of servanthood, in which no one among the former or the latter generations can equal him. Likewise, He described him as a servant in the station of the Night Journey, saying: ﴿Glory be to the One who took His servant by night﴾, and in the station of the revelation, saying: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾.

Also in it: the monotheists, even if they commit some major sins, will not abide forever in the Fire, because He said: ﴿prepared for the disbelievers﴾. If the sinful monotheists were to abide in it, it would not be prepared for the disbelievers alone, contrary to the Khawarij and the Mu'tazila. And in it: a proof that punishment is deserved through its causes, which are disbelief and the various kinds of sins, each differing from the others.

If the matter is as you say, then ﴿bring a surah like it﴾, and seek help from whomever among your helpers and witnesses you are able to. This is an easy matter for you, especially since you are people of eloquence and oratory, and have great enmity toward the Messenger. If you bring a surah like it, then it is as you claim. {25} When He mentioned the recompense of the disbelievers, He mentioned the recompense of the believers who do righteous deeds, as is His way in His Book, combining encouragement (tarhib) and warning (tarhib)... 

Correction to the above: the Arabic says "الترغيب والترهيب" which is "encouragement (targhib) and warning (tarhib)." Here is the full translation:

{25} When He mentioned the recompense of the disbelievers, He mentioned the recompense of the believers who do righteous deeds, as is His way in His Book, combining encouragement (targhib) and warning (tarhib), so that the servant may be eager, fearful, hopeful, and apprehensive. So He said: {And give good tidings}; that is: O Messenger, and whoever stands in your station, {to those who have believed} with their hearts {and done righteous deeds} with their limbs. They confirm their faith through their righteous deeds. Acts of goodness are described as "righteous" (ṣāliḥāt) because through them the conditions of the servant are set right, and his affairs of religion and worldly life, his life in this world and in the Hereafter, and through them the corruption of his conditions is removed. Thus he becomes among the righteous (ṣāliḥūn) who are fit to dwell alongside the Most Merciful in His Garden. So give them good tidings {that for them are gardens}; that is: orchards comprising wondrous trees, elegant fruits, extended shade, and branches and boughs. Thus it becomes a garden whose inhabitants are covered by it and whose dweller is pleased in it. {Beneath which rivers flow}; that is: rivers of water, milk, honey, and wine, which they cause to flow however they wish and direct wherever they desire, and from which those trees are watered, so that all kinds of fruit grow. {Whenever they are provided with a fruit therefrom as provision, they say: "This is what we were provided with before"}; that is: this is of its kind and of its description. They are all similar in beauty and delight, with no fruit that is disagreeable, and they have no time free of pleasure; they are constantly enjoying its produce. And His saying {and they are given it in likeness} — it has been said: similar in name but different in taste; and it has been said: similar in color but different in name; and it has been said: some of it resembles other parts in beauty, delight, and enjoyment, and this is perhaps the best view.

Then, having mentioned their dwelling, their sustenance of food and drink, and their fruits, He mentioned their spouses, describing them with the most perfect, concise, and clear description, saying: {And for them therein are purified spouses}. He did not say "purified from such-and-such a defect," so that it encompasses all kinds of purification: they are purified in character, purified in creation, purified in tongue, and purified in gaze. As for their character, they are loving and amiable toward their husbands through good disposition, good conduct as wives, and verbal and practical courtesy. As for their creation, they are purified from menstruation, postnatal bleeding, semen, urine, feces, mucus, saliva, and foul odor. They are also purified in creation through perfection of beauty; there is no defect in them and no ugliness of form, but rather they are "good and beautiful" (khayrāt ḥisān). They are purified in tongue and glance, restricting their gaze to their husbands and restraining their tongues from every ugly speech.

In this noble verse are mentioned the one who gives good tidings, the one who receives them, the thing given as good tidings, and the means that lead to this good tidings. The one giving good tidings is the Messenger (ﷺ) and whoever stands in his station from his community. Those who receive it are the believers who do righteous deeds. The thing given as good tidings is the Gardens described with those attributes. The means leading to it is faith and righteous action; there is no way to attain this good tidings except through both. This is the greatest good tidings, delivered by the best of creation through the best of means. It also indicates the recommendation of giving good tidings to believers and encouraging them to act by mentioning their recompense and fruits, for thereby deeds become light and easy. The greatest joy attained by a person is that Allah grants him success in faith and righteous action; this is the first and foundation of good tidings. After it is the glad tidings at death, and after that, arrival at this everlasting bliss. We ask Allah for His bounty.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 26–27:

{26} The Exalted says: {Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present an example, [even] of a mosquito or what is smaller than it}; that is, whatever example it may be, {a mosquito or what is above it}, because examples contain wisdom and clarify the truth, and Allah is not ashamed of the truth. In this there is an answer to those who denied the striking of examples with lowly things and objected to Allah concerning that. There is no room for objection in it; rather, it is from Allah's teaching to His servants and His mercy toward them, so it must be received with acceptance and gratitude. For this reason He said: {As for those who believe, they know that it is the truth from their Lord}; they understand it and reflect upon it. If they know what it contains in detail, their knowledge and faith increase thereby; otherwise they know that it is true, and that what it contains is true, even if the aspect of truth in it is hidden from them, because they know that Allah did not strike it in vain but for a far-reaching wisdom and an abundant blessing. {And as for those who disbelieve, they say: "What did Allah intend by this as an example?"}; they raise objections and become bewildered, and so their disbelief increases upon their disbelief, just as the believers' faith increases upon their faith. For this reason He said: {By it He leads many astray and by it He guides many}; this is the condition of believers and disbelievers at the descent of the Qur'anic verses. The Exalted said: {And whenever a surah is revealed, among them are some who say, "Which of you has this increased in faith?" As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice. But as for those in whose hearts is disease, it has increased them in evil upon their evil, and they died while they were disbelievers} [9:124–125]. There is no greater blessing upon the servants than the descent of the Qur'anic verses, yet with this it becomes for some people a trial, bewilderment, misguidance, and an increase of evil upon their evil, and for others a gift, mercy, and an increase of good upon their good. Glory be to Him who differentiates among His servants and alone possesses guidance and misguidance.

Then He mentioned His wisdom and justice in His misguidance of whom He misguides, saying: {And He misguides thereby none except the defiantly disobedient}; that is, those who go out of obedience to Allah and are stubborn toward the messengers of Allah, those whose attribute has become defiant disobedience, who do not seek any substitute for it. Therefore His wisdom required their misguidance, due to their unfitness for guidance, just as His grace and wisdom required the guidance of those characterized by faith and adorned with righteous deeds.

Defiant disobedience (fisq) is of two kinds: a kind that expels one from religion, which is the defiance that necessitates exit from faith, as mentioned in this verse and similar ones; and a kind that does not expel one from faith, as in His saying: {O you who have believed, if a defiant person comes to you with information, then verify it...} [49:6]; the verse.

Then He described the defiantly disobedient, saying:

{27} {Those who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification}; this encompasses the covenant between them and their Lord and the covenant between them and the creation, which He affirmed upon them with heavy pledges and obligations. They do not heed those pledges but break them, abandon His commands, commit what He has forbidden, and break the agreements between them and the creation. {And they sever what Allah has commanded to be joined}; this includes many things. Allah commanded us to join what is between us and Him by faith in Him and devotion to His worship; what is between us and His Messenger by faith in him, love for him, honoring him, and fulfilling his rights; and what is between us and parents, relatives, companions, and all of creation by fulfilling their rights, which Allah commanded us to uphold. As for the believers, they joined what Allah commanded to be joined of these rights and upheld them most completely. As for the defiantly disobedient, they severed them, cast them behind their backs, substituting for them defiance, severance, and acts of disobedience, which is corruption on the earth. {Those}; that is, whoever has this attribute {are the losers}; in this world and the Hereafter. Loss is restricted to them because their loss is general in all their conditions, and they have no kind of gain, since every righteous deed is conditioned upon faith; whoever has no faith has no deed. This loss is the loss of disbelief. As for the loss that may be disbelief, may be disobedience, or may be negligence in abandoning a recommended act, mentioned in His saying: {Indeed, mankind is in loss} [103:2], this is general to every creature except those who are characterized by faith, righteous deeds, mutual exhortation to truth, and mutual exhortation to patience. Its reality is the loss of the good that the servant was aiming to attain while it was within his capacity.

Then the Exalted said:

{28} This is a rhetorical question expressing astonishment, rebuke and denial. That is: how can disbelief in God occur from you, when He created you from non-existence, bestowed upon you various kinds of blessings, then causes you to die when your appointed terms are complete, and requites you in the graves, then brings you back to life after the resurrection and the rising up, and then to Him you will be returned, and He will requite you with the complete recompense? So when you are under His disposal, His management and His kindness, and under His religious commands, and after that under His requital, is it fitting for you to disbelieve in Him? Is this anything but great ignorance and profound foolishness? Rather, what befits you is that you fear Him, thank Him, believe in Him, dread His punishment, and hope for His reward.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 29:

{29} I.e., He created for you, out of His kindness and mercy toward you, everything that is on the earth, for you to benefit from, enjoy, and take heed from.

This noble verse is evidence that the basic principle regarding things is permissibility and purity, since it is presented in the context of bestowing favour. Excluded from this are the impure things (al-khaba'ith), for their prohibition is also derived from the implication of the verse and from the explanation of its purpose: that He created them for our benefit. Whatever is harmful is therefore excluded from that. And among the completeness of His blessing is that He forbade us from the impure things, as a means of purifying us. His words:

﴿Then He turned to the heaven and made them seven heavens; and He is Knowing of all things﴾.

"Istawa" (turned to, directed Himself) occurs in the Qur'an with three meanings. Sometimes it is not followed by a preposition, and then its meaning is perfection and completion, as in His words about Musa: ﴿And when he reached his maturity and was perfected﴾. Sometimes it means "to rise high and be elevated," which is the case when it is followed by "ʿala" (on), as in His words, Exalted is He: ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾, and ﴿that you may sit firmly upon its back﴾. Sometimes it means "to intend" or "to turn toward," which is the case when it is followed by "ila" (to), as in this verse. That is, when God Exalted created the earth, He turned toward creating the heavens, and made them seven heavens; He fashioned them, perfected them, and made them firm, and He is Knowing of all things. He knows what enters the earth and what comes out of it, what descends from the sky and what ascends into it, and He knows what you conceal and what you disclose; He knows the secret and what is even more hidden.

He frequently links His creation with the affirmation of His knowledge, as in this verse and in His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Should not He who created know? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware﴾; because His creating of creatures is the most evident proof of His knowledge, wisdom, and power.

{30} This begins the account of the creation of Adam (peace be upon him), father of mankind, and his excellence, and that when God Most High willed to create him, He informed the angels of this, and that God would appoint him as successor (khalifah) on the earth. The angels (peace be upon them) said: "Will You place in it one who will cause corruption therein through sins and shed blood?" This is a specification after a generalization, to show the severity of the corruption of killing. This was according to their assumption that the successor placed on the earth would produce such things from himself. So they exalted the Creator above that and glorified Him, and informed Him that they were engaged in the worship of God in a manner free of corruption, and they said: ﴿while we glorify You with Your praise﴾; i.e., we declare You free of imperfection in a manner befitting Your praise and majesty; ﴿and sanctify You﴾. It may be that its meaning is "and sanctify You," in which case the lam (in lak) conveys specification and sincerity. It may also be that it means "and sanctify ourselves for You," i.e., we purify them with beautiful character traits such as love of God, fear of Him, and magnifying Him, and we purify them from base character traits. ﴿He said﴾; God said to the angels: ﴿Indeed, I know﴾; of this successor ﴿what you do not know.﴾ Because your speech is according to what you assumed, whereas I have knowledge of the outward and the inward. I know that the good resulting from the creation of this successor is many times greater than the evil contained within it. Even if there were nothing in it except that God Most High wills to choose from among them prophets, the truthful ones, the martyrs and the righteous, and that His signs may become manifest to creation, and that there may result from it acts of worship that would not have occurred without the creation of this successor, such as jihad and other things, and that what is hidden in the dispositions of the accountable beings of good and evil may become manifest through trial, and that His enemy may be distinguished from His ally, and His party from His opponent, and that what was concealed in the soul of Iblis of the evil which he harbored and was characterized by may become manifest. These are great wisdoms, of which some suffice for this.

Then, since the statement of the angels (peace be upon them) contained an allusion to their excellence over the successor whom God would place on the earth, God Most High willed to show them of Adam's excellence what would make them recognize his merit and the perfection of God's wisdom and knowledge.

{31} ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them﴾; i.e., the names of things and of what is named by them. He taught him the name and the named, i.e., the words and their meanings, including the diminutive of names and the augmentative, such as qas'ah and quzay'ah (both meaning a bowl). ﴿Then He presented them﴾; i.e., He presented the named things ﴿to the angels﴾ as a test for them, to see whether they would know them or not. ﴿He said: "Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful"﴾; in your statement and your assumption that you are superior to this successor.

{32} ﴿They said: "Glory be to You"﴾; i.e., we declare You free of any objection from us to You, or of opposition to Your command. ﴿We have no knowledge﴾; in any respect ﴿except what You have taught us﴾; out of Your grace and generosity. ﴿Indeed, You are the Knowing, the Wise﴾; the Knowing who has encompassed all things in knowledge, so that nothing is hidden from Him, and not an atom's weight in the heavens or the earth escapes Him, nor anything smaller than that or greater. The Wise: the One who possesses perfect wisdom from which no creature is excluded and from which no one commanded deviates. He created nothing except for a wisdom, and commanded nothing except for a wisdom, and wisdom is placing a thing in its proper place.
Thus they acknowledged and confessed God's knowledge and wisdom, and their own inability to know even the least thing, and their acknowledgment of God's favor upon them and His teaching them what they did not know.

{33} Then God said: ﴿O Adam, inform them of their names﴾; i.e., the names of the named things that God presented to the angels, which they were unable to know. ﴿So when he informed them of their names﴾; the angels saw the excellence of Adam over them, and the wisdom and knowledge of the Creator in appointing this successor. ﴿He said: "Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth"﴾; which is what is hidden from us so that we do not witness it. Since He knows the unseen, the witnessed is all the more so by priority. ﴿And I know what you reveal and what you have been concealing.﴾

{34} Then God Most High commanded them to prostrate to Adam, honoring and magnifying him and as an act of servitude to God Most High. They complied with God's command and all hastened to prostrate, ﴿except Iblis; he refused﴾; he refused to prostrate and was arrogant toward God's command, and about Adam he said: ﴿"Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?"﴾ This refusal and arrogance of his was the result of the disbelief that he harbored. Thus his enmity toward God and toward Adam, his disbelief and his arrogance became manifest.
In these verses are lessons and signs: the affirmation that God speaks, that He has never ceased to be speaking, saying what He wills and speaking as He wills, and that He is All-Knowing and All-Wise. And in them: when the servant finds God's wisdom in some of the creatures and commands obscure to him, it is obligatory for him to submit, to distrust his own intellect, and to affirm to God the attribute of wisdom. And in them: God's care for the angels and His kindness to them by teaching them what they did not know and alerting them to what they had not known.
And in them is the excellence of knowledge in several respects:
Among them: that God made His angels recognize His knowledge and wisdom.
Among them: that God made them recognize Adam's excellence through knowledge, and that it is the most excellent attribute that can be in a servant.
Among them: that God commanded them to prostrate to Adam in honor of him when the excellence of his knowledge became evident.
Among them: that when a test is administered to others and they are unable to meet it, and then the one of excellence informs them of it, this is more perfect than if he had informed them from the outset.
Among them: taking heed from the condition of the two parents of mankind and of the jinn, the explanation of Adam's excellence, God's bounties upon him, Iblis's enmity toward him, and other lessons.

{30} This begins the account of the creation of Adam (peace be upon him), father of mankind, and his excellence, and that when God Most High willed to create him, He informed the angels of this, and that God would appoint him as successor (khalifah) on the earth. The angels (peace be upon them) said: "Will You place in it one who will cause corruption therein through sins and shed blood?" {35} When Allah created Adam and favoured him, He completed His blessing upon him by creating from him a wife, so that he might find tranquillity in her and be at ease with her. So whoever among you follows My guidance,

by believing in My messengers and My books and being guided by them, and that is by affirming all the reports of the messengers and books and by complying with the command and abstaining from the prohibition, ﴿there shall be no fear upon them, nor shall they grieve﴾; and in the other verse, ﴿whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be distressed﴾.

The negation of fear, of grief, and the difference between them: for what is disliked, if it has already passed, produces grief, and if it is still awaited, produces fear. He negated both for those who follow the guidance, and when both are negated, their opposite is attained, which is complete security.

{39} Likewise: the negation of misguidance and wretchedness for those who follow His guidance; and when these are negated, their opposites are established, which are guidance and happiness. Whoever follows His guidance attains security, worldly and otherworldly happiness, and guidance, and every disliked thing is removed from him: fear, grief, misguidance and wretchedness. Thus he attains what is desired and is protected from what is feared. This is the opposite of one who does not follow His guidance, but disbelieves in it and denies His signs; ﴿those are the companions of the Fire﴾, that is, those who are constant in it, like a companion to his companion and a creditor to his creditor, ﴿they will abide therein forever﴾, not leaving it, and their punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be given respite.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verses 40–43:

{40} {O Children of Israel}: By "Israel" is meant Ya'qub (peace be upon him). The address is directed to the groups of the Children of Israel who were in Madinah and its surroundings, and it includes those who came after them. He then commands them with a general command, saying: {Remember My favour which I bestowed upon you}. This includes all the blessings, some of which will be mentioned in this surah. Remembering them is by the heart, through acknowledgment; by the tongue, through praise; and by the limbs, through using them in what He loves and is pleased with. {And fulfil My covenant}: this is what He covenanted with them concerning faith in Him, His messengers, and establishing His law. {I will fulfil your covenant}: this is the recompense for that. What is meant by this is what Allah mentioned in His saying: {And Allah had already taken the covenant of the Children of Israel, and We raised among them twelve chiefs. And Allah said, "Indeed, I am with you. If you establish prayer and give zakah and believe in My messengers..."} up to His saying: {then he has certainly strayed from the sound way}. Then He commanded them with the factor that moves them to fulfil His covenant, which is awe of Him, the Exalted, and fear of Him alone, for whoever fears Him, his fear of Him obliges him to obey His command and avoid His prohibition. Then He commanded them with the specific matter without which their faith is not complete and not valid, saying:

{41} {And believe in what I have sent down}: this is the Qur'an which He sent down to His servant and messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). So He commanded them to believe in it and follow it, and this necessarily entails believing in the one upon whom it was sent down. He mentioned the incentive to their belief, saying: {confirming what is with you}; that is, in agreement with it, not opposing it nor contradicting it. Since it agrees with what is with you of the Scriptures and does not oppose them, there is no obstacle for you to believe in it, for it came with what the messengers came with, so you are more worthy than anyone to believe in it and affirm it, being the People of the Book and knowledge.

Also, in His saying {confirming what is with you} there is an indication that if you do not believe in it, that will return upon you as denial of what is with you, because what it brought is what Musa, Isa and other prophets brought, so your denial of it is a denial of what is with you.

Also, in the Scriptures that are in your hands there is the description of this Prophet who brought this Qur'an, and the glad tidings of him. So if you do not believe in him, you have denied part of what was sent down to you, and whoever denies part of what was sent down to him has denied all of it, just as whoever disbelieves in one messenger has denied all the messengers. When He commanded them to believe in it, He forbade them and warned them against its opposite, which is disbelief in it, saying: {And be not the first to disbelieve in it}; that is, in the Messenger and the Qur'an. His saying {the first to disbelieve in it} is more emphatic than His saying "and do not disbelieve in it," because if they were the first to disbelieve in it, there would be in that their hastening to disbelief, the reverse of what is fitting for them, and their sin would fall upon them along with the sin of those who follow them after them.

So they sold them for the verses of Allah, preferred them and gave them precedence. {And Me alone}; that is, not other than Me, {fear}; for if you fear Allah alone, His fear obliges you to put faith in His verses before the small price, just as if you choose the small price, that is evidence of the departure of taqwa from your hearts. Then He said:

{42} {And do not mix}; that is, do not confound {the truth with falsehood, nor conceal the truth}. He forbade them from two things: mixing truth with falsehood, and concealing the truth. Whoever confounds truth with falsehood, not distinguishing this from that while knowing it, and conceals the truth that he knows and is commanded to make manifest, is among the callers to Hell, for people do not follow in matters of their religion anyone other than their scholars. So choose for yourselves one of the two states.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 44:

{44} ﴿Do you enjoin righteousness upon the people while you forget yourselves, and you recite the Book? Will you not then reason?﴾ That is: enjoining faith and goodness, while you neglect yourselves, leaving them from doing that, when the situation is such that you recite the Book. ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾

Reason ('aql) is so named because one restrains (ya'qilu) by it what benefits him of good, and is restrained (yan'aqilu) by it from what harms him. This is because reason urges its possessor to be the first to do what he commands and the first to abstain from what he forbids. So whoever enjoins others to do good but does not do it himself, or forbids them from evil but does not abandon it himself, shows the absence of his reason and his ignorance, especially if he knows this and the proof has been established against him. Although this verse was revealed concerning the case of the Children of Israel, it is general for everyone, due to the words of the Most High: ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? It is greatly hateful in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do.﴾

The verse does not imply that a person who does not carry out what he is commanded to do should abandon enjoining good and forbidding evil. It indicates rebuke concerning the two obligations. Otherwise, it is well known that a person has two obligations: enjoining others and forbidding them, and enjoining himself and forbidding himself. Neglecting one of them is not a concession for neglecting the other. Perfection is for a person to fulfill both obligations, and complete deficiency is to abandon both. As for fulfilling one without the other, it is not at the rank of the first, but it is below the last. Also, souls are naturally inclined not to submit to one whose deeds contradict his words, so their being guided by actions is more effective than their being guided by bare words.

{45} God commanded them to seek help in all their affairs through patience in all its forms: patience in obeying God until one performs the obedience, patience in refraining from disobeying God until one abandons the disobedience, and patience in the painful decrees of God, so that one does not become resentful of them. Patience and restraining the self upon what God has commanded patience for is a great aid in every matter. And whoever seeks to be patient, God will grant him patience. Likewise prayer (al-salah), which is the balance of faith and which forbids indecency and wrongdoing, is a means of seeking help in every matter. {And indeed it}, i.e., prayer, {is burdensome} i.e., difficult, {except for the humble}; for it is easy and light for them, because humility (khushu') and fear of God and hope for what is with Him make its performance a matter of an expanded breast, as they anticipate its reward and fear its punishment. This is unlike one who is not like that, for he has no motive that calls him to it, and when he performs it, it becomes among the heaviest things upon him.

Humility (khushu') is the submission of the heart, its tranquility and stillness before God Most High, and its being broken before Him in abasement, need, and faith in Him and in meeting Him. For this reason He said:

{46} {Those who are certain} i.e., who are convinced {that they will meet their Lord}; so He will recompense them for their deeds, {and that to Him they will return}. This is what makes acts of worship light for them, grants them consolation in calamities, relieves them of distresses, and restrains them from committing evil deeds. For these there is everlasting bliss in lofty chambers. As for one who does not believe in meeting his Lord, prayer and other acts of worship are among the hardest things for him.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verses 49–57:

{49–54} This begins an enumeration, in detail, of His blessings upon the Children of Israel.

He said: ﴿And [recall] when We saved you from the people of Pharaoh﴾; that is, from Pharaoh, his chiefs, and his soldiers, and they had been, before that, ﴿subjecting you to the worst torment﴾; that is, they assigned you to and made you serve in the most severe form of it, such that ﴿they slaughtered your sons﴾ out of fear of your growth, ﴿and spared your women﴾; that is, they did not kill them. Thus you were caught between the slain and those humiliated by hard labor, the women spared in a manner of condescension and domination over them, and this is the utmost humiliation. So Allah bestowed upon them complete deliverance and the drowning of their enemy while they were watching, so that their eyes might be comforted. ﴿And in that [deliverance] was a tremendous trial from your Lord﴾; that is, the deliverance was a great favor from your Lord. This is what obligates you to gratitude and to carrying out His commands.

Then He mentioned His favor upon them through His promise to Moses of forty nights, so that He might send down to them the Torah, containing great blessings and abundant benefits. Then they did not show patience before the appointed term was complete, and they worshipped the calf after him; that is, after his departure. ﴿And you were wrongdoers﴾; knowing of your wrongdoing, with the proof established against you, so your crime was greater and your sin more grave.

Then He commanded you to repent through the tongue of His prophet Moses, by having some of you kill others; so Allah pardoned you because of that, ﴿that perhaps you would be grateful﴾ to Allah.

{55} ﴿And [recall] when you said, "O Moses, we will never believe you until we see Allah plainly"﴾. This is the utmost audacity toward Allah and His messenger. ﴿So the thunderbolt seized you﴾; either death or a severe swoon, ﴿while you were looking on﴾; each one looking at his companion as it occurred.

{56} ﴿Then We revived you after your death, that perhaps you would be grateful﴾. Then He mentioned His blessing upon them in the wilderness, the desert devoid of shade, and the abundance of provision, saying:

{57} ﴿And We shaded you with clouds and sent down upon you the manna and the quail﴾. Manna is a comprehensive term for every good provision that comes without toil, including ginger, truffles, bread, and other things. The quail is a small bird known as the sammani, whose meat is delicious; so there would descend upon them from the manna and the quail what sufficed them and sustained them. ﴿Eat of the good things with which We have provided you﴾; that is, a provision whose like is not obtained by the affluent people of cities. Yet they did not thank Allah for this blessing, and they persisted in hardness of heart and abundance of sins. ﴿And they did not wrong Us﴾; meaning, by those actions contrary to Our commands, for Allah is not harmed by the disobedience of the disobedient, just as He is not benefited by the worship of the worshippers. ﴿But they were wronging themselves﴾; so its harm returns upon them.

{55} ﴿And [recall] when you said, "O Moses, we will never believe you until we see Allah plainly"﴾. This is the utmost audacity toward Allah and His messenger. ﴿So the thunderbolt seized you﴾; either death or a severe swoon, ﴿while you were looking on﴾; each one looking at his companion as it occurred.

{57} ﴿And We shaded you with clouds and sent down upon you the manna and the quail﴾. Manna is a comprehensive term for every good provision that comes without toil, including ginger, truffles, bread, and other things. The quail is a small bird known as the sammani, whose meat is delicious; so there would descend upon them from the manna and the quail what sufficed them and sustained them. ﴿Eat of the good things with which We have provided you﴾; that is, a provision whose like is not obtained by the affluent people of cities. This is also one of His favours upon them after their disobedience of Him. He commanded them to enter a town that would be for them a source of honour, a homeland and a dwelling, and in which they would obtain abundant provision; and that their entering should be in a manner of submission to God, both in action and in speech. In action: entering the gate prostrating (sujjadan), that is, humbly submissive and abased. In speech: that they should say, "Hittah" (حطة), meaning: that He should remove from them their sins, by their asking Him for forgiveness. "We will forgive you your sins" (﴿نغفر لكم خطاياكم﴾) by your asking for forgiveness, "and We will increase the good-doers" (﴿وسنزيد المحسنين﴾) by their deeds, that is, a reward both in this world and in the next.

"But those who wronged" (﴿فبدل الذين ظلموا﴾) from among them. He did not say "so they changed" (فبدلوا), because not all of them changed. "A saying other than that which had been said to them" (﴿قولاً غير الذي قيل لهم﴾): they said "habbah fi hintah" (حبة في حنطة, "a grain in wheat") instead of "Hittah," mocking the command of God and ridiculing it. If they changed the saying, despite its lightness, then changing the action is all the more and more fitting (min bab awla wa-ahra) for that. For this reason they entered crawling on their backsides (يزحفون على أدبارهم). And since this transgression was the greatest cause for God's punishment befalling them, He said: "So We sent down upon those who wronged" (﴿فأنزلنا على الذين ظلموا﴾) from among them "a plague" (﴿رجزاً﴾), that is, a punishment (عذاباً) "from the sky" (﴿من السماء﴾), because of their defiance (فسقهم) and their rebellion (بغيهم).
