{60} "Istasqa" means he asked on their behalf for water for them to drink. {"So We said: Strike the rock with your staff."} This may be a specific, known rock that he knew of, or it may be a generic noun.
{"And there gushed forth from it twelve springs."} The tribes of the Children of Israel numbered twelve.
{"Every people knew their drinking place."} That is, the place from these springs where each of them would drink, so that none of them crowded out the others; rather, they drank it in ease and comfort, not in distress. For this reason He said: {"Eat and drink of the provision of Allah."} That is, which He gave you without effort or toil. {"And do not commit corruption on the earth, spreading mischief."} That is, do not cause ruin in the manner of spreading corruption.

{61} That is: remember when you said to Musa, showing weariness toward the blessings of Allah and contempt for them: "We will not be patient with one kind of food," that is, one type of food, even though, as mentioned before, their varieties were many, but they did not change. "So call upon your Lord for us to bring forth for us from what the earth grows: its herbs," that is, its plants that do not stand upon a stem as trees do, "and its cucumbers," which are the cucumbers, "and its garlic," that is, its garlic, "and its lentils, and its onions," which are well known. Musa said to them: "Would you exchange what is lower," which is the foods mentioned, "for what is better," which is the manna and the quail. This is not fitting for you, for these foods you requested, wherever you descended into any city, you would find them; but your food with which Allah favoured you is the best of foods and the most noble, so how can you seek a substitute for it?

Since what occurred from them was the greatest proof of their lack of patience and their contempt for the commands of Allah and His blessings, He recompensed them in kind for their deeds, saying: "And humiliation and wretchedness were stamped upon them," the humiliation which is seen on the outward appearance of their bodies, "and wretchedness" in their hearts, so their souls were not honourable, nor did they have lofty aspirations; rather their souls were debased souls, and their aspirations the basest of aspirations. "And they returned with anger from Allah," that is, the spoils with which they returned and in which they succeeded were nothing but that they returned bearing His wrath upon them; how wretched is the spoil of their spoils, and how wretched is their condition. "That," the reason for which they deserved His anger, "is because they used to disbelieve in the signs of Allah," which indicate the truth and make it clear to them; when they disbelieved in them, He punished them with His anger upon them and with what they were doing: "and killed the prophets without right." His saying "without right" is for added condemnation, since it is known that killing prophets is never with right; but it is so that one does not think they acted out of ignorance or lack of knowledge. "That is because they disobeyed," by committing the acts of disobedience to Allah, "and used to transgress," against the servants of Allah; for sins drag one another along. Heedlessness gives rise to a minor sin, then from it arises a greater sin, then from it arise kinds of innovation, disbelief and other things. So we ask Allah for well-being from every affliction.

Know that the address in these verses is to the community of the Children of Israel who existed at the time of the revelation of the Qur'an, and these actions mentioned were addressed to them, though they were the deeds of their forefathers, and they were attributed to them for many benefits.

Among them: they used to praise themselves, purify themselves, and claim their superiority over Muhammad and those who believed in him. So Allah clarified from the conditions of their predecessors, which were established among them, what would make clear to each one of them that they are not among the people of patience, noble character, and lofty deeds. If this was the condition of their predecessors, even though it is presumed that they were more deserving and higher in status than those after them, then how should one judge the addressees!

Among them: the blessing of Allah upon the earlier ones among them is a blessing that reaches the later ones, and a blessing upon the fathers is a blessing upon the sons, so they were addressed with it, because these are blessings that encompass and include them.

Among them: addressing them with the actions of others indicates that a community united upon one religion supports and aids one another in their interests, so that their earlier and later generations are as if they were at one time, and what happens from some of them is as if it happened from all of them; because what some of them do of good returns to the benefit of all, and what some of them do of evil returns to the harm of all.

Among them: most of their actions were not denounced by them, and one who is pleased with disobedience is a partner of the one who disobeys, along with other wisdoms known only to Allah.

Then He, exalted, said, judging between the groups of the People of the Book:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 62:

{62} This ruling concerning the People of the Book is specific to them, because the Sabians, according to the sound view, are among the sects of the Christians. Allah informed that the believers of this nation, the Jews, the Christians and the Sabians, whoever believes in Allah [among them] and the Last Day and affirms their messengers, then for them is the great reward, and security, ﴿and no fear shall befall them, nor shall they grieve﴾. As for whoever among them disbelieves in Allah, His messengers and the Last Day, his state is the opposite of this; for him is ﴿fear and grief﴾.

And the sound view is that this ruling applies among these groups as such, not in relation to belief in Muhammad, for this is a report about them before the mission of Muhammad, and this is the established content of their conditions. This is the method of the Qur'an: when some doubts enter some souls upon the context of the verses, you will certainly find something that removes that doubt, because it is a revelation from One who knows things before their existence, and "His mercy encompasses all things."

That, and Allah knows best, is because when He mentioned the Children of Israel and censured them, and mentioned their disobedience and ugly deeds, it may have occurred to some souls that all of them are encompassed by the blame. So the Creator, exalted is He, wished to clarify who among them is not touched by the blame by means of his description. And since the mention of the Children of Israel specifically could also give the impression of exclusivity to them, He, exalted is He, mentioned a general ruling encompassing all the groups, so that the truth becomes clear and the delusion and confusion disappear. So glory be to the One who deposited in His Book what dazzles the minds of all the worlds.

Then, blessed and exalted is He, returned to rebuke the Children of Israel for what their predecessors did:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 63–64:

{63} That is: remember when We took your covenant, {when We took your covenant}; a heavy pact, emphasized by the threat of raising Mount Sinai (al-Tur) above them, and it was said to them, {Take what We have given you} from the Torah {with strength}; that is, with earnestness and diligence, and patience in carrying out the commands of God, {and remember what is in it}; that is, what is in your Book, by reciting it and learning it, {so that you may be God-fearing (tattaqun)}; from the punishment and wrath of God, or so that you may be among the people of taqwa (God-consciousness).

{64} After this emphatic affirmation, {you turned away (tawallaytum)}; and you turned aside, and that was something that would have made the greatest punishments befall you, but {had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, you would surely have been among the losers}.

{66} ﴿an example for those present before it﴾; that is, for the nations present at it and those of their time who received news of it, ﴿and for those after it﴾; that is, for those who come after them, so that it would stand as a proof of Allah against the servants, and that they would refrain from His disobedience. But it is not a beneficial admonition except for the God-fearing; as for others, they do not benefit from the signs.

{67} That is: remember what happened to you with Musa (Moses), when you killed a person and then disputed about him, that is, you pushed the blame onto one another and disagreed about his killer, until the matter grew serious among you, and great evil was nearly about to befall you between yourselves had Allah not made it clear to you. Musa said to you, to make clear the killer: "Slaughter a cow." It was obligatory to hasten to carry out his command and not to object to it. But they refused except to object, and said: ﴿Do you make a mockery of us?﴾ The Prophet of Allah said: ﴿I seek refuge in Allah from being among the ignorant.﴾ For the ignorant is the one who speaks words that have no benefit, and who mocks people. As for the wise person, he sees that among the greatest defects that disgrace religion and intellect is mocking one who is a human being like himself, even if he has been favoured over him, for that favour requires from him gratitude to his Lord and mercy toward His servants. When Musa said that to them, they knew it was the truth, and they said:

{68} ﴿Ask your Lord for us to make clear to us what it is.﴾ That is, what its description is. ﴿He said: "He says it is a cow neither old nor young,"﴾ that is, neither aged, ﴿nor virgin,﴾ that is, neither young. ﴿Between these two, so do what you are commanded﴾, and leave off strictness and obstinacy.

{69} ﴿They said: "Ask your Lord for us to make clear to us what its colour is." He said: "He says it is a yellow cow, bright in its colour,"﴾ that is, intensely so, ﴿gladdening those who look at it,﴾ because of its beauty.

{70} ﴿They said: "Ask your Lord for us to make clear to us what it is, for cows look alike to us, and we, if Allah wills, will surely be guided."﴾ So we did not find our way to what you want, ﴿and we, if Allah wills, will surely be guided.﴾

{71} ﴿He said: "He says it is a cow not broken to plough the earth,"﴾ that is, made tame by work, ﴿nor irrigating the field,﴾ that is, not a water-drawing cow, ﴿sound, with no mark on it,﴾ that is, free of defects or of work, ﴿with no colour in it other than its described colour already mentioned.﴾ ﴿They said: "Now you have brought the truth,"﴾ that is, the clear explanation. This is from their ignorance, for he had already brought them the truth the first time. Had they objected to any cow at all, the purpose would have been achieved, but they made it strict by asking many questions, so Allah made it strict for them. Had they not said "if Allah wills," they would not have been guided to it either. ﴿So they slaughtered it,﴾ that is, the cow described with those attributes, ﴿and they almost did not do it.﴾ This was because of the obstinacy that had occurred from them.

{72–73} ﴿When you slew a person and disputed about it, and Allah brought forth what you were concealing.﴾ So We said to them: "Strike him with part of it," that is, with a part of it, whether a specific part or any part of it, since specifying it brings no benefit. They struck him with part of it, and Allah brought him to life and brought forth what they had been concealing, so he informed them of his killer. In his revival, while they were watching, there was a sign showing that Allah revives the dead, ﴿so that you may understand,﴾ and thus restrain yourselves from what harms you.

{74} ﴿Then your hearts became hard,﴾ that is, they became rigid and coarse, so that admonition had no effect on them, ﴿after that,﴾ that is, after Allah had bestowed on you great blessings and shown you the signs. Your hearts should not have hardened, because what you witnessed should have caused tenderness of heart and submission. Then He described their hardness as ﴿like stones,﴾ which are harder than iron, because iron and lead melt when heated in fire, unlike stones. His words ﴿or even harder﴾ mean that their hardness does not fall short of the hardness of stones; the word "or" here is not in the sense of "rather." Then He mentioned the virtue of stones over their hearts, saying: ﴿Indeed, among stones there are some from which rivers gush forth, and indeed among them there are some that split open so water comes out of them, and indeed among them there are some that fall down out of fear of Allah.﴾ By these matters your hearts were inferior. Then Allah, exalted is He, gave them the most severe warning, saying: ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do,﴾ rather He knows it, preserving the small and the great of it, and He will recompense you for it with the most complete and perfect recompense.

Know that many of the exegetes, may Allah have mercy on them, have greatly filled their commentaries with the stories of the Children of Israel, and have applied Qur'anic verses to them, making them an explanation of the Book of Allah, citing his saying (ﷺ): "Narrate from the Children of Israel, and there is no harm." What I see is that although it is permissible to relate their reports in a manner where they stand alone, not joined to or applied to the Book of Allah, it is absolutely not permissible to make them an explanation of the Book of Allah when they are not authentically transmitted from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Their rank, as he (ﷺ) said: "Do not believe the People of the Book, nor disbelieve them," is that they are doubtful. Since their rank is that they are doubtful, and since it is known necessarily from the religion of Islam that the Qur'an must be believed in and held with certainty in its words and meanings, it is not permissible to make those stories transmitted through unknown narrations, whose falsehood or the falsehood of most of them is considered likely, into definite meanings of the Book of Allah. No one doubts this, but through heedlessness about it what happened occurred. And Allah is the Granter of success.

Then He described their hardness as ﴿like stones,﴾ which are harder than iron, because iron and lead melt when heated in fire, unlike stones. His words ﴿or even harder﴾ mean that their hardness does not fall short of the hardness of stones; the word "or" here is not in the sense of "rather." Then He mentioned the virtue of stones over their hearts, saying: ﴿Indeed, among stones there are some from which rivers gush forth, and indeed among them there are some that split open so water comes out of them, and indeed among them there are some that fall down out of fear of Allah.﴾ By these matters your hearts were inferior. Then Allah, exalted is He, gave them the most severe warning, saying: ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do,﴾ rather He knows it, preserving the small and the great of it, and He will recompense you for it with the most complete and perfect recompense.

Know that many of the exegetes, may Allah have mercy on them, have greatly filled their commentaries with the stories of the Children of Israel, and have applied Qur'anic verses to them, making them an explanation of the Book of Allah, citing his saying (ﷺ): "Narrate from the Children of Israel, and there is no harm." What I see is that although it is permissible to relate their reports in a manner where they stand alone, not joined to or applied to the Book of Allah, it is absolutely not permissible to make them an explanation of the Book of Allah when they are not authentically transmitted from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Their rank, as he (ﷺ) said: "Do not believe the People of the Book, nor disbelieve them," is that they are doubtful. No one doubts this, but through heedlessness about it what happened occurred. And Allah is the Granter of success.

{67} That is: remember what happened to you with Musa (Moses), when you killed a person and then disputed about him, that is, you pushed the blame onto one another and disagreed about his killer, until the matter grew serious among you, and great evil was nearly about to befall you between yourselves had Allah not made it clear to you. Musa said to you, to make clear the killer: "Slaughter a cow." It was obligatory to hasten to carry out his command and not to object to it. But they refused except to object, and said: ﴿Do you make a mockery of us?﴾ The Prophet of Allah said: ﴿I seek refuge in Allah from being among the ignorant.﴾ For the ignorant is the one who speaks words that have no benefit, and who mocks people. As for the wise person, he sees that among the greatest defects that disgrace religion and intellect is mocking one who is a human being like himself, even if he has been favoured over him, for that favour requires from him gratitude to his Lord and mercy toward His servants. When Musa said that to them, they knew it was the truth, and they said:

{68} ﴿Ask your Lord for us to make clear to us what it is.﴾ That is, what its description is. ﴿He said: "He says it is a cow neither old nor young,"﴾ that is, neither aged, ﴿nor virgin,﴾ that is, neither young. ﴿Between these two, so do what you are commanded﴾, and leave off strictness and obstinacy.

{69} ﴿They said: "Ask your Lord for us to make clear to us what its colour is." He said: "He says it is a yellow cow, bright in its colour,"﴾ that is, intensely so, ﴿gladdening those who look at it,﴾ because of its beauty.

{70} ﴿They said: "Ask your Lord for us to make clear to us what it is, for cows look alike to us, and we, if Allah wills, will surely be guided."﴾ So we did not find our way to what you want, ﴿and we, if Allah wills, will surely be guided.﴾

{71} ﴿He said: "He says it is a cow not broken to plough the earth,"﴾ that is, made tame by work, ﴿nor irrigating the field,﴾ that is, not a water-drawing cow, ﴿sound, with no mark on it,﴾ that is, free of defects or of work, ﴿with no colour in it other than its described colour already mentioned.﴾ ﴿They said: "Now you have brought the truth,"﴾ that is, the clear explanation. This is from their ignorance, for he had already brought them the truth the first time. Had they objected to any cow at all, the purpose would have been achieved, but they made it strict by asking many questions, so Allah made it strict for them. Had they not said "if Allah wills," they would not have been guided to it either. ﴿So they slaughtered it,﴾ that is, the cow described with those attributes, ﴿and they almost did not do it.﴾ This was because of the obstinacy that had occurred from them.

{75} This is a cutting off of the hopes of the believers regarding the faith of the People of the Book; that is, do not hope for their faith, and their character does not warrant hoping for them. For they used to distort the words of God after they had understood and known them, placing for them meanings which God did not intend, in order to make people believe that they were from God, when they were not from God. So if this is their condition with their Book, which they regard as their honour and their religion, by which they turn people away from the way of God, then how can faith from them be hoped for you?! This is among the most distant of things.

{76} Then he mentioned the condition of the hypocrites among the People of the Book, saying: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe."﴾ So they displayed faith to them verbally with their tongues, while what was in their hearts was otherwise. ﴿But when they are alone with one another﴾; when there was no one present from outside their religion, some of them said to others: ﴿"Do you speak to them of what God has opened to you?"﴾; that is, do you show them faith and tell them that you are like them? That would become a proof for them against you, as they would say that they have acknowledged that what we are upon is true and what they are upon is false, and so they would argue against you with that before your Lord. ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾; that is, will you not have intellect so that you would refrain from what is a proof against you?

{77} This is what some of them say to others: ﴿Do they not know that God knows what they conceal and what they reveal?﴾ Even if they conceal what they believe among themselves, and presume that by concealing it no argument of the believers can reach them, this is an error on their part and a great ignorance; for God knows their secret and their open conduct, and He makes manifest to His servants what they are upon.

{78} ﴿And among them﴾; that is, among the People of the Book, ﴿are the unlettered﴾; that is, the common folk, who are not of the people of knowledge, ﴿who do not know the Book except as wishful fancies﴾; that is, they have no share of God's Book except recitation alone, and they have no knowledge of what the earlier ones have, who know their condition with true knowledge. These only have conjectures and imitation of their people of knowledge. 

So in these verses He mentioned their scholars, their common folk, their hypocrites, and those among them who did not become hypocrites. {79} The Exalted warns those who distort the Book, who say, with their distortion and what they write: {This is from Allah}. Thus they wronged people in two ways: by confusing their religion for them, and by taking their wealth without right, rather, by the most blatant falsehood. [This] is greater than one who takes it by usurpation, theft, or the like. Shaykh al-Islam (Ibn Taymiyyah), when mentioning these verses from His saying: "Do you hope..." up to "they earn," said: "Allah has censured those who distort words from their places. This encompasses whoever bends the Book and the Sunnah to what he has founded of false innovations. He also censured those who do not know the Book except as wishful fancies, and this encompasses whoever abandons contemplation of the Qur'an and knows only the mere recitation of its letters. It also encompasses whoever writes a book with his own hand contrary to the Book of Allah to gain worldly benefit, and then says: 'It is from Allah,' such as saying: 'This is the Shari'ah and the religion, this is the meaning of the Book and the Sunnah, this is the [understanding] of the Salaf and the Imams, and this is the foundation of religion which must be believed individually or collectively.' It also encompasses whoever conceals what he has of the Book and the Sunnah, lest his opponent argue with it against the truth he says. These matters are very numerous among the people of desires in general, such as the Rafidah [and the Jahmiyyah and others among the people of desires and kalam, and among the people of desires] and in detail, like many of those affiliated with the jurists..."

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verses 80–82:

{80} He mentioned their ugly deeds, then mentioned, along with this, that they purify themselves (yuzakkun anfusahum), testifying for themselves to deliverance from the punishment of God and success in His reward, and that the Fire will not touch them except for a number of days (ayyaman ma'dudatan), i.e., a few days, countable on the fingers. Thus they combined wrongdoing with a sense of security. Since this was merely a claim, God responded to them, saying: {Say}, O Messenger, to them: {Have you taken a covenant with God?} (i.e., by faith in Him, His messengers, and obedience to Him), for this promise that brings deliverance to its holder is one that does not change or alter. {Or do you say about God what you do not know?} Thus God informed that the truth of their claim depends on one of these two matters, which have no third:

Either they have taken a covenant with God, in which case their claim is correct;

or they are fabricating against Him, in which case their claim is false, and this is more severe for their disgrace and punishment. And it is known from their state that they have not taken a covenant with God, because of their denial of many of the prophets, to the extent that they reached the point of killing a group of them, and because of their refusal to obey God and their breaking of covenants. It is therefore established that they are fabricators, inventing and speaking about God what they have no knowledge of, and speaking about God without knowledge is among the greatest of forbidden acts and the most abominable of ugly deeds.

Then God mentioned a general ruling for everyone, which includes the Children of Israel and others, and it is the ruling besides which there is no ruling, not their wishes and claims about the attributes of the destroyed and the saved. So He said: {Nay}, i.e., the matter is not as you have mentioned, for that is a statement without reality. Rather:

{81} {Whoever earns an evil deed}: and it is an indefinite noun in a conditional context, so it encompasses shirk and what is below it. What is meant here is shirk, by the evidence of His saying: {and his sin has encompassed him}, i.e., it has surrounded its doer and left him no outlet, and this can only be shirk, for one who has faith is not encompassed by his sin. {Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.}

The Kharijites have used this verse as evidence for the disbelief of the one who commits a sin, but it is evidence against them, as you can see, for it is clearly about shirk. Likewise, every person who is false (mubtil) argues with a verse or a authentic hadith in support of his false view; it must be that what he argues with is a proof against him.

{82} {And those who believed}: in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, {and did righteous deeds}; and deeds are not righteous except with two conditions: that they be sincerely for the sake of God's Countenance, and that they follow the Sunnah of His Messenger.

The sum of these two verses is that the people of deliverance and success are the people of faith and righteous deeds, while the people who are destroyed are the people of the Fire, the polytheists who associate partners with God and the disbelievers in Him.

{83} These laws are among the fundamental principles of religion, which God commanded in every revelation, because they include the general benefits suited to every time and place. Therefore abrogation (naskh) does not apply to them, just as it does not apply to the core of religion. This is why God commanded us with them in His words: {Worship God and associate nothing with Him}; to the end of the verse.

As for His words: {And when We took the covenant from the Children of Israel}; this is from their hardness, for every command they were given they resisted, and they would not accept it except with binding oaths and firm pledges. {You shall worship none but God}; this is a command to worship God alone and a prohibition of associating anything with Him. This is the foundation of religion, for no deeds are accepted if this is not their basis. This is the right of God the Exalted over His servants. Then He said: {And to parents, kindness}; that is, show kindness to parents. This encompasses every kind of kindness, verbal and practical, that is a benefit to them. It also contains a prohibition of mistreating parents, or of neglecting kindness and mistreating them; for kindness is obligatory, and a command to do something is a prohibition of its opposite. Kindness has two opposites: mistreatment, which is the greater sin, and abandoning kindness without mistreatment, which is forbidden but not necessarily placed on the same level as the first.

The same applies to maintaining ties with relatives, orphans, and the needy. The details of kindness cannot be confined to counting; rather they are bounded by the general limit, as has been mentioned. Then He commanded kindness toward people in general, saying: {And speak to people kindly}.

Among good speech is commanding what is right, forbidding what is wrong, teaching knowledge, extending greetings, showing a cheerful face, and all other good words. Since a person cannot embrace people with his wealth, he was commanded with something by which he can be kind to every creature, namely kindness in speech. Included in this is a prohibition of foul speech toward people, even toward disbelievers. This is why God the Exalted said: {And do not dispute with the People of the Book except in the best manner}. Among the courtesy with which God trained His servants is that a person should be pure in his words and deeds, neither obscene, nor vulgar, nor abusive, nor quarrelsome; rather he should have good character, wide forbearance, be accommodating to everyone, and patient with the harm he receives from people, in obedience to God's command and hoping for His reward.

Then He commanded them to establish prayer and give zakat, since it has been mentioned that prayer includes sincerity toward the One worshipped, and zakat includes kindness to servants. Then, after this, He said: "To you I have given these good commands, which, when a discerning and intelligent person considers them, he recognizes that among God's kindness to His servants is that He commanded them with these and graced them with them." And He took covenants from you. {Then you turned away}; in a manner of aversion. For one who turns away may turn with the intention of returning to what he turned from, but these people had no desire or intention to return to these commands. We seek refuge in God from abandonment. His words {except a few of you} are an exception, so that it is not thought that they all turned away; He informs that a few of them, God protected and made steadfast.

{84–85} This act mentioned in this verse was committed by those who lived at the time of the revelation in Medina. The Aws and the Khazraj, who are the Ansar, were polytheists before the mission of the Prophet (ﷺ), and they used to fight one another in the manner of the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance). Three groups of the Jews settled among them: Banu Qurayzah, Banu al-Nadir, and Banu Qaynuqa'. Each Jewish group had an alliance with one of the groups of the people of Medina. So whenever they fought, each Jew would help his ally against his opponents, whom the other Jewish group supported. Thus a Jew would kill a Jew, and expel him from his home when there was exile and plunder. Then, when the war laid down its burdens, and captives had been taken between the two parties, they would ransom one another. All three of these matters had been made obligatory for them: it was obligatory for them that none of them shed the blood of another, nor expel one another, and when they found a captive from among them, it was obligatory upon them to ransom him. They acted upon the last and abandoned the first two. So God denounced them for this, saying: ﴿Do you believe in part of the Book﴾, which is the ransoming of the captive, ﴿and disbelieve in part﴾, which is the killing and the expulsion. In this there is evidence that faith requires performing the commands and avoiding the prohibitions, and that the obligatory matters are part of faith. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Then what is the recompense of those among you who do that except disgrace in the life of this world?﴾ This did occur, and God disgraced them, and He gave His Messenger power over them, so he killed those who were to be killed, took captive those who were to be taken captive among them, and expelled those who were to be expelled. ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will be returned to the most severe punishment﴾, that is, its greatest form. ﴿And God is not unaware of what you do.﴾ Then He, the Exalted, informed about the cause that necessitated for them disbelief in part of the Book and belief in part of it, saying:

{86} ﴿Those are the ones who have bought the life of this world at the price of the Hereafter.﴾
They imagined that if they did not help their allies, shame would befall them, so they chose the Fire over shame. Therefore He said: ﴿So their punishment will not be lightened, nor will they be helped.﴾ Rather, it remains at its severity, and they will not attain relief at any time, ﴿nor will they be helped﴾, that is, no harm will be repelled from them.

{87} The Exalted grants a favor upon the Children of Israel in that He sent to them His interlocutor, Musa (Moses), and gave him the Torah. Then He followed him with messengers after him who judged by the Torah, until He concluded their prophets with ʿĪsā (Jesus) son of Maryam, peace be upon him, and gave him clear signs such that mankind could believe on the like of them. {And We strengthened him with the Holy Spirit} — that is, Allah strengthened him with the Holy Spirit (rūḥ al-qudus). Most of the exegetes said it is Jibril (Gabriel), peace be upon him, and it was said that it is the faith with which Allah supports His servants. Then, despite these blessings whose worth cannot be measured, whenever a messenger came to you {with what your souls do not desire, you became arrogant} — that is, arrogant toward believing in them — {so a group} of them {you denied, and a group you killed}. You put desire before guidance and preferred the worldly life over the Hereafter, and in this there is a rebuke and severe condemnation that is not hidden.

{88} That is: they excused themselves from faith when you invited them to it, O Messenger, by saying that their hearts are *ghulf* (ghulf: wrapped, covered), meaning that they have a covering and wrappings over them, so they do not understand what you say. This would give them, by their own claim, an excuse for lacking knowledge. But this is a lie on their part. Therefore He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Rather, Allah has cursed them for their disbelief﴾; that is, they are cast out and cursed because of their disbelief. So little of them believes, or their belief is little, and their disbelief is the greater part.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verses 89–90:

{89–90} That is: ﴿And when there came to them [a Book]﴾ from Allah, through the hand of the best of creation and the seal of the prophets, comprising confirmation of what they possessed of the Torah. They knew it and were certain of it, for whenever wars had broken out between them and the polytheists in the Jahiliyyah, they sought victory through this Prophet and threatened them with his coming out, and that they would fight the polytheists alongside him. Yet when there came to them this Book and the Prophet whom they had recognized, they disbelieved in it, out of insolence and envy that Allah should send down of His bounty upon whomever He wills of His servants. So Allah cursed them and became angry with them, anger upon anger, because of the abundance of their disbelief and the continuous succession of their doubt and their polytheism. For them in the Hereafter is a humiliating punishment (ʿadhāb muhīn), that is, a painful and agonizing one, and it is the burning of the Blazing Fire and the loss of everlasting bliss. How evil is their state, and how evil is what they exchanged and substituted for faith in Allah, His books and His messengers: disbelief in Him, His books and His messengers, while knowing and being certain. This makes their punishment even greater.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verses 91–93:

{91} That is: when the Jews were commanded to believe in what Allah sent down to His Messenger, which is the Qur'an, they were arrogant and defiant, and ﴿they say, "We believe in what was sent down to us," and they disbelieve in what is beyond it﴾; that is, in what is other than it of the Scriptures. Yet what is obligatory is that they believe in what Allah has sent down absolutely, whether it was sent down to them or to others. This is the beneficial faith: belief in what Allah sent down to all of Allah's messengers. As for distinguishing between the messengers and the books, and claiming to believe in some of them while rejecting others, this is not faith at all; rather, it is outright disbelief. For this reason the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers and want to differentiate between Allah and His messengers and say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and want to adopt a way between that — those are the disbelievers in truth﴾.

Therefore, the Blessed and Exalted One responded to them here with a decisive response and imposed upon them an argument from which they have no escape. He refuted their disbelief in the Qur'an with two matters. He said: ﴿while it is the truth﴾. So if it is the truth in all that it contains of reports, commands, and prohibitions, and it is from their Lord, then disbelief in it after this is disbelief in Allah and disbelief in the truth that He sent down.

Then He said: ﴿confirming what is with them﴾; that is, agreeing with it in everything that indicates the truth and being a witness over it. So why do you believe in what was sent down to you and disbelieve in its like? Is this anything but partisanship and following of whims rather than guidance? Moreover, the Qur'an being a confirmation of what is with them requires that it be a proof for them of the truth of what is in their hands of Scriptures. There is no way for them to establish those except through it. So when they disbelieve in it and deny it, they become like one who makes a claim with a proof and evidence that he has no other than that, and his claim is not complete except by the soundness of his evidence; then he himself comes against his evidence and proof, discredits it, and denies it. Is this not foolishness and madness? Thus their disbelief in the Qur'an was disbelief in what is in their hands and a violation of it. Then the Exalted refuted their claim to believe in what was sent down to them, by saying: ﴿Say, "Why then did you kill the prophets of Allah before, if you were believers?"﴾ — (addressed) to them.

{92} ﴿And Moses had certainly come to you with clear proofs﴾; that is, with clear evidences explaining the truth. ﴿Then you took the calf [for worship] after him﴾; that is, after his coming, ﴿while you were wrongdoers﴾ in that; you have no excuse.

{93} ﴿And [recall] when We took your covenant and raised above you the mountain, [saying], "Hold to what We have given you with determination and listen."﴾; that is, listen with acceptance, obedience, and compliance. ﴿They said, "We hear and disobey."﴾; that is, this became their state. ﴿And they were given to drink [the worship of] the calf into their hearts﴾; that is, the love of the calf and the love of worshipping it were dyed into their hearts and drunk in, because of their disbelief. ﴿Say, "Wretched is that which your faith commands you, if you are believers."﴾; that is, you claim faith and boast of the true religion, yet you killed the prophets of Allah and took the calf as a god besides Allah when Moses, the prophet of Allah, was absent from you, and you did not accept his commands and prohibitions except after threat and the raising of the mountain above you. So you committed yourselves verbally and broke your word in deed. So what is this faith you claim? And what is this religion? If this is faith by your assertion, then wretched is the faith whose adherent it calls to tyranny, disbelief in the messengers of Allah, and abundant disobedience. It is well known that true faith commands its adherent to every good and forbids him from every evil. Thus their lying became clear, and their contradiction became evident.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 94–96:

{94} Meaning: {Say}, to them, in order to test the validity of their claim, {If the Last Abode with Allah is yours exclusively, to the exclusion of the rest of mankind}, meaning Paradise, as you claim that none will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians, and that the Fire will touch them only for a limited number of days. If you are truthful in this claim, {then wish for death}. This is a form of mubahalah (mutual imprecation) between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). After their obstinacy, there is no remaining pressure or constraint upon them beyond one of two matters: either they believe in Allah and His Messenger, or they call down the curse upon themselves regarding what they hold, through an easy matter for them, which is wishing for death, the thing that would bring them to the Abode that is exclusively theirs. They refrained from this, and so everyone knew that they were in the utmost obstinacy and opposition to Allah and His Messenger, despite their own knowledge of this. Therefore, the Exalted said:

{95} {And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward}, meaning, because of disbelief and disobedience. This is because they know that it is a path leading to their recompense for their evil deeds. Death is the thing most hateful to them, and they are the most eager for life of all people, even more than the polytheists who do not believe in any of the Messengers or Books. Then He mentioned the intensity of their love for this world, saying:

{96} {Each of them wishes he could be granted a life of a thousand years}. This is the utmost degree of greed. They wish for a state that is impossible, and even if they were granted the lifespan mentioned, it would not benefit them at all, nor would it avert any punishment from them. {And Allah is Seeing of what they do}, a warning to them regarding the recompense for their deeds.

They wish for a state that is impossible, and even if they were granted the lifespan mentioned, it would not benefit them at all, nor would it avert any punishment from them. {And Allah is Seeing of what they do}, a warning to them regarding the recompense for their deeds.

{97–98} That is: say, [O Muhammad], to these Jews who claim that what prevented them from believing is that your friend is Jibril (peace be upon him), whereas if it had been any other of the angels of Allah they would have believed you and affirmed you: this claim of yours is self-contradictory, confused, and arrogant toward Allah. For Jibril (peace be upon him) is the one who brought down the Qur'an from Allah upon your heart, and he is the one who descended upon the prophets before you, while Allah is the one who commanded him and sent him with that. He is therefore a pure messenger. Moreover, this Book which Jibril brought down confirms what came before it of the scriptures, does not oppose them, and does not contradict them; in it is complete guidance from all kinds of misguidance, and glad tidings of worldly and otherworldly good for whoever believes in it. Hence, enmity toward Jibril, who is described with this, is disbelief in Allah and His signs, and enmity toward Allah, His messengers, and His angels. Their enmity toward Jibril is not for his own sake, but for the truth that he brings down from Allah to the messengers of Allah; so it entails disbelief in and enmity toward the One who sent it down and sent him, toward the one who sent it, and toward the one to whom it was sent. This is the explanation of that.

{99} He says to His Prophet (ﷺ): {And We have certainly sent down to you clear verses}; through which guidance is attained by whoever seeks guidance, and the proof is established against whoever is obstinate. Their clarity and their indication of the truth have reached a great degree, arriving at a state that none refuses to accept except one who has defied the command of Allah, departed from the obedience of Allah, and become exceedingly arrogant.

{100} This contains a note of wonder at how often they make covenants and how little they are patient in keeping them.
"Kullama" (whenever) indicates repetition: whenever a covenant is made, its breaking follows. What is the cause of this? The cause is that most of them do not believe. Their lack of faith is what made breaking covenants necessary for them. Had their faith been true, they would have been like those about whom God said: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with God.﴾

{101} That is: when this noble Messenger came to them with the great Book, bringing the truth that agrees with what they already had, and they claimed that they held fast to their own Book, yet when they disbelieved in this Messenger and in what he brought, "a party of those who were given the Scripture threw away the Book of Allah," which was sent down to them, meaning they cast it aside out of aversion to it, "behind their backs." This is a more emphatic form of turning away, as if in doing this they were among the ignorant, though they knew of his truthfulness and the reality of what he brought. Through this it becomes clear that this party of the People of the Book retained nothing in their hands once they did not believe in this Messenger, so their disbelief in him became disbelief in their own Book, without their realizing it.

It is among the customary decrees of destiny and the divine wisdom that whoever abandons what would benefit him, while being able to benefit from it and not doing so, is tested with occupation with what harms him. Whoever abandons the worship of the Most Merciful is tested with the worship of idols; whoever abandons the love of Allah, fear of Him, and hope in Him is tested with love of other than Allah, fear of other than Him, and hope in other than Him; whoever does not spend his wealth in obedience to Allah spends it in obedience to Satan; and whoever abandons humbling himself before his Lord is tested with humbling himself before creatures; and whoever abandons the truth is tested with falsehood.

{102–103} Likewise: these Jews, when they threw away the Book of Allah, followed "what the devils recited" and fabricated of magic "over the kingdom of Solomon," for the devils brought out magic for the people, and they claimed that Solomon, peace be upon him, used it and through it obtained his great kingdom. They were liars in this, for Solomon did not use it; rather the Truthful One (Allah) cleared him in His saying: "Solomon did not disbelieve," that is, by learning magic, so he did not learn it. "But the devils disbelieved," in that matter, "teaching people magic," through their misguidance and their eagerness to lead the children of Adam astray. Likewise, the Jews followed the magic that was sent down upon the two angels in the land of Babylon, in the land of Iraq. It was sent down to them as a trial and test from Allah for His servants, so they taught them magic, "but they did not teach anyone until" they advised him and "said: We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve," that is, do not learn magic, for it is disbelief. Thus they forbade him from magic and informed him of its status.

So the devils' teaching of magic was by way of deception and misguidance, and attributing it and promoting it to the one whom Allah cleared of it, namely Solomon, peace be upon him. The angels' teaching was as a trial, along with their advice, lest they have any excuse. These Jews followed the magic that the devils taught and the magic that the two angels taught; they abandoned the knowledge of the prophets and messengers and turned to the knowledge of the devils, and each inclines toward what suits him.

Then he mentioned the corruptions of magic, saying: "So they learn from them what they use to cause division between a man and his wife," even though the love between spouses cannot be compared to the love of others, since Allah said concerning them: "And He placed between you affection and mercy." This is evidence that magic has a real effect and that it harms "by the permission of Allah," that is, by the will of Allah. Permission is of two kinds: permission of destiny, which is connected to the will of Allah as in this verse, and permission of legislation, as in the Most High's saying in the preceding verse: "Then indeed he has brought it down upon your heart by the permission of Allah." This verse and what resembles it show that causes, however powerful their influence, are subject to the decree and destiny of Allah and are not independent in their effect. None of the sects of this Ummah has opposed this principle except the Qadariyyah regarding the actions of servants, who claimed that they are independent and not subject to the will of Allah, thereby removing them from the power of Allah. Thus they contradicted the Book of Allah, the Sunnah of His Messenger, and the consensus of the Companions and the Followers.

Then he mentioned that the knowledge of magic is pure harm, with no benefit, neither religious nor worldly, unlike some worldly benefits found in some sins, as the Most High said concerning wine and gambling: "Say: In both is great sin and some benefit for people, but their sin is greater than their benefit." So this magic is pure harm, with no motive at all. All prohibitions are either pure harm or their evil outweighs their good, just as the commands are either pure benefit or their good outweighs their evil.

"And they had certainly known," that is, the Jews, "that whoever purchased it," that is, desired magic as a buyer desires a commodity, "would have no share in the Hereafter," that is, no portion; rather it entails punishment. So their doing it was not out of ignorance, but they preferred the present life over the Hereafter. "Wretched is that for which they sold themselves, if only they had known" — knowledge that would produce action — what they did.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verses 104–105:

{104} The Muslims used to say, when addressing the Messenger while learning the matters of the religion: {Ra'ina} (lit. "Attend to us," i.e., "Pay attention to our circumstances"), intending by it a correct meaning. But the Jews intended by it a corrupt meaning, so they seized the opportunity and began addressing the Messenger with it while intending the corrupt meaning. Therefore Allah forbade the believers from this word, blocking this avenue (sadd al-dhara'i', blocking the means to what is forbidden). In this is the prohibition of what is permissible when it becomes a means to what is forbidden. It also includes good manners and the use of words that admit only what is good, avoiding obscenity and leaving aside words that are ugly or that carry some confusion and possibility of an improper meaning. So He commanded them with a word that admits only what is good, saying: {And say, "Unzurna" (lit. "Regard us," i.e., "Give us consideration")}, for it is sufficient and achieves the intended purpose without any objectionable implication. {And listen}: He did not mention the object of listening, so that it is general, covering everything He commanded them to listen to, including hearing the Qur'an and hearing the Sunnah, which is wisdom in wording, meaning, and acceptance. In this is good manners and obedience. Then He threatened the disbelievers with a painful, agonizing punishment.

{105} He informed of the enmity of the Jews and the polytheists toward the believers, that they do not wish {that there should be sent down upon you any good} (i.e., not even a little nor a lot) {from your Lord}, out of envy and hatred toward you that He should single you out with His bounty. But {Allah is the Owner of great bounty}, and among His bounty upon you is the sending down of the Book to your Messenger, to purify you and teach you the Book and wisdom, and to teach you what you did not know. So to Him belong all praise and favor.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 106–107:

{106} Naskh (abrogation) means transfer. The reality of naskh is the transfer of the responsible persons (mukallafun) from one legislated ruling to another ruling, or to its cancellation. The Jews used to deny naskh and claimed that it is not permissible, although it is mentioned in their own Torah. Their denial of it is disbelief and pure caprice. So God, exalted is He, informed about His wisdom in naskh, and that He does not abrogate ﴿any verse or cause it to be forgotten﴾; i.e., He causes His servants to forget it, so He removes it from their hearts, ﴿We bring a better one than it﴾, and more beneficial for you, ﴿or its like﴾. This indicates that naskh does not occur except for a greater benefit for you than the former, because His bounty increases, especially upon this nation, for whom their religion was made extremely easy. He also informed that whoever casts doubt on naskh [has] cast doubt on His dominion and power, so He said: ﴿Do you not know that God is over all things competent?﴾

{107} ﴿Do you not know that to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth?﴾
If He is the Owner of you, disposing of you as a righteous and merciful owner disposes of his affairs, in His decrees, commands and prohibitions, then just as there is no restriction upon Him in determining whatever He determines of various kinds of decrees for His servants, likewise He cannot be opposed in what He legislates for His servants of rulings. The servant is managed and subjected under the religious and decreed commands of his Lord, so what right has he to object? He is also the Protector and Helper of His servants, so He takes charge of securing their benefits and helps them in repelling their harms. From His guardianship over them is that He legislates for them those rulings which His wisdom and mercy toward them require.
Whoever reflects on what occurs in the Qur'an and the Sunnah of abrogation will come to know thereby the wisdom of God, His mercy toward His servants, and His bringing them to their interests from where they do not perceive, through His kindness.

{108} God forbids the believers, or the Jews, from asking their Messenger as Moses was asked before (kama su'ila Musa min qabl). What is meant is questions of contention and objection, as the Exalted said: ﴿The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from heaven. They asked Moses for greater than that, when they said, "Show us God openly"﴾ [An-Nisa 4:153]. And the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were made apparent to you, would distress you﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 5:101].

These and similar questions are what is forbidden.

As for questions asked seeking guidance and knowledge, these are praiseworthy, and God has commanded them, as the Exalted said: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know﴾ [An-Nahl 16:43]. He also approves of them, as in His saying: ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:219], and ﴿They ask you concerning orphans﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:220], and the like.

Since the forbidden questions are blameworthy and may lead their asker to disbelief, He said: ﴿And whoever exchanges faith for disbelief has certainly strayed from the sound way﴾.

{109} Then He informed of the envy of many of the People of the Scripture, and that their condition reached the point where they ﴿wished, if they could, to turn you back to disbelief after your belief﴾. They strove toward that, and devised schemes, but their scheming returns upon themselves, as the Exalted said: ﴿And a faction of the People of the Scripture say, "Believe in what has been revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day and disbelieve at its end; perhaps they will return"﴾ [Ali 'Imran 3:72].

This envy arose from their own souls, so God commanded the believers to respond to whoever wronged them [to the utmost degree of wrongdoing] with pardon and forgiveness until God brings His command. Then, after that, God brought His command to them to fight, and He healed the hearts of the believers from them: they killed whom they killed, enslaved whom they enslaved, and expelled whom they expelled. ﴿Indeed, God is over all things competent﴾.

{110} Then God commanded them to occupy themselves with the present time by establishing prayer, giving zakat, and performing all acts of worship, and He promised them that whatever good they do will not be lost with God; rather, they will find it with Him in full and abundant measure, which He has preserved. ﴿Indeed, God is Seeing of what you do﴾.

And the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were made apparent to you, would distress you﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 5:101].

These and similar questions are what is forbidden.

As for questions asked seeking guidance and knowledge, these are praiseworthy, and God has commanded them, as the Exalted said: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know﴾ [An-Nahl 16:43]. He also approves of them, as in His saying: ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:219], and ﴿They ask you concerning orphans﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:220], and the like.

Since the forbidden questions are blameworthy and may lead their asker to disbelief, He said: ﴿And whoever exchanges faith for disbelief has certainly strayed from the sound way﴾.

{109} Then He informed of the envy of many of the People of the Scripture, and that their condition reached the point where they ﴿wished, if they could, to turn you back to disbelief after your belief﴾. They strove toward that, and devised schemes, but their scheming returns upon themselves, as the Exalted said: ﴿And a faction of the People of the Scripture say, "Believe in what has been revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day and disbelieve at its end; perhaps they will return"﴾ [Ali 'Imran 3:72].

This envy arose from their own souls, so God commanded the believers to respond to whoever wronged them [to the utmost degree of wrongdoing] with pardon and forgiveness until God brings His command. Then, after that, God brought His command to them to fight, and He healed the hearts of the believers from them: they killed whom they killed, enslaved whom they enslaved, and expelled whom they expelled. ﴿Indeed, God is over all things competent﴾.

{110} Then God commanded them to occupy themselves with the present time by establishing prayer, giving zakat, and performing all acts of worship, and He promised them that whatever good they do will not be lost with God; rather, they will find it with Him in full and abundant measure, which He has preserved. ﴿Indeed, God is Seeing of what you do﴾.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verses 111–112:

{111} That is: the Jews said, "None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews," and the Christians said, "None will enter Paradise except those who are Christians." Thus they assigned Paradise exclusively to themselves. These are merely wishful claims (amani), not accepted unless supported by proof and evidence, so "Bring your proof, if you are truthful" (﴿فَأْتُوا بِرُهَانَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾). This is the case with everyone who makes a claim: he must establish evidence for the soundness of his claim. Otherwise, if his claim were reversed and another claimant asserted the opposite without evidence, there would be no difference between them. Evidence is what confirms claims or refutes them. Since they had no evidence, their falsehood in this claim was known.

{112} Then He mentioned the clear evidence, general to every person, saying: ﴿بَلَىٰ﴾ ("Yes" / "Rather"); that is, it is not by your wishful claims and assertions, but rather: ﴿مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُ لِلَّهِ﴾ ("whoever submits his face to Allah"), that is, he sincerely dedicates his deeds to Allah, turning to Him with his heart, ﴿وَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌ﴾ ("while he is a doer of good"), that is, while being sincere, he worships his Lord in accordance with His Law, having worshipped Him by what He prescribed. ﴿فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ ("for them is their reward with their Lord"), which is Paradise with all the bliss it contains. ﴿وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ ("no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve"). Thus they attain what they desire and are saved from what they dread. It is understood from this that whoever is not like this is among the people of the Fire, the ruined. There is no salvation except for the people of sincere devotion to the One worshipped and of following the Messenger.

There is no salvation except for the people of sincere devotion to the One worshipped and of following the Messenger.

{113} The reason is that desire and envy drove the People of the Book to such an extent that some of them declared others to be misguided, and some of them declared others to be disbelievers, just as the unlettered ones among the polytheists of the Arabs and others did. Thus every sect declares the other sect to be misguided. On the Day of Judgment, Allah will judge between those who differed with His just judgment, which He has informed His servants of. There is no success and no salvation except for those who affirm the truth of all the Prophets and Messengers, carry out the commands of their Lord, and avoid His prohibitions. Whoever other than these is doomed.

{114} That is: there is no one more unjust or more gravely sinful than the one who prevents the mosques of Allah from the remembrance of Allah within them, and from establishing the prayer and the other [kinds of] acts of obedience. {And strives} means: he exerts himself and expends his utmost effort {in their ruin}, both the physical and the spiritual ruin. Physical ruin is demolishing them, destroying them, and defiling them; spiritual ruin is preventing those who remember the name of Allah from doing so within them. This is general to everyone who is characterized by this attribute, and it includes the People of the Elephant, and the Quraysh when they barred the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from them in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah, and the Christians when they ruined Bayt al-Maqdis, and other kinds of oppressors who strive for their ruin, in opposition to Allah and in hostility toward Him. So Allah requited them by preventing them from entering them, both legally and by decree, except in fear and humiliation. When they terrified the servants of Allah, Allah terrified them. As for the polytheists who barred His Messenger, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not remain long before Allah permitted him to conquer Makkah and prevented the polytheists from approaching His House. Thus the Exalted said: {O you who have believed, the polytheists are but impure, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year}.

As for the People of the Elephant, Allah has mentioned what befell them. As for the Christians, Allah empowered the believers over them and they expelled them from it. Likewise, everyone who is characterized by their attribute will surely receive his share. This is among the great signs, which the Creator reported before its occurrence, and it occurred as He had reported. The scholars have derived from this noble verse that it is not permissible to enable disbelievers to enter the mosques. {For them in this world is disgrace}, meaning: disgrace and exposure, as has preceded. {And for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment}.

Since there is no one more unjust than the one who prevents the mosques of Allah from having His name mentioned in them, then there is no one greater in faith than the one who strives in the building of the mosques, both the physical and the spiritual building. As the Exalted said: {Only those who believe in Allah and the Last Day maintain the mosques of Allah}. Indeed, Allah the Exalted has commanded that His houses be raised, magnified, and honored, as He said: {In houses which Allah has permitted to be raised and in which His name is remembered}.

The mosques have many rulings, the sum of which returns to the meaning of these noble verses.

{115} That is: {To Allah belongs the east and the west}. He specified them for mention because they are the locations of the great signs; they are the places where the lights rise and set. So when He owns them, He owns all directions. {Wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah}: whichever direction you face is by His command, whether He commands you to face the Ka'bah after you had been commanded to face Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), or you are commanded to pray while traveling on a mount or the like. The qiblah is wherever the servant turns, or when the qiblah is unclear, he seeks out the direction for prayer (yataharra); then the error becomes evident to him, or he is excused by a disability or illness or the like. These matters are ones in which the servant is either excused or commanded.

In every case, whatever direction he faces is not outside the dominion of his Lord. {Then there is the Face of Allah. Indeed Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing}: this affirms the Face for Allah, Exalted is He, in a manner befitting Him; Allah has a Face that is not like the faces of creation. He, Exalted is He, is vast in grace and great in attributes, All-Knowing of your secrets and intentions. From His vastness and knowledge, He has made the matter easy for you and accepted from you what was commanded, so to Him belongs all praise and thanks.

{116} {And they say}; that is: the Jews, the Christians, the polytheists, and everyone who says this, {"God has taken a son."}; so they attributed to Him what is not fitting to His majesty, and they committed the greatest of wrongs and wronged themselves. Yet He, exalted is He, is patient with them in this, forbearing toward them, granting them well-being, and providing for them despite their disparagement of Him. {Glory be to Him}; that is: He is exalted and sanctified above everything the polytheists and wrongdoers ascribe to Him that is not fitting to His majesty. Glory be to the One who possesses absolute perfection in every respect, to whom no deficiency attaches in any way. And along with rejecting their claim, He established the proof and evidence of His transcendence above that, saying: {Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth}; that is: all of them are His dominion and His servants; He disposes of them as an owner disposes of his possessions, and they are {devoutly obedient to Him}, subjected under His management. If they are all His servants, dependent upon Him, while He is independent of them, how could any of them be a son to Him? A son must be of the same kind as his father, for he is a part of him. God is the Owner, the Dominant, and you are the owned and subdued; He is the Rich and you are the poor. So how, given this, could He have a son? This is among the most manifest and most absurd falsehoods.

Qunut (devotion, obedience) is of two kinds: general qunut, which is the submission of all creatures to the management of the Creator, and specific qunut, which is the qunut of worship. The first kind is what is in this verse, and the second kind is as in His saying, exalted is He: {And stand before God in devout obedience} (2:238). Then He said:

{117} {Originator of the heavens and the earth}; that is: their Creator, in a manner that perfected and beautified them, without any previous pattern. {And when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is}; so nothing resists Him or eludes Him.

{116} {And they say}; that is: the Jews, the Christians, the polytheists, and everyone who says this, {"God has taken a son."}; so they attributed to Him what is not fitting to His majesty, and they committed the greatest of wrongs and wronged themselves. Yet He, exalted is He, is patient with them in this, forbearing toward them, granting them well-being, and providing for them despite their disparagement of Him. {Glory be to Him}; that is: He is exalted and sanctified above everything the polytheists and wrongdoers ascribe to Him that is not fitting to His majesty. Glory be to the One who possesses absolute perfection in every respect, to whom no deficiency attaches in any way. And along with rejecting their claim, He established the proof and evidence of His transcendence above that, saying: {Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth}; that is: all of them are His dominion and His servants; He disposes of them as an owner disposes of his possessions, and they are {devoutly obedient to Him}, subjected under His management. If they are all His servants, dependent upon Him, while He is independent of them, how could any of them be a son to Him? A son must be of the same kind as his father, for he is a part of him. The first kind is what is in this verse, and the second kind is as in His saying, exalted is He: {And stand before God in devout obedience} (2:238). Then He said:

{117} {Originator of the heavens and the earth}; that is: their Creator, in a manner that perfected and beautified them, without any previous pattern. {And when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is}; so nothing resists Him or eludes Him.

{118} That is: the ignorant ones among the People of the Book and others said, "Why does God not speak to us as He speaks to the messengers?" "Or a sign come to us"; they mean the demanded signs (ayat al-iqtirah) which they propose by their corrupt minds and their worthless opinions, by which they dared against the Creator and grew arrogant toward His messengers, such as their saying: ﴿We will never believe you until we see God plainly﴾; ﴿The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a Book from heaven. They had already asked Moses for something greater than that...﴾; the verse. And ﴿They say, "What is this messenger who eats food and walks in the markets? Why has an angel not been sent down to him to be a warner with him, or a treasure not been thrown to him, or he not been given a garden from which to eat...﴾; the verses. And His saying: ﴿They say, "We will never believe you until you cause a spring to gush for us from the earth..."﴾; the verses.

This is their custom with their messengers: they seek signs of obstinacy, not signs of guidance, and their aim was not to clarify the truth, for the messengers had brought signs of the kind by which human beings believe. Therefore God, exalted is He, said: ﴿We have made the signs clear for a people who are certain﴾. Every person of certainty has recognized, from God's dazzling signs and manifest proofs, that which produced certainty in him, and every doubt and suspicion was driven away from him.

Then God, exalted is He, mentioned a brief and concise verse that comprises the signs indicating the truthfulness of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the soundness of what he brought, saying:

{119} ﴿Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾. This comprises the signs he brought, and they return to three matters: the first concerns the very fact of his being sent; the second concerns his conduct, guidance and manner; the third concerns knowledge of what he brought of the Qur'an and the Sunnah. The first and second are included in His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent you﴾; and the third [is included] in His saying: ﴿with the truth﴾.

As for the explanation of the first matter, namely the very fact of his being sent: he (ﷺ) knew the state of the people of the earth before his mission, and what they were upon: worshipping idols, fires and crosses, and altering their religions, until they were in a darkness of disbelief that had enveloped and covered them, except for remnants of the People of the Book who had died out shortly before the mission. He also knew that God, exalted is He, did not create His creatures in vain, nor leave them neglected, for He is All-Wise, All-Knowing, All-Powerful, Most Merciful. So, from His wisdom and mercy toward His servants, He sent to them this great Messenger, commanding them to worship the Merciful alone, with no partner. Thus by the mere fact of his mission, the intelligent person recognizes his truthfulness, and it is a great sign that he is the Messenger of God.

As for the second matter: whoever knows the Prophet (ﷺ) with complete knowledge, and knows his conduct and guidance before the mission and his upbringing in the most perfect qualities, and then after that his noble character and great, dazzling excellence increased for those who look upon him, will know through examining his circumstances and tracing his states that these can only be the qualities of perfected prophets; for God, exalted is He, made attributes the greatest evidence for recognizing their bearers and their truthfulness or falsehood.

As for the third matter: it is knowledge of what the Prophet (ﷺ) brought of the great Shari'ah and the noble Qur'an, comprising true reports, good commands, the prohibition of every ugliness, and dazzling miracles. Thus all the signs fall within these three.

His saying: ﴿a bringer of good tidings﴾: that is, to whoever obeys you, with worldly and otherworldly happiness; ﴿and a warner﴾: to whoever disobeys you, with wretchedness and worldly and otherworldly ruin. ﴿And you will not be asked about the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾: that is, you are not responsible for them; upon you is only the conveyance (of the message), and upon Us is the reckoning.

His saying: ﴿a bringer of good tidings﴾: that is, to whoever obeys you, with worldly and otherworldly happiness; ﴿and a warner﴾: to whoever disobeys you, with wretchedness and worldly and otherworldly ruin. ﴿And you will not be asked about the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾: that is, you are not responsible for them; upon you is only the conveyance (of the message), and upon Us is the reckoning.

{120} Almighty God informs His Messenger that the Jews and the Christians will never be pleased with him unless he follows their religion, because they are callers to the religion they adhere to, claiming that it is the guidance. So say to them: ﴿Indeed, the guidance of God﴾, which you have been sent with, ﴿is the guidance﴾; as for what you are upon, it is desire (hawa), as evidenced by His saying: ﴿And if you were to follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, you would have against God no protector or helper﴾.

In this there is a great prohibition against following the desires of the Jews and the Christians and imitating them in what is specific to their religion.

Although the address is directed to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), his community is included in it, because the consideration is with the generality of the meaning, not the specificity of the one addressed, just as the lesson is drawn from the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the occasion of revelation.

Then he said:

{121} Almighty God informs that those to whom We gave the Book and who were granted it as an absolute favour, {recite it with its proper recitation}; that is, they follow it with its proper following. Recitation (tilawah) means following. So they make lawful what it makes lawful, forbid what it forbids, act upon its clear (muhkam) verses, and believe in its ambiguous (mutashabih) verses.

These are the fortunate among the People of the Book, who recognised God's blessing and gave thanks for it, and who believed in all the messengers without distinguishing between any of them. These are the true believers, not those among them who say, "We believe in what was sent down to us," and reject what comes after it. For this reason He threatened them with His words: {And whoever disbelieves in it, those are the losers}.

{122–123} The explanation of the verse that follows has already been given.
