{124} God tells of His servant and close friend Ibrahim (peace be upon him), whose leadership and greatness are agreed upon, and whom every group of the People of the Book claims as their own, and the polytheists as well: that Allah tested him and examined him with "words", meaning commands and prohibitions, as is God's custom in testing His servants, so that the liar, who does not stand firm under trial and examination, may be distinguished from the truthful, whose rank is raised, whose worth increases, whose deeds grow pure, and whose gold is refined. Among the most distinguished in this station was the Friend (peace be upon him), so he fulfilled what Allah tested him with, completed it, and carried it out in full. Allah thanked him for that, for Allah is ever Most Appreciative, and He said: ﴿Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people﴾; that is, they will follow you in guidance and walk behind you toward their everlasting happiness, and you will earn lasting praise, abundant reward, and honor from everyone.

By the life of Allah, this is the most excellent rank that competitors have competed for, the highest station that the diligent have striven toward, and the most complete state attained by the steadfast messengers and their followers from every truthful person who follows them and calls to Allah and His path. When Ibrahim rejoiced in this station and understood it, he asked for it for his offspring, so that his rank and the rank of his descendants might be elevated. This too is part of his leadership, his sincere counsel to the servants of Allah, and his love that there be many guides among them. How great is the magnitude of these lofty aspirations and exalted stations!

The All-Gracious, the Subtly Kind, responded to him and informed him of the obstacle preventing the attainment of this station, saying: ﴿My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers﴾; that is, leadership in religion is not attained by one who has wronged himself, harmed it, and lowered its worth, because wrongdoing is incompatible with this station. Its means are patience and certainty, and its outcome is that its possessor will be upon a great level of faith, righteous deeds, beautiful character, sound dispositions, complete love, fear of Allah, and turning back to Him in repentance. How can wrongdoing coexist with this station? The implication of the verse indicates that one who is not a wrongdoer will attain leadership, but only by bringing about its causes.

{125} Then God mentioned an enduring model that points to Ibrahim's leadership, which is: this Sacred House, whose direction He made a pillar of the pillars of Islam, a means of erasing sins and transgressions. In it are traces of the Friend and his descendants by which his leadership is recognized and his condition is remembered. So He said: ﴿And when We made the House a place of return for the people﴾; that is, a place to which they return, obtaining their religious and worldly benefits, repeatedly coming to it without ever being satiated from it. And He made it ﴿a sanctuary﴾, where everyone is safe, even wild animals and inanimate things such as trees. For this reason, in the pre-Islamic period, while they were polytheists, they venerated it with the utmost reverence; one of them would find the killer of his father within the sanctuary and would not molest him. When Islam came, it increased its sanctity, glorification, honor, and dignity. ﴿And take from the station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾; it is possible that the intended meaning is the well-known station that is now placed opposite the door of the Ka'bah, and that the intended meaning here is that the two rak'ahs of circumambulation are recommended to be performed behind the Station of Ibrahim, which is the view of the majority of the exegetes. It is also possible that "the station" is singular but annexed, so that it encompasses all of Ibrahim's stations in the Hajj, namely all the rites: the circumambulation, the running between Safa and Marwah, standing at Arafat, Muzdalifah, stoning the pillars, sacrificing, and other acts of Hajj. In that case the meaning of His words ﴿a place of prayer﴾ is a place of worship, that is, follow him in the rites of Hajj. This latter meaning is perhaps more preferable, since the first meaning is included in it and the wording allows it.

﴿And We charged Ibrahim and Isma'il﴾; that is, We revealed to them and commanded them to purify the House of Allah from polytheism, disbelief, and sins, and from filth, impurities, and defilements, so that it would be for ﴿those who circumambulate it, and those who stay in devotion, and those who bow and prostrate﴾; that is, those who pray. He mentioned circumambulation first because it is specific to the Sacred Mosque, then staying in devotion (i'tikaf), because its condition is a mosque in general, then prayer, even though it is more excellent, for this reason. The Creator attributed the House to Himself for several benefits:
Among them: that this implies the great concern of Ibrahim and Isma'il for its purification, since it is the House of Allah, so they would exert their utmost effort and expend their full capacity in this.
Among them: that the attribution implies honor and esteem, and so it contains a command to His servants to glorify and honor it.
Among them: that this attribution is the cause that draws hearts toward it.

{124} God tells of His servant and close friend Ibrahim (peace be upon him), whose leadership and greatness are agreed upon, and whom every group of the People of the Book claims as their own, and the polytheists as well: that Allah tested him and examined him with "words", meaning commands and prohibitions, as is God's custom in testing His servants, so that the liar, who does not stand firm under trial and examination, may be distinguished from the truthful, whose rank is raised, whose worth increases, whose deeds grow pure, and whose gold is refined. Among the most distinguished in this station was the Friend (peace be upon him), so he fulfilled what Allah tested him with, completed it, and carried it out in full. Allah thanked him for that, for Allah is ever Most Appreciative, and He said: ﴿Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people﴾; that is, they will follow you in guidance and walk behind you toward their everlasting happiness, and you will earn lasting praise, abundant reward, and honor from everyone.

By the life of Allah, this is the most excellent rank that competitors have competed for, the highest station that the diligent have striven toward, and the most complete state attained by the steadfast messengers and their followers from every truthful person who follows them and calls to Allah and His path. When Ibrahim rejoiced in this station and understood it, he asked for it for his offspring, so that his rank and the rank of his descendants might be elevated. This too is part of his leadership, his sincere counsel to the servants of Allah, and his love that there be many guides among them. How great is the magnitude of these lofty aspirations and exalted stations!

The All-Gracious, the Subtly Kind, responded to him and informed him of the obstacle preventing the attainment of this station, saying: ﴿My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers﴾; that is, leadership in religion is not attained by one who has wronged himself, harmed it, and lowered its worth, because wrongdoing is incompatible with this station. Its means are patience and certainty, and its outcome is that its possessor will be upon a great level of faith, righteous deeds, beautiful character, sound dispositions, complete love, fear of Allah, and turning back to Him in repentance. How can wrongdoing coexist with this station? The implication of the verse indicates that one who is not a wrongdoer will attain leadership, but only by bringing about its causes.

{125} Then God mentioned an enduring model that points to Ibrahim's leadership, which is: this Sacred House, whose direction He made a pillar of the pillars of Islam, a means of erasing sins and transgressions. In it are traces of the Friend and his descendants by which his leadership is recognized and his condition is remembered. So He said: ﴿And when We made the House a place of return for the people﴾; that is, a place to which they return, obtaining their religious and worldly benefits, repeatedly coming to it without ever being satiated from it. And He made it ﴿a sanctuary﴾, where everyone is safe, even wild animals and inanimate things such as trees. For this reason, in the pre-Islamic period, while they were polytheists, they venerated it with the utmost reverence; one of them would find the killer of his father within the sanctuary and would not molest him. When Islam came, it increased its sanctity, glorification, honor, and dignity. ﴿And take from the station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾; it is possible that the intended meaning is the well-known station that is now placed opposite the door of the Ka'bah, and that the intended meaning here is that the two rak'ahs of circumambulation are recommended to be performed behind the Station of Ibrahim, which is the view of the majority of the exegetes. It is also possible that "the station" is singular but annexed, so that it encompasses all of Ibrahim's stations in the Hajj, namely all the rites: the circumambulation, the running between Safa and Marwah, standing at Arafat, Muzdalifah, stoning the pillars, sacrificing, and other acts of Hajj. In that case the meaning of His words ﴿a place of prayer﴾ is a place of worship, that is, follow him in the rites of Hajj. This latter meaning is perhaps more preferable, since the first meaning is included in it and the wording allows it.

{126} That is: "And when Ibrahim (Abraham) said: 'My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits, those among them who believe in Allah and the Last Day.'" Then peace be upon him restricted this supplication to the believers, out of courtesy toward Allah, since his first supplication was unrestricted, whereas the answer was restricted to exclude the wrongdoer. So when he asked for provision for them and restricted it to the believer, and Allah's provision encompasses the believer, the disbeliever, the disobedient and the obedient, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever disbelieves﴾; that is, "I will provide for them all, their Muslims and their disbelievers. As for the Muslim, he uses provision as an aid to worship Allah, and then passes from it to the bliss of Paradise. As for the disbeliever, he enjoys it for a little while." ﴿Then I will compel him﴾; that is, I will force him and drive him out, unwilling, ﴿to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination.﴾

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 127–129:

{127} That is: Remember Ibrahim (Abraham) and Isma'il (Ishmael) as they raised the foundations of the House, and as they persisted in this great work, and how their state was one of fear and hope, to the extent that even with this work they called upon Allah to accept their deed from them, so that He would place in it abundant benefit.

{128} They also prayed for themselves and their offspring for Islam (submission), whose reality is the submission of the heart and its yielding to its Lord, which implies the submission of the limbs. "And show us our rites (manasikana)": that is, teach us them in a manner of showing and witnessing, so that it is more emphatic. The intended meaning of "manasik" may be the acts of Hajj in their entirety, as the context and the situation indicate; and it may be what is more general than that, namely the whole religion and all acts of worship, as the general wording indicates, because the nusk (ritual worship) is worship; but it has come to be predominantly applied to the acts of worship of Hajj by customary usage (taghlib 'urfi). So the outcome of their supplication returns to being granted success in beneficial knowledge and righteous action.
Since the servant, whoever he may be, must inevitably fall short and need repentance, they said: "And accept our repentance; indeed You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful."

{129} "Our Lord, and raise among them": that is, among our offspring, "a messenger from among them," so that he would be higher in rank for them, and so that they would submit to him and truly know him, "who will recite to them Your verses" in wording, memorization, and making them memorize; "and teach them the Book and wisdom," meaning; "and purify them" through training in righteous deeds and disassociation from wicked deeds by which the soul does not thrive. "Indeed You are the Mighty": that is, the Subduer of everything, whose might nothing can resist; "the Wise": who places things in their proper places. So by Your might and wisdom, raise among them this messenger.
So Allah answered them, and raised this noble Messenger, through whom Allah showed mercy to their offspring in particular and to all creation in general. For this reason, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am the answer to the prayer of my father Ibrahim."

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 130–134:

{130} That is: who would turn away from the religion (millah) of Ibraheem (Abraham) after knowing of his virtue, except one who makes a fool of himself (safaha nafsahu); that is, one who ignores his own worth (jahilaha), degrades it, is content for it with what is base, and sells it in the bargain of the one who is cheated. Just as there is no one more rightly guided and more perfect than the one who desires the religion of Ibraheem. Then He informed about his state in this world and the Hereafter, saying: ﴿And We had chosen him in this world﴾; that is, We chose him and granted him success in the deeds by which he became one of the chosen and the righteous. ﴿And indeed, in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous﴾; those who have the highest ranks.

{131} ﴿When his Lord said to him, "Submit," he said, "I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds."﴾ Obeying his Lord; ﴿I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds﴾, in sincerity, monotheism, love and turning back in repentance. So tawhid (monotheism) to Allah was his attribute. Then he bequeathed it to his offspring and enjoined it upon them, and made it a lasting word among his descendants, and it was passed down among them until it reached Ya'qub (Jacob), who enjoined it upon his sons.

So you, O children of Ya'qub, your father has enjoined upon you this particular matter, so it is obligatory upon you to fully submit and to follow the Seal of the Prophets. He said:

{132} ﴿O my sons, indeed Allah has chosen for you this religion, so do not die except while you are Muslims.﴾ That is, He chose it and selected it for you out of mercy and kindness toward you. So stand firm by it, be characterized by its laws, and be colored by its ethics, so that you persist in that until death does not come to you except while you are upon it, because whoever lives upon something dies upon it, and whoever dies upon something is resurrected upon it.

{133} Since the Jews claimed that they were upon the religion of Ibraheem and after him Ya'qub, Allah the Exalted said, rebuking them: ﴿Or were you witnesses when death approached Ya'qub?﴾; that is, present, ﴿when death approached Ya'qub﴾; that is, its preliminaries and causes. He said to his sons, as a test, and so that his eye would be comforted during his life by their compliance with what he had enjoined upon them: ﴿"What will you worship after me?"﴾ They answered him with what comforted his eye, saying: ﴿"We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Ibraheem and Isma'il and Ishaq, one God, and to Him we are Muslims."﴾ So we do not associate anything with Him, nor do we equate anything with Him. Thus they combined tawhid and action. It is known that they were not present with Ya'qub, because they had not yet come into existence. Since they were not present, Allah has informed about him that he enjoined his sons with hanifiyyah (pure monotheism), not Judaism. Then Allah the Exalted said:

{134} ﴿That is a nation that has passed away. For it is what it earned, and for you is what you have earned.﴾ That is, passed away; each has his own deeds, and each will be recompensed for what he did. No one is held accountable for another's sin, and nothing benefits anyone except his own faith and piety. Your preoccupation with them, your claim that you are upon their religion, and contentment with mere words is an empty matter with no reality. Rather, it is obligatory upon you to examine your own state, whether it is fit for salvation or not.

He said to his sons, as a test, and so that his eye would be comforted during his life by their compliance with what he had enjoined upon them: ﴿"What will you worship after me?"﴾ They answered him with what comforted his eye, saying: ﴿"We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Ibraheem and Isma'il and Ishaq, one God, and to Him we are Muslims."﴾ So we do not associate anything with Him, nor do we equate anything with Him. Thus they combined tawhid and action. It is known that they were not present with Ya'qub, because they had not yet come into existence. Since they were not present, Allah has informed about him that he enjoined his sons with hanifiyyah (pure monotheism), not Judaism. Then Allah the Exalted said:

{134} ﴿That is a nation that has passed away. For it is what it earned, and for you is what you have earned.﴾ That is, passed away; each has his own deeds, and each will be recompensed for what he did. No one is held accountable for another's sin, and nothing benefits anyone except his own faith and piety. Your preoccupation with them, your claim that you are upon their religion, and contentment with mere words is an empty matter with no reality. Rather, it is obligatory upon you to examine your own state, whether it is fit for salvation or not.

{135} That is: each of the Jews and the Christians called the Muslims to enter their religion, claiming that they themselves are the rightly guided and that others are astray. Say to them, in a conclusive reply: {Rather, we follow the religion of Abraham, inclining (ḥanīfan)}; that is, turning wholly toward God, turning away from all else, upholding monotheism and abandoning association with Him and rivalry to Him. In following this is guidance, and in turning away from his religion is disbelief and misguidance.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 136:

{136} This noble verse includes everything that must be believed in. Know that faith (iman), which is the complete affirmation of the heart in these foundations and its acknowledgment, encompassing the actions of the hearts and the limbs, is, in this sense, one that includes Islam (islam), and all righteous deeds enter into it; they are part of faith and an effect of its effects. Therefore, when faith is mentioned without qualification, it includes all that has been mentioned, and likewise Islam, when mentioned without qualification, includes faith. But when the two are joined together, faith is a name for what is in the heart of acknowledgment and affirmation, and Islam is a name for the outward actions. Likewise when faith is joined with righteous deeds.

As for His saying, exalted is He: {Say} (qulu), meaning: with your tongues, with your hearts in agreement with them. This is the complete statement that brings about reward and recompense. Just as uttering something with the tongue without belief of the heart is hypocrisy and disbelief, so a statement devoid of action of the heart is without effect and of little benefit. Although the servant is rewarded for it if it is good and accompanied by the root of faith, there is still a difference between a bare statement and one accompanied by the action of the heart.

In His saying {Say} there is an indication of proclaiming the creed, declaring it openly, and calling to it, since it is the foundation and basis of the religion. In His saying {We believe} (amanna) and similar expressions in which the act is attributed to the entire community, there is an indication that the community is obligated to hold fast together to the rope of Allah, all of them, and to urge unity, so that their caller is one and their action is unified; and implicit in this is the prohibition of division. In it is also that the believers are like one body.

In His saying: {Say: We believe in Allah...} etc., there is evidence for the permissibility of a person attributing faith to himself, in a qualified manner; indeed, it is obligatory to do so, unlike the statement "I am a believer" and similar, which is only said conjoined with the exception "God willing," because of the self-praise and testimony about oneself regarding faith it contains. So His saying {We believe in Allah} means: that He is the Necessary Existent, One, Unique, characterized by every attribute of perfection, free of every deficiency and defect, deserving to be singled out for all worship, and that none be associated with Him in any part of it in any way whatsoever.

{And in what has been sent down to us} includes the Qur'an and the Sunnah, by His saying: {And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom}. It includes belief in what the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger contain regarding the attributes of the Creator, the attributes of His messengers, the Last Day, the past and future unseen matters, and belief in what those contain of legal commands and rulings, rulings on recompense, and other things.

{And in what was sent down to Abraham...} to the end of the verse: it includes belief in all the books sent down upon all the prophets, and belief in the prophets generally and specifically those named in the verse, for their nobility and for bringing the great laws. Thus, what is obligatory in faith in the prophets and the books is to believe in them in a general and comprehensive manner, and then whatever is known of them in detail must be believed in detail.

As for His saying: {We make no distinction between any of them}, meaning: rather we believe in all of them. This is the distinguishing characteristic of the Muslims, which sets them apart from everyone who claims to be upon a religion. The Jews, the Christians, the Sabians and others, even if they claim that they believe in what they believe of the messengers and books, they disbelieve in others, distinguishing between the messengers and the books: they believe in some and disbelieve in others. Their denial nullifies their affirmation, for the messenger whom they claim to have believed in has confirmed all the other messengers, especially Muhammad (ﷺ). So when they deny Muhammad, they have denied their own messenger in what he told them, and this is disbelief in their messenger.

In His saying: {And what was given to the prophets from their Lord} there is evidence that the gift of religion is the true gift, connected to worldly and otherworldly happiness. He did not command us to believe in what the prophets were given of kingship, wealth and the like; rather He commanded us to believe in what they were given of books and laws. There is also in it that the prophets are conveyers from Allah and intermediaries between Allah and His creation in conveying His religion, having no share of the command whatsoever.

In His saying: {From their Lord} there is an indication that it is part of the perfection of His lordship over His servants that He sends down books to them and sends messengers to them, so His lordship does not require leaving them neglected or aimless. And since what the prophets were given was indeed from their Lord, there is in this a distinction between the prophets and those who claim prophethood, and that the distinction between them is achieved merely by knowing what they call to. The messengers call only to good and forbid only evil, and each of them confirms the others and bears witness to the truth without contradiction or inconsistency, because it is from their Lord. {Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much discrepancy.} This is unlike one who claims prophethood, for they will inevitably contradict one another in their reports, commands and prohibitions, as is known to whoever examines the conditions of all of them and knows what they call to.

When Almighty Allah had made clear everything to be believed in, generally and specifically, and since speech alone does not suffice without action, He said: {And we are to Him Muslims}, meaning: submissive to His greatness, obedient to His worship, outwardly and inwardly, sincere to Him in worship, as is shown by the placing of the object {to Him} before the verb {Muslims}.

This noble verse, despite its brevity and conciseness, includes the three kinds of Tawhid: Tawhid al-Rububiyyah (Lordship), Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah (divinity), and Tawhid al-Asma' wal-Sifat (names and attributes). It includes belief in all the messengers and all the books, the specification after generalization that indicates excellence, affirmation by the heart, tongue and limbs, and sincerity to Allah in that; it includes the distinction between the truthful messengers and the liars who claim prophethood; it includes the Creator teaching His servants how to speak, and His mercy and kindness toward them through religious blessings connected to the happiness of this world and the next. Glory be to Him who made His Book an explanation of all things, a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe.

{137} That is: if the People of the Book believe in the like of what you believe in, O assembly of believers, of all the Messengers and all the Books, the first to enter among them and the foremost and best of their seal being Muhammad (ﷺ), and the Qur'an, and they submit to God alone and do not make any distinction between any of the Messengers, "then they are rightly guided" to the straight path that leads to the Gardens of Bliss. That is, there is no way for them to be guided except by this faith, not as they claimed by their saying, "Be Jews or Christians and you will be guided," for they asserted that guidance is exclusive to what they were upon.

Guidance (al-huda) is knowledge of the truth and acting upon it, and its opposite is going astray from knowledge, and going astray from action after knowledge, which is the opposition (al-shiqaq) they were upon when they "turned away and withdrew." The one who opposes (al-mushaqq) is the one who is in one side while God and His Messenger are on the other side. Opposition necessarily entails enmity (al-muhadda) and intense hostility, whose necessary consequence is exerting every effort they are able to in harming the Messenger. Therefore God promised His Messenger that He would suffice him against them, for He is "the All-Hearing" of all voices in their differing languages, with varied needs. "The All-Knowing" of what is before them and behind them, of the unseen and the witnessed, of the outward and the inward. Since this is so, God has sufficed you against their evil, and God has fulfilled His promise to His Messenger, giving him power over them, so that He killed some of them, took captive some of them, expelled some of them, and scattered them every way. In this is one of the miracles of the Qur'an, namely the report of a thing before its occurrence, and it occurred exactly as it was reported.

{138} That is: hold fast to the sibghah of Allah, which is His religion, and stand by it with complete standing, in all its outward and inward deeds and all its beliefs, at all times, until it becomes a dye and an attribute of yours. When it becomes one of your attributes, it necessarily brings you to submit to His commands willingly, by choice, and with love, and religion becomes your nature, like the complete dye of a garment that has taken on its colour. Thus you attain the happiness of this world and the Hereafter, because religion urges toward noble morals, good deeds and lofty matters.

Therefore He said, in an expression of wonder that is firmly fixed in pure minds: ﴿And who is better than Allah in sibghah?﴾ That is, there is no sibghah better than His sibghah. If you wish to know an example that shows you the difference between the sibghah of Allah and other dyes, then judge the thing by its opposite. Consider how you see a servant who believed in his Lord with sound faith, whose faith was accompanied by humility of the heart and submission of the limbs. He never ceased to adorn himself with every good attribute, beautiful deed, complete character and noble quality, and to strip himself of every ugly attribute, vice and defect. His attributes are truthfulness in his speech and deed, patience, forbearance, chastity, courage, and kindness in word and deed, along with love of Allah, fear of Him, and hope in Him. His state is sincerity toward the One worshipped and kindness toward His servants. Now compare him with a servant who disbelieved in his Lord, fled from Him, and turned to other creatures, so that he took on ugly attributes: disbelief, polytheism, lying, treachery, deceit, cunning, lack of chastity, and harm to creatures in his words and deeds. For him there is no sincerity toward the One worshipped and no kindness toward His servants. Thus the great difference between them becomes clear to you, and it becomes evident that there is no sibghah better than the sibghah of Allah. Implicit in this is that there is no uglier dye than that of one who is dyed with other than His religion.

In His words ﴿And we are worshippers of Him﴾ is an explanation of this sibghah, which is standing by these two foundations: sincerity (al-ikhlas) and following the Messenger (al-mutaba'ah). For 'ibadah (worship) is a comprehensive term for everything that Allah loves and is pleased with of deeds and words, outward and inward, and it is not so unless Allah has prescribed it upon the tongue of His Messenger. Sincerity (al-ikhlas) is that the servant intends the Face of Allah alone in those deeds. The fronting of the object (taqdim al-ma'mul) indicates restriction. He said ﴿And we are worshippers of Him﴾, describing them with the active participle, which indicates permanence and constancy, so as to show their being characterized by this and that it has become a constant dye for them.

{139} Al-muhajjah (disputation, debate): it is argument between two or more parties concerning matters of disagreement, such that each of the two opponents seeks to support his own position and nullify the position of his adversary, and each of them strives to establish proof for that. What is required in it is that it be "in the manner that is best," by the nearest route that brings the astray back to the truth, establishes proof against the obstinate, clarifies the truth, and makes falsehood manifest. If it departs from these matters, it becomes mere contention and quarrelsome strife, in which there is no good, and it produces whatever evil it produces. The People of the Book used to claim that they were more deserving of Allah than the Muslims. This is a mere assertion requiring proof and evidence. If the Lord of all is One, not a Lord to you exclusively without us, and each of us and of you has his own deeds, then we and you are equal in this, and this does not necessitate that one of the two groups be more deserving of Allah than the other. For differentiating between two things that share something in common, without any effective distinction, is a false claim and a differentiation between things that are alike, and a manifest arrogance. Preference is attained only through sincerely directing righteous deeds to Allah alone, and this state is the attribute of the believers alone. Thus it is established that they are more deserving of Allah than others, because sincerity is the path to deliverance.

So this is the distinction between the friends of the Most Merciful and the friends of Satan, by the real attributes which people of intellect accept and which none disputes except the utterly obstinate ignoramus. In this verse there is a subtle guidance regarding the method of argument, and that matters are based on joining between things that are alike and distinguishing between things that differ.

{140} This is another claim of theirs and a dispute concerning the messengers of God. They asserted that they had a better claim to these mentioned messengers than the Muslims did. So God refuted them with His words: ﴿Are you more knowing, or is God?﴾ For God says: ﴿Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a ḥanīf (upright one), a Muslim, and he was not of the polytheists.﴾

They, however, say: "Rather, he was a Jew or a Christian." So either they are the truthful and knowing ones, or God, exalted is He, is the Truthful and Knowing One concerning this matter. One of the two alternatives is necessarily determined. The form of the answer is indefinite, yet it is in the utmost clarity and explicitness, so much so that, because of its clarity, there was no need to say "God knows best and He is most truthful," and the like, since it is evident to everyone. It is like when it is said: "Is the night brighter, or the day? Is fire hotter, or water? Is polytheism better, or monotheism?" and similar questions. Everyone who has even a little intellect knows this. Indeed, they themselves know it, and they know that Abraham and the other prophets were not Jews or Christians. Yet they concealed this knowledge and this testimony, and therefore their wrongdoing was the greatest wrongdoing. For this reason God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who conceals a testimony he has from God?﴾ This testimony is with them, deposited by God and not by creatures, which requires great concern for upholding it. But they concealed it and displayed its opposite. They combined concealing the truth and not speaking it with displaying falsehood and calling to it. Is this not the greatest wrongdoing? Yes, by God, and He will punish them for it with the most severe punishment. Therefore He said: ﴿And God is not unaware of what you do.﴾ Rather, He has counted their deeds, enumerated them, and stored up their recompense for them. ﴿Wretched is the recompense they receive, and wretched is the Fire as an abode for the wrongdoers.﴾

This is the Qur'an's method: it mentions knowledge and power right after verses containing deeds for which one is recompensed. This conveys promise and warning, encouragement and deterrence. It also conveys that mentioning the Most Beautiful Names after the rulings indicates that the religious and retributive command is an effect of those Names and one of their requirements, and that they necessitate it. Then God, exalted is He, said:

{141} Its explanation has already been given, and He repeated it to cut off attachment to created beings, and that what is relied upon is what a person himself has acquired, not the deeds of his forebears and fathers. True benefit lies in actions, not in mere affiliation to men.

{142} The first verse contains a miracle, consolation, and reassurance for the hearts of the believers, an objection, and its answer in three aspects, along with a description of the objector and a description of the one who submits to God's judgment in his religion. God informed that the foolish among the people, those who do not know their own interests but rather waste them and sell them for the lowest price, namely the Jews and Christians and those who resemble them among the objectors to God's judgments and laws, will certainly raise objections. This is because the Muslims were commanded to face Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) during their stay in Makkah, and then after the Hijrah to Madinah for about a year and a half, due to the wisdom of God in that, some of which He will indicate. His wisdom required that they be commanded to face the Ka'bah, so He informed them that the foolish among the people would surely say: ﴿What has turned them from their qiblah which they used to face?﴾; that is, the facing of Bayt al-Maqdis. That is: what turned them away from it? In that is an objection to God's judgment, His law, His grace and His kindness. He consoled them, informed them of its occurrence, and that it only occurs from one characterized by foolishness, little intellect, forbearance and religiosity. So do not be concerned with them, since the source of this speech is known. The intelligent person is not troubled by the objection of the foolish and does not give his mind to it.

The verse indicates that none objects to the judgments of God except a foolish, ignorant, stubborn person. As for the rightly-guided, believing, intelligent person, he receives the judgments of his Lord with acceptance, submission and surrender, as God the Exalted said: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should [thereafter] have any choice about their affair﴾; ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves﴾; the verse ﴿The only statement of the believers, when they are invited to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, is that they say, "We hear and we obey."﴾

In His saying "the foolish" there was enough to dispense with refuting their statement and disregarding it, but He, the Exalted, nevertheless did not leave this doubt until He removed it and uncovered it, from what would occur to some hearts of objection. So He the Exalted said, ﴿Say﴾ to them, answering: ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west. He guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾; that is: if the east and the west are the possession of Allah, and there is no direction outside His dominion, and yet He guides whom He wills to a straight path, and among that is His guidance of you to this qiblah, which is the religion of your father Ibrahim, then for what reason does the objector object to your facing a direction that falls under the dominion of Allah? You did not face a direction that is not His possession. This necessitates submission to His command by this alone, so how much more so when it is from His bounty upon you, His guidance and His kindness, that He guided you to it. The objector to you is objecting to the bounty of Allah out of envy of you and transgression.

Since His saying ﴿He guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾ is unrestricted, and the unrestricted is to be understood in light of the restricted, guidance and misguidance have causes which the wisdom and justice of Allah have made necessary. He has informed in other places of His Book of the causes of guidance which, when the servant brings them about, guidance is attained for him, as He the Exalted said: ﴿With it Allah guides whoever follows His pleasure to the ways of peace﴾. In this verse He mentioned the cause that necessitates the guidance of this nation absolutely, in all kinds of guidance, and the favor of Allah upon it, so He said:

{143} ﴿And thus We have made you a justly balanced nation﴾; that is: just, excellent. Whatever is beyond the middle is extremes, falling under danger. So Allah made this nation a middle path in all matters of religion:

A middle path regarding the prophets, between those who exaggerated about them, like the Christians, and those who neglected them, like the Jews, by believing in all of them in the manner befitting that.

A middle path in the Law: not the harshness of the Jews and their burdens, nor the laxity of the Christians.

In matters of purity and food: not like the Jews, whose prayer is valid only in their synagogues and churches, and water does not purify them from impurities, and good things were made unlawful for them as a punishment; nor like the Christians, who consider nothing impure and forbid nothing, but permit whatever crawls and walks. Rather, their purity is the most complete and perfect purity.

Allah permitted them the good things of food, drink, clothing and marriage, and forbade them the corrupt things of these. Thus this nation possesses the most complete religion, the most excellent morals, and the best deeds, and Allah bestowed upon them of knowledge, forbearance, justice and kindness what He has not bestowed upon any other nation. Therefore they are ﴿a justly balanced nation﴾, complete and moderate, so that they may be ﴿witnesses over the people﴾ by reason of their justice and judging with equity. They judge the people of all other religions, and no one judges them. Whatever this nation testifies to be accepted is accepted, and whatever it testifies to be rejected is rejected.

If it is said: how is their judgment over others accepted, when every party to a dispute is not accepted in his statement about the other?

It is said: the statement of one of the disputants is not accepted due to the presence of suspicion. But when suspicion is absent and complete justice is established, as in this nation, then the aim is judgment by justice and truth, and the condition of that is knowledge and justice, and both exist in this nation, so its statement is accepted. If anyone doubts its excellence and seeks someone to vouch for it, then their Prophet, the most perfect of creation, (ﷺ), is its vouchsafer. Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the Messenger will be a witness over you﴾.

Among the testimony of this nation over others is that on the Day of Resurrection, when Allah questions the messengers about their delivery and the disbelieving nations about that, and they deny that the prophets had delivered to them, the prophets will call this nation as witnesses, and their Prophet will vouch for them.

The verse is evidence that the consensus (ijma') of this nation is a decisive proof, and that they are protected from error, due to the unrestricted nature of His saying ﴿a middle nation﴾. For if their agreement upon error were assumed, they would not be a middle nation except in some matters. [And His saying ﴿that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ requires that when they testify that Allah has made lawful, or forbidden, or obligated a ruling, they are protected in that.] And in it is the stipulation of justice (ʿadalah) in judgment, testimony, giving legal opinions (fatwa), and the like.

﴿And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels﴾; that is, the facing of Bayt al-Maqdis at first. ﴿Except that We might know﴾; that is, knowledge connected to reward and punishment, for He is otherwise knowing of all things before their existence. But this knowledge does not make reward or punishment contingent upon it, because of His perfect justice and the establishment of proof upon His servants. Rather, when their deeds exist, reward and punishment are ordained upon them. That is: We legislated that qiblah so that We might know and test ﴿who follows the Messenger﴾, who believes in him and follows him in every situation, because he is a commanded and directed servant. And because the previous scriptures had informed that he would face the Ka'bah, the fair-minded person whose aim is the truth is increased in faith and obedience to the Messenger by that. As for the one who turns back on his heels, turns away from the truth and follows his desire, he increases in disbelief upon his disbelief and bewilderment upon his bewilderment, and he presents a false argument based on a doubt that has no reality. ﴿And indeed, it was [a great matter]﴾; that is, its turning away from it was ﴿difficult﴾; that is, burdensome, ﴿except for those whom Allah has guided﴾. They recognized thereby the favor of Allah upon them, and were thankful and acknowledged His kindness in directing them to this great House, which He preferred over the rest of the lands and made its intention one of the pillars of Islam and a destroyer of sins and transgressions. Therefore that became light for them, and burdensome for others.

Then He the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah would never make your faith ineffective﴾; that is: it is not befitting nor suitable for Him, the Exalted, but rather it is impossible for Him. He informed that it is impossible and inconceivable for Him to waste your faith. In this is a great glad tidings for those upon whom Allah has bestowed Islam and faith, that Allah will preserve their faith for them and not waste it. Its preservation is of two kinds: preservation from being lost and nullified, by protecting them from every corrupter and remover of it, and from things that diminish it, such as distressing trials and obstructing desires; and preservation by increasing it for them and granting them success in what increases their faith and perfects their certainty. Just as He began by guiding you to faith, He will preserve it for you and complete His favor by increasing it and increasing its reward and recompense, and preserving it from every troubling thing. Indeed, when trials exist whose purpose is to distinguish the true believer from the liar, they purify the believers and manifest their sincerity. It seems that in this there is a safeguard against what might be said, that His saying ﴿And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except that We might know who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels﴾ might be a cause for some believers to abandon their faith. So He removed this illusion by His saying ﴿And Allah would never make your faith ineffective﴾, by His decree of this trial or other. This includes those believers who died before the turning of the Ka'bah, for Allah does not waste their faith, because they complied with the command of Allah and the obedience to His Messenger at its time; and obedience to Allah is compliance with His command at every time according to that. In this verse is evidence for the school of Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah that faith includes the deeds of the limbs.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is, toward the people, Kind and Merciful﴾; that is: most intensely merciful toward them. From His kindness and mercy toward them is that He completes His favor upon them, which He began for them; that He distinguished from them those who entered faith with their tongues without their hearts; that He tested them with a test by which He increased their faith and raised their rank; and that He directed them to the most noble and excellent of houses.

{143} ﴿And thus We have made you a justly balanced nation﴾; that is: just, excellent. Whatever is beyond the middle is extremes, falling under danger. So Allah made this nation a middle path in all matters of religion:

A middle path regarding the prophets, between those who exaggerated about them, like the Christians, and those who neglected them, like the Jews, by believing in all of them in the manner befitting that.

A middle path in the Law: not the harshness of the Jews and their burdens, nor the laxity of the Christians.

In matters of purity and food: not like the Jews, whose prayer is valid only in their synagogues and churches, and water does not purify them from impurities, and good things were made unlawful for them as a punishment; nor like the Christians, who consider nothing impure and forbid nothing, but permit whatever crawls and walks. Rather, their purity is the most complete and perfect purity.

Allah permitted them the good things of food, drink, clothing and marriage, and forbade them the corrupt things of these. Thus this nation possesses the most complete religion, the most excellent morals, and the best deeds, and Allah bestowed upon them of knowledge, forbearance, justice and kindness what He has not bestowed upon any other nation. Therefore they are ﴿a justly balanced nation﴾, complete and moderate, so that they may be ﴿witnesses over the people﴾ by reason of their justice and judging with equity. They judge the people of all other religions, and no one judges them. Whatever this nation testifies to be accepted is accepted, and whatever it testifies to be rejected is rejected.

If it is said: how is their judgment over others accepted, when every party to a dispute is not accepted in his statement about the other?

It is said: the statement of one of the disputants is not accepted due to the presence of suspicion. But when suspicion is absent and complete justice is established, as in this nation, then the aim is judgment by justice and truth, and the condition of that is knowledge and justice, and both exist in this nation, so its statement is accepted. If anyone doubts its excellence and seeks someone to vouch for it, then their Prophet, the most perfect of creation, (ﷺ), is its vouchsafer. Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the Messenger will be a witness over you﴾.

Among the testimony of this nation over others is that on the Day of Resurrection, when Allah questions the messengers about their delivery and the disbelieving nations about that, and they deny that the prophets had delivered to them, the prophets will call this nation as witnesses, and their Prophet will vouch for them.

The verse is evidence that the consensus (ijma') of this nation is a decisive proof, and that they are protected from error, due to the unrestricted nature of His saying ﴿a middle nation﴾. For if their agreement upon error were assumed, they would not be a middle nation except in some matters. [And His saying ﴿that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ requires that when they testify that Allah has made lawful, or forbidden, or obligated a ruling, they are protected in that.] And in it is the stipulation of justice (ʿadalah) in judgment, testimony, giving legal opinions (fatwa), and the like.

﴿And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels﴾; that is, the facing of Bayt al-Maqdis at first. ﴿Except that We might know﴾; that is, knowledge connected to reward and punishment, for He is otherwise knowing of all things before their existence. But this knowledge does not make reward or punishment contingent upon it, because of His perfect justice and the establishment of proof upon His servants. Rather, when their deeds exist, reward and punishment are ordained upon them. That is: We legislated that qiblah so that We might know and test ﴿who follows the Messenger﴾, who believes in him and follows him in every situation, because he is a commanded and directed servant. And because the previous scriptures had informed that he would face the Ka'bah, the fair-minded person whose aim is the truth is increased in faith and obedience to the Messenger by that. As for the one who turns back on his heels, turns away from the truth and follows his desire, he increases in disbelief upon his disbelief and bewilderment upon his bewilderment, and he presents a false argument based on a doubt that has no reality. ﴿And indeed, it was [a great matter]﴾; that is, its turning away from it was ﴿difficult﴾; that is, burdensome, ﴿except for those whom Allah has guided﴾. They recognized thereby the favor of Allah upon them, and were thankful and acknowledged His kindness in directing them to this great House, which He preferred over the rest of the lands and made its intention one of the pillars of Islam and a destroyer of sins and transgressions. Therefore that became light for them, and burdensome for others.

Then He the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah would never make your faith ineffective﴾; that is: it is not befitting nor suitable for Him, the Exalted, but rather it is impossible for Him. He informed that it is impossible and inconceivable for Him to waste your faith. In this is a great glad tidings for those upon whom Allah has bestowed Islam and faith, that Allah will preserve their faith for them and not waste it. Its preservation is of two kinds: preservation from being lost and nullified, by protecting them from every corrupter and remover of it, and from things that diminish it, such as distressing trials and obstructing desires; and preservation by increasing it for them and granting them success in what increases their faith and perfects their certainty. Just as He began by guiding you to faith, He will preserve it for you and complete His favor by increasing it and increasing its reward and recompense, and preserving it from every troubling thing. Indeed, when trials exist whose purpose is to distinguish the true believer from the liar, they purify the believers and manifest their sincerity. It seems that in this there is a safeguard against what might be said, that His saying ﴿And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except that We might know who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels﴾ might be a cause for some believers to abandon their faith. So He removed this illusion by His saying ﴿And Allah would never make your faith ineffective﴾, by His decree of this trial or other. This includes those believers who died before the turning of the Ka'bah, for Allah does not waste their faith, because they complied with the command of Allah and the obedience to His Messenger at its time; and obedience to Allah is compliance with His command at every time according to that. In this verse is evidence for the school of Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah that faith includes the deeds of the limbs.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is, toward the people, Kind and Merciful﴾; that is: most intensely merciful toward them. From His kindness and mercy toward them is that He completes His favor upon them, which He began for them; that He distinguished from them those who entered faith with their tongues without their hearts; that He tested them with a test by which He increased their faith and raised their rank; and that He directed them to the most noble and excellent of houses.

{144} God says to His Prophet: {We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the sky}; that is, his frequent turning of his face in all directions, out of longing and expectation for the descent of revelation concerning facing the Ka'bah. He said {your face} and did not say {your sight}, to increase the emphasis on his concern, and because turning the face necessitates turning the sight. {So We will surely turn you to a qiblah You will be pleased with}; that is, We will direct you to it by Our appointing you to it, {a qiblah you will be pleased with}; that is, you will love it, and it is the Ka'bah. In this there is a demonstration of his virtue and nobility, peace and blessings be upon him, since God, exalted is He, hastens to fulfill his pleasure. Then He explicitly commanded him to face it, saying: {So turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque}; and the "face" (wajh) is that part of the human body which faces forward. {And wherever you are}; that is, on land or sea, in the east or west, south or north, {turn your faces toward it}; that is, toward its direction. In this is the requirement of facing the Ka'bah for all prayers, obligatory and voluntary, and that if it is possible to face the very structure, then that is required; otherwise, it suffices to face its side and direction. And that turning the body away invalidates the prayer, because a command to do something is a prohibition of its opposite.

When God, exalted is He, mentioned earlier the objectors to this among the People of the Book and others, and mentioned their answer, He here mentioned that the People of the Book and the learned among them know that you are in this upon a clear truth, because of what they find in their books, yet they object out of obstinacy and rebellion. If they know of their own error, then do not be concerned about it, for a person is only troubled by the objection of one who objects to him when the matter is uncertain and it is possible that the objector is right. But when it is certain that the correct position and truth are with the one being objected to, and the objector is stubborn and knows his claim is false, then there is no room for concern. Rather, the objector awaits worldly and otherworldly punishment. Therefore God, exalted is He, said: {And God is not unaware of what you do}; rather, He records their deeds and recompenses them for them. In this is a warning to the objectors and consolation for the believers.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 145:

{145} The Prophet (ﷺ), out of the perfection of his eagerness for the guidance of creation, would expend the utmost of what he was able to give in counsel, and would be gentle in guiding them, and would grieve when they did not submit to the command of Allah. Among the disbelievers were those who rebelled against the command of Allah, were arrogant toward the messengers of Allah, and abandoned guidance deliberately and with hostility. Among them were the Jews and the Christians, the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab) of old, who disbelieved in Muhammad with certainty, not out of ignorance. Therefore Allah, exalted is He, informed him that even if you brought to those who were given the Book {every sign}; that is, every proof and evidence that clarifies your statement and makes plain what you call to, {they would not follow your qibla}; that is, they would not follow you. This is because following the qibla is a sign of following him, and because the cause is the matter of the qibla itself. The matter is thus because they are obstinate; they knew the truth and abandoned it. Signs benefit only the one who seeks the truth while it is unclear to him, so the clear signs make it evident to him. As for one who has resolved not to follow the truth, there is no remedy for him. Also, their disagreement among themselves exists, and some of them do not follow the qibla of others. So it is not strange from them, in addition to this, that they do not follow your qibla, O Muhammad, for they are truly enemies and envious. His saying {and you are not one who follows their qibla} is more emphatic than saying "and do not follow," because that implies that he (ﷺ) would be characterized by opposing them, and so it cannot occur from him. He did not say "even if they were brought every sign," because they have no proof for their saying. Likewise, when the truth has become clear through its certain proofs, it is not necessary to bring answers to the doubts that are raised against it, since they have no limit; and because he knows their falsehood, by the knowledge that everything that contradicts clear truth is false, so resolving doubts falls under the category of voluntary effort (tabarru').
{And if you were to follow their desires}; he said "their desires" and did not say "their religion," because what they are upon is merely desires of the self, to the extent that in their hearts they know that it is not a religion, and whoever abandons religion follows desire without doubt. Allah, exalted is He, said: {Have you seen one who has taken his own desire as his god?} {after the knowledge that has come to you}; that you are upon the truth and they are upon falsehood. {Indeed, you would then be} (إذاً); that is, if you followed them. This is a qualification lest this sentence be separated from what precedes it, even in understanding. {Certainly among the wrongdoers}; that is, included among them and counted within their number. And what injustice is greater than the injustice of one who knows truth and falsehood and then prefers falsehood over truth? Although the address is to him (ﷺ), his community is included in this. Also, if he (ﷺ), were he to do that, which is far from him, would become a wrongdoer despite his high rank and abundant goodness, then others are all the more and more fittingly so. Then Allah, exalted is He, said:

{146} Almighty God informs that the People of the Book have a firm, established knowledge that Muhammad is the Messenger of God and that what he has brought is truth and sincerity. They are as certain of it as they are certain of their own sons, such that they cannot confuse them with anyone else. Thus their knowledge of Muhammad (ﷺ) reached a point where they have no doubt and no hesitation about it. Yet a group among them, who are most of them, those who disbelieved in him, concealed this testimony despite their certainty of it, and they know. ﴿And who is more unjust than one who conceals a testimony he has from God?﴾ Within this is consolation for the Messenger and the believers, and a warning to them against their evil and their dubious practices. And a group among them did not conceal the truth knowingly; among them are those who believed in it, and among them are those who disbelieved in it out of ignorance.

So it is incumbent upon the scholar to make the truth manifest, to clarify it, and to adorn it with everything he is able to use, whether expression, proof, example, or other means; and to nullify falsehood, distinguish it from the truth, and make it ugly and repugnant to souls by every means that leads to that. These concealers reversed the matter, so their own conditions were reversed.

{147} ﴿The truth is from your Lord﴾; i.e., this truth, which is most deserving of being called truth above everything else, because of what it contains of lofty aims, good commands, the purification of souls, and urging them to attain their benefits and repel their harms, since it proceeds from your Lord, whose nurturing of you includes that He sent down to you this Qur'an, in which is the nurturing of minds, souls, and all benefits. ﴿So do not be among the doubters﴾; i.e., let no slightest doubt or suspicion about it arise in you. Rather, reflect upon it and contemplate it until you reach certainty through it, for reflection upon it is inevitably a repeller of doubt and a means to certainty.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 148:

{148} That is: every people of a religion and creed has a direction (wijhah) toward which they turn in their worship. The matter is not the facing of the qibla, for that is among the legal rulings (shara'i') whose times and circumstances vary, and into which abrogation (naskh) and transfer from one direction to another enter. Rather, the whole matter lies in complying with the obedience of God, drawing near to Him, and seeking nearness (zulfa) with Him. This is the emblem of happiness and the banner of divine friendship (wilayah). When souls do not possess it, they incur the loss of this world and the Hereafter; and when they possess it, they are the true winners. This is a matter agreed upon in all the legal systems, and it is that for which God created creation and commanded them. The command to race toward good deeds (al-istibaq ila al-khayrat) is a degree beyond the command to perform good deeds, for racing toward them includes performing them, perfecting them, carrying them out in the most complete states, and hastening to them. Whoever precedes others in this world to the good deeds is the one who precedes others in the Hereafter to the Gardens. Thus "the foremost" (al-sabiqun) are the highest of creation in rank. The good deeds include all obligatory and voluntary acts: prayer, fasting, zakat, pilgrimage (hajj), lesser pilgrimage (umrah), jihad, and beneficence that is both beyond and within the self. Since the strongest thing that urges souls toward hastening to good and energizes them is the reward God has ordained for it, He said: {Wherever you are, God will bring you all together. Indeed, God is over all things competent.} That is: He will gather you together on the Day of Resurrection by His power, and He will recompense every doer for his deed; {that He may reward those who did evil according to what they did and reward those who did good with the best}.

This noble verse is cited as evidence for performing every virtue that characterizes an act, such as praying at the beginning of its time, hastening to discharge one's obligation of fasting, hajj, umrah and paying zakat, and performing the recommended practices (sunan) and etiquettes (adab) of acts of worship. How comprehensive and beneficial a verse it is!

{149} That is: "And from wherever you set out" — on your journeys and otherwise; this is general — "then turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque," that is, toward its direction. Then He addressed the community in general, saying:

{150} "And wherever you are, turn your faces toward it." He said: "And indeed it is the truth from your Lord," emphasizing it with inna and the lam, so that no one would have the slightest doubt about it, and so that it would not be thought that it is a matter of whim rather than of obedience. "And Allah is not unaware of what you do": rather, He is watching over you in all your conditions, so be courteous toward Him and be mindful of Him by complying with His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, for your deeds are not overlooked; rather, you will be recompensed for them in full. If they are good, the reward is good, and if they are evil, the requital is evil.

He said here: "So that the people will have no argument against you" — that is, We have prescribed for you facing the Sacred Ka'bah, so that the arguments of the people, from among the People of the Book and the polytheists, be cut off from you. For if it had remained facing Bayt al-Maqdis, an argument would have been directed against it, since the People of the Book find in their scripture that its permanent qibla is the Ka'bah, the Sacred House. The polytheists consider this great House to be one of their sources of pride, and that it belongs to the creed of Ibrahim. If Muhammad (ﷺ) did not face it, their arguments would have turned toward him, and they would have said: "How can he claim to be upon the creed of Ibrahim while he is of his offspring and has abandoned facing his qibla?" So by facing the qibla, the proof was established against the People of the Book and the polytheists, and their arguments against him were cut off, "except those of them who do wrong": that is, whoever among them argues with an argument in which he is a wrongdoer, having no basis for it except following desire and injustice. There is no path to persuading such a person or arguing with him. Likewise, there is no sense in treating the doubts they raise as an argument deserving of attention or consideration. Therefore Allah, exalted is He, said: "So do not fear them," for their argument is false, and falsehood, like its name, is forsaken — its holder is forsaken. This is in contrast to the possessor of truth, for truth has a force and dignity that necessitates fear of the one who holds it. Allah commanded fear of Him, which is the foundation of all good; whoever does not fear Allah does not refrain from His disobedience and does not comply with His command.

The turning of the Muslims toward the Ka'bah was a matter in which a great trial occurred, which the People of the Book, the hypocrites, and the polytheists spread about, multiplying words and doubts concerning it. Therefore Allah expanded upon it, explained it in the most complete manner, and emphasized it with various kinds of emphasis contained in these verses.

Among them: the command regarding it is repeated three times, though a single repetition would have sufficed.

Among them: it is customary that a command is either directed to the Messenger, so that the community is included [by implication], or to the community in general. In this verse, a command is addressed to the Messenger specifically in His words "So turn your face," and to the community in general in His words "So turn your faces."

Among them: it refutes all the false arguments that the obstinate ones raised, nullifying them one by one, as their clarification has already passed.

Among them: it cut off the hopes of those who sought to have the Messenger follow the qibla of the People of the Book.

Among them: His words "And indeed it is the truth from your Lord." The mere report of the Truthful, the Mighty, is sufficient and healing; yet despite this He said: "And indeed it is the truth from your Lord."

Among them: He informed, while He is the Knower of hidden things, that the validity of this matter is firmly established among the People of the Book, yet they conceal this testimony despite knowing it.

Since His directing us to face the qibla is a tremendous blessing, and His kindness and mercy toward this community never cease to increase, and whenever He prescribes a law for them it is a great blessing, He said: "And that I may complete My favor upon you." The root of the blessing is guidance to His religion through sending His Messenger and sending down His Book. Then, after this, the blessings that complete this root are countless and cannot be enumerated, from the time Allah sent His Messenger until the time of his departure from this world drew near. Allah gave him conditions and blessings, and gave his community what completed His favor upon him and upon them. Allah revealed to him: "Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favor upon you, and approved Islam as a religion for you."

So to Allah belongs praise for His bounty, which we cannot reckon, let alone give thanks for as it deserves. "And that you may be guided": that is, that you may know the truth and act upon it. Allah, blessed and exalted, out of His mercy toward the servants, has facilitated for them the means of guidance to the utmost ease, and alerted them to following its paths, and explained them to them in the most complete explanation. Among that is that He raises up opponents of the truth who dispute about it, so that the truth becomes clear through that, its signs and marks appear, and the falsehood's nullity becomes evident, that it has no reality. Had it not been for its standing in opposition to the truth, the condition of falsehood would perhaps not have been made clear to most people. Things are made manifest by their opposites: were it not for the night, the virtue of day would not be recognized; were it not for ugliness, the virtue of beauty would not be recognized; were it not for darkness, the benefit of light would not be recognized; and were it not for falsehood, the truth would not have become manifestly clear. So to Allah belongs praise for that.

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 2, verses 151–152:**

{151} He, exalted is He, says: Our bestowal of favour upon you by directing you to the Ka'bah (the Sacred House) and by completing it with the laws and the complete blessings is not something novel from Our kindness, nor is it its first instance. Rather, We have bestowed upon you the foundations of blessings and what completes them. Then the completion of that was Our sending to you this noble Messenger from among yourselves, whose lineage, truthfulness, trustworthiness, perfection and sincerity you know. ﴿He recites to you Our verses﴾; this encompasses the Qur'anic verses and others. So he recites to you the verses that make clear the truth from falsehood and guidance from error, which first guided you to the Oneness of Allah and His perfection, then to the truthfulness of His Messenger and the obligation of believing in him, then to all that he informed of concerning the Hereafter and the unseen, until you attained complete guidance and certain knowledge. ﴿And purifies you﴾; that is, he purifies your character and your souls by training them in beautiful morals and cleansing them of blameworthy morals. This is like purifying them from polytheism to Monotheism, from showing off to sincerity, from lying to truthfulness, from treachery to trustworthiness, from arrogance to humility, from bad character to good character, and from mutual hatred, shunning and severing of ties to mutual love, connection and affection, and other kinds of purification. ﴿And teaches you the Book﴾; that is, the Qur'an, its wording and its meanings, ﴿and the wisdom﴾. It has been said that this is the Sunnah. It has also been said that wisdom is knowing the secrets of the Sharia and understanding it, and placing matters in their proper places. On this view, teaching the Sunnah falls within teaching the Book, because the Sunnah clarifies the Qur'an, explains it and expresses it. ﴿And teaches you what you did not know﴾; because before his mission they were in manifest error, with neither knowledge nor action. So every knowledge or action this Ummah has attained came through his hand (ﷺ) and because of him.

These blessings are the foundations of blessings in the absolute sense, and they are the greatest blessings Allah bestows upon His servants. Therefore their duty is to thank Allah for them and to fulfil them. For this reason, Allah, exalted is He, said:

{152} ﴿So remember Me, I will remember you﴾; He, exalted is He, commanded remembrance of Him and promised in return the best reward, which is His remembrance of the one who remembers Him, as He said on the tongue of His Messenger: "Whoever remembers Me in himself, I remember him in Myself; and whoever remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than theirs." Remembrance is the head of thanks. Therefore He commanded it specifically, and then after it commanded thanks in general, saying: ﴿And give thanks to Me﴾; that is, for what I have bestowed upon you of these blessings and what I have averted from you of the various calamities. Then the completion of that was Our sending to you this noble Messenger from among yourselves, whose lineage, truthfulness, trustworthiness, perfection and sincerity you know. ﴿He recites to you Our verses﴾; this encompasses the Qur'anic verses and others. So he recites to you the verses that make clear the truth from falsehood and guidance from error, which first guided you to the Oneness of Allah and His perfection, then to the truthfulness of His Messenger and the obligation of believing in him, then to all that he informed of concerning the Hereafter and the unseen, until you attained complete guidance and certain knowledge. ﴿And purifies you﴾; that is, he purifies your character and your souls by training them in beautiful morals and cleansing them of blameworthy morals.
