Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 153:

{153} God, exalted is He, commanded the believers to seek help with their religious and worldly affairs {through patience and prayer}. Patience (sabr) is restraining and withholding the self from what it dislikes. It is of three kinds: patience in obeying God until one performs the act; patience in refraining from disobedience to God until one abandons it; and patience in God's painful decrees, so that one does not resent them.

Patience is the greatest aid in every matter, for there is no way for one who lacks patience to attain his goal, especially in arduous and continuous acts of worship, which depend most profoundly on bearing patience and swallowing the hard bitterness. When the one who practices them perseveres in patience, he succeeds. But if hardship and difficulty turn him away from patience and perseverance in it, he attains nothing and obtains deprivation. Likewise with sin, where the soul's impulses and urges toward it are strong and it lies within the servant's capacity. Such sin cannot be abandoned except with great patience and by restraining the impulses and urges of the heart for the sake of God, and by seeking God's help to be protected from it, for it is among the great trials. Likewise with severe affliction, especially if it persists, for with it the psychological and physical powers weaken, and its natural consequence, resentment, arises unless its bearer opposes it with patience for God, reliance upon Him, turning to Him, and constant need of Him. Thus you know that patience is something the servant needs, indeed is compelled to have in every state of his. For this reason God commanded it and informed that He is {with the patient}; that is, with those for whom patience is a disposition, a quality, and a settled trait, by His help, His grace, and His support. Hardships and adversities become light for them through this, every great matter becomes easy for them, and every difficulty leaves them. This is a special companionship that entails His love, His help, His victory, and His nearness, and it is a great distinction for the patient. Even if the patient had no virtue except that they attain this companionship from God, it would suffice them as excellence and honor. As for the general companionship, it is the companionship of knowledge and power, as in His saying: ﴿And He is with you wherever you are﴾, and this is general to all creation.

God, exalted is He, also commanded seeking help through prayer, because prayer is the pillar of religion and the light of the believers, and it is the connection between the servant and his Lord. When the servant's prayer is complete, comprising all that is obligatory in it and all that is recommended, and when it includes presence of heart, which is its essence, then whenever the servant enters into it he feels that he is entering into the presence of his Lord and standing before Him in the position of a servant who serves and behaves with courtesy, being mindful of everything he says and does, immersed in intimate conversation with his Lord and supplication to Him. Undoubtedly, this prayer is among the greatest aids in all matters, for prayer forbids indecency and wrongdoing. Moreover, this presence that occurs in prayer produces in the servant's heart a quality and a motive that calls him to comply with his Lord's commands and avoid His prohibitions. This is the prayer through which God commanded us to seek help in everything.

{154} When the Exalted and Blessed One mentioned the command to seek help through patience in all circumstances, He gave an example of what patience is used to endure: jihad in His cause. It is the best of the bodily acts of worship and the hardest on souls, because of its hardship in itself and because it entails killing and the loss of life. Those who desire this world only desire life and its requirements, so everything they do is a pursuit of it and a repelling of what opposes it.

It is well known that a sensible person does not give up a beloved thing except for something beloved that is higher and greater than it. Thus God, exalted is He, informed that whoever is killed in His cause, that is, who fights in the cause of God so that the word of God is supreme and His religion prevails, and not for any other aim, has not lost the beloved life. Rather, he has gained a life greater and more perfect than you imagine and suppose. "The martyrs are alive with their Lord, receiving provision. They rejoice in what God has given them of His bounty, and they rejoice for those who have not yet joined them from behind them, that no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve. They rejoice in a favor from God and bounty, and that God does not waste the reward of the believers" (﴿Ali 'Imran 3:169-171).

Is there any greater than this life, which includes nearness to God, their enjoyment of His provision in delicious food and drink for the body, and the spiritual provision, which is joy, rejoicing, and the removal of every fear and sorrow? This is an intermediate life (barzakhiyyah) more perfect than the life of this world. Indeed, the Prophet (ﷺ) informed that the souls of the martyrs are in the crops of green birds that graze in the rivers of Paradise, eat of its fruits, and take refuge in lamps suspended beneath the Throne.

In this verse there is the greatest exhortation to jihad in the cause of God and to persistence in patience in it. Had the servants perceived what reward the slain in God's cause have, none would have held back from it. But the lack of complete certain knowledge is what weakens resolve, increases the sleep of the sleeper, and forfeits great rewards and spoils. Why would it not be so, when God, exalted is He, has "bought from the believers their souls and their wealth, in return for which they will have Paradise: they fight in God's cause, so they kill and are killed" (﴿at-Tawbah 9:111﴾)?

By God, if a person had a thousand souls, each one departing in the cause of God, it would be insignificant beside this great reward.

For this reason, the martyrs, after having witnessed God's reward and the goodness of His recompense, wish only to be returned to the world, so that they may be killed in His cause again and again.

In this verse is evidence for the bliss and punishment of the barzakh (intermediate state), as many texts have repeatedly affirmed.

{155} God, exalted is He, informs that He will certainly test His servants with trials, so that the truthful is distinguished from the liar, and the impatient from the patient. This is His sunnah (established way) regarding His servants. For if ease (al-sarra) were to continue for the people of faith without any trial accompanying it, mixing would occur, which is corruption, and the wisdom of God requires the distinguishing of the people of good from the people of evil. This is the benefit of trials: not the removal of the faith that is with the believers, nor turning them back from their religion, for God would never waste the faith of the believers.

So in this verse He informs that He will test His servants {with something of fear}, that is, from enemies; {and hunger}, that is, with a small measure of these two, because if He tested them with all of the fear or the hunger, they would perish, whereas trials purify and do not destroy; {and loss of wealth}, and this encompasses all loss that befalls wealth, from heavenly calamities, drowning, loss, the seizing of wealth by oppressive rulers, highwaymen, and other things; {and lives}, that is, the departure of loved ones among children, relatives and companions, and among kinds of sickness in the body of the servant or in the body of one he loves; {and fruits}, that is, grains, date palms, all trees and vegetables, by hail, cold, burning, or a heavenly blight such as locusts and the like. These matters must occur, because the All-Knowing, the All-Aware, has informed of them, and so they occur as He has informed. When they occur, people divide into two groups: the impatient and the patient.

The impatient one suffers two calamities: the loss of what he loves, which is the existence of this calamity, and the loss of what is greater than it, which is the reward for complying with God's command to be patient. Thus he gains loss and deprivation, the decrease of the faith he has, and he forfeits patience, contentment and gratitude, and there befalls him discontent, which indicates severe deficiency.

As for the one whom God enables to be patient when these calamities occur, he restrains himself from displeasure, in speech and in action, seeks his reward from God, and knows that the reward he will obtain through his patience is greater than the calamity that has befallen him. Indeed, the calamity becomes a blessing for him, because it becomes a path to obtaining what is better and more beneficial for him than it. He has complied with God's command and gained the reward. Therefore God, exalted is He, said: {And give glad tidings to the patient}, that is, give them the good news that they will be paid their reward without reckoning. The patient are those who have attained the great glad tidings and the abundant bounty. Then He described them by His saying:

{156} {Who, when a calamity strikes them}, which is everything that pains the heart, the body, or both, of what has been mentioned before, {they say: Indeed we belong to God}, that is, we are owned by God, governed under His command and disposal, and so we have nothing of our own selves and our wealth. When He tests us with something of these, the Most Merciful of the merciful has disposed of His own servants and their wealth, so there is no objection to Him. Rather, from the perfection of the servant's servitude is his knowledge that the occurrence of the affliction is from the Wise Owner, who is more merciful to His servant than the servant is to himself. This requires in him contentment with God and gratitude to Him for His management of what is good for His servant, even if he does not perceive it. And although we belong to God, {indeed to Him we shall return} on the Day of Return, and each doer will be recompensed for his deed. If we are patient and seek reward, we will find our reward abundantly with Him; and if we become impatient and discontented, our share will be nothing but discontent and the loss of the reward. Thus, the servant's being God's and returning to Him is among the strongest causes of patience.

{157} {Those}, namely those described with the patience mentioned, {upon them are blessings from their Lord}, that is, praise and honouring of their condition; {and mercy}, a great mercy. Among His mercy to them is that He enabled them to be patient, by which they attain perfection of reward. {And those are the guided}, who have recognised the truth. Here the truth means their knowledge that they belong to God and that they will return to Him, and their acting upon it; and here it is their patience for God's sake. This verse indicates that whoever does not be patient has the opposite of what they have, so there befalls him blame from God, punishment, misguidance and loss. How great is the difference between the two groups, how little is the hardship of the patient, and how great is the suffering of the impatient.

These two verses contain the conditioning of souls to calamities before they occur, so that they become light and easy when they do occur; an explanation of what one should meet them with when they occur, which is patience; an explanation of what helps one to be patient and what reward the patient have. The state of the one who is not patient is known by the opposite of the state of the patient. And this trial and testing is the sunnah of God which has already passed, and you will never find any change in the sunnah of God; and an explanation of the kinds of calamities.

{158} The Exalted says: "Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah" — two well-known hills — "are among the symbols of Allah," i.e., the apparent markers of His religion through which He has His servants worship Him. Since they are among the symbols of Allah, Allah has commanded the glorification of His symbols, saying: ﴿And whoever honors the symbols of Allah, indeed it is from the piety of hearts﴾. The combination of the two texts shows that they are among the symbols of Allah, and that glorifying His symbols is from the piety of hearts. Piety is obligatory upon every responsible person, and this indicates that sa'y (running) between them is an obligatory pillar (fard lazim) of Hajj and 'Umrah, as the majority (al-jumhur) hold, and as the prophetic hadiths indicate, and as the Prophet (ﷺ) performed it, and he said: "Take your rites from me" (khudhu 'anni manasikakum).

﴿So whoever performs Hajj to the House or performs 'Umrah, there is no blame upon him for going back and forth between them﴾. This is a refutation of the misconception and scruple that some Muslims had about circumambulating between them, because in the pre-Islamic period idols were worshipped at them. Allah negated blame to dispel this misconception, not because it is not obligatory. The restriction of the negation of blame to those who go between them during Hajj and 'Umrah indicates that one does not perform sa'y voluntarily on its own, except when it is combined with Hajj or 'Umrah—unlike the circumambulation of the House, which is legislated alongside 'Umrah and Hajj and is also an independent act of worship.

As for sa'y, standing at 'Arafah, standing at Muzdalifah, and throwing the pebbles (al-jimar), these follow the rites (al-nusuk). If they were performed without being connected to the rites, they would be an innovation (bid'ah), because innovation is of two kinds: one kind is worshipping Allah with an act He has not legislated at all, and the other is worshipping Him with an act He has legislated but in a specific form, and then performing it in a form other than that one—and this is of that kind.

His saying: ﴿And whoever volunteers﴾, i.e., performs an act of obedience sincerely for Allah, ﴿good﴾, such as Hajj, 'Umrah, circumambulation, prayer, fasting and other things, ﴿it is better for him﴾. This indicates that whenever a servant increases in obedience to Allah, his good, perfection and rank with Allah increase in proportion to the increase of his faith. The restriction of voluntary acts to "good" indicates that whoever volunteers with innovations that Allah and His Messenger have not legislated gains nothing but fatigue, and it is not good for him; rather, it may be evil for him if he does it deliberately and knowingly, since the act is not legislated.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Grateful and All-Knowing﴾. Ash-Shakir and ash-Shakur are among the names of Allah, the Exalted, who accepts from His servants even small deeds and rewards them with great reward. When His servant carries out His commands and complies with His obedience, He helps him in that, praises him, commends him, and recompenses him with light, faith and expansiveness in the heart, with strength and vigor in the body, with increased blessing and growth in all his circumstances, and with increased success in his deeds. Then, after that, he arrives at the deferred reward with his Lord, complete and full, not diminished by these matters. Among His gratitude to His servant is that whoever leaves something for Allah, Allah replaces it for him with something better; whoever draws near to Him a span, He draws near to him a cubit; whoever draws near to Him a cubit, He draws near to him a fathom; whoever comes to Him walking, He comes to him running; and whoever deals with Him, He returns to him profit manifold. And despite being Grateful, He is All-Knowing of who deserves complete reward according to his intention, faith and piety, versus those who are not so. He is All-Knowing of the deeds of His servants, so He does not waste them; rather, they find them more complete than they were, in accordance with their intentions, which the All-Knowing, All-Wise has perceived.

{159} Although this verse was revealed concerning the People of the Book and what they concealed regarding the matter and attributes of the Messenger (ﷺ), its ruling is general for everyone who is characterized by concealing what God has sent down, {of the clear proofs} that indicate the truth and make it manifest, {and the guidance}, which is the knowledge through which one is guided to the straight path and by which the way of the people of bliss is distinguished from the way of the people of the Hellfire. God has taken a covenant from the people of knowledge that they should make clear to the people what God has bestowed upon them of the knowledge of the Book, and not conceal it. Whoever casts that aside and combines the two corruptions, concealing what God has sent down and deceiving the servants of God, {God curses them}, meaning He removes them far away and expels them from His nearness and His mercy, {and those who curse curse them}, and they are all of creation. So the curse falls upon them from all of creation, because of their striving to deceive people, corrupt their religions, and distance them from the mercy of God. They are recompensed in kind for their deeds, just as the teacher of people in goodness is blessed by God, His angels, and even the fish in the depths of the water, because of his striving for the welfare of creation, the reform of their religions, and bringing them nearer to the mercy of God; he is recompensed in kind for his work. The one who conceals what God has sent down opposes the command of God and opposes God; God makes the verses clear to people and explains them, while he strives to obliterate and hide them. Therefore he deserves this severe threat.

{160} {Except those who repent}, meaning they turn back from the sins they were engaged in, with remorse, giving them up, and resolving not to return to them, {and make amends}, correcting whatever was corrupted of their deeds. Abandoning the evil is not sufficient until the good is done. Nor is that sufficient for the concealer either, until he clarifies what he concealed and displays the opposite of what he hid. Such a person, God accepts his repentance, because God's acceptance of repentance is not withheld from anyone; whoever brings about the cause of repentance, God accepts his repentance, for He is {the Accepting of repentance}, meaning He returns to His servants with pardon and forgiveness after sin when they repent, and with goodness and blessings after withholding when they turn back, {the Most Merciful}, who is characterized by a great mercy that encompasses all things. Among His mercy is that He enabled them to repent and turn back in devotion, so they repented and turned back, then He showed them mercy by accepting that from them, out of kindness and generosity. This is the ruling for one who repents from sin.

{161} As for one who disbelieves and persists in his disbelief until he dies, not returning to his Lord, not turning to Him in devotion, and not repenting soon, {upon them is the curse of God, and of the angels, and of people, all together}. Because their disbelief has become a fixed attribute, the curse upon them has become a fixed attribute that does not cease, since the ruling revolves with its cause, existing and non-existing.

{162} {Abiding therein}, meaning: within the curse or within the punishment, and these two are inseparable. {Their punishment will not be lightened}, rather their punishment is constant, severe, and perpetual. {Nor will they be reprieved}, meaning they will not be given respite, because the time of respite, which is this world, has passed, and they have no excuse left to offer.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 163:

{163} He, the Most Truthful of speakers, informs that He is {One God} — meaning unique and alone in His Essence, His Names, His Attributes, and His Actions. He has no partner in His Essence, no namesake, no equal, no like, no peer, and no creator or governor other than Him. Since this is so, He alone deserves to be worshipped (ta'lah) and served with all kinds of worship, and none of His creatures may be associated with Him. He is {the Most Merciful, the Ever-Merciful}, characterized by a great mercy to which no one's mercy is comparable. It has encompassed everything and embraced every living being. By His mercy, creatures came into existence, by His mercy they attained every kind of perfection, and by His mercy every affliction has been repelled from them. By His mercy He made His servants know Himself through His attributes and bounties, and He made clear to them everything they need for the welfare of their religion and their worldly life by sending the messengers and revealing the scriptures. So when one knows that whatever blessing the servants have is from God, and that none of the creatures benefits anyone, one knows that God alone deserves all kinds of worship, and that He should be singled out for love, fear, hope, veneration, reliance upon Him, and the other kinds of obedience. And that among the greatest of injustices and the ugliest of ugly things is to turn away from His worship to the worship of slaves, or to associate with the Lord of lords creatures made of dust, or to worship a created governor who is in every respect powerless, alongside the Creator and Governor, the Capable, the Mighty, who has subdued everything and to whom everything submits.

In this verse there is an affirmation of the Creator's oneness and divinity, and an establishment of it by negating it from others among the creatures, along with an explanation of the root of the evidence for this, namely the affirmation of His mercy, of which the effects are the existence of all blessings and the repelling of all afflictions. This is a general proof of His oneness, may He be exalted.

Then He mentioned the detailed proofs, saying:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 164:

{164} He, may He be exalted, informs that in these great creations there are signs (ayat); that is, proofs of the Creator's oneness (wahdaniyyah), His divinity (ilahiyyah), the greatness of His dominion and mercy, and all His other attributes. But they are {for a people who use their intellects}; that is, for those who have minds that they employ for the purpose for which things were created. According to the measure of intellect that God has bestowed upon His servant, he benefits from the signs and recognizes them through his reason, thought and reflection. In {the creation of the heavens}: in their height, their vastness, their firm construction and perfection, and what God has placed in them of the sun, the moon and the stars, and their arrangement for the benefit of the servants. And in the creation of {the earth}: as a spread-out bed (mihad) for creatures, enabling them to settle upon it, to benefit from what is on it, and to take heed. All of this indicates that God, may He be exalted, alone creates and governs, and demonstrates His great power by which He created it, His wisdom by which He perfected and beautified and ordered it, and His knowledge and mercy by which He deposited what He deposited of benefits for creatures, their welfare, their necessities and their needs. In this is the most eloquent proof of His perfection and of His deserving to be singled out for worship, because He alone creates, governs and manages the affairs of His servants.

In {the alternation of night and day}; namely, their succession constantly, when one departs the other follows it; and in their difference in heat and cold and moderation, and in length and shortness and moderation, and what arises from that of the seasons by which the welfare of the children of Adam and their animals is regulated, and all that is on the surface of the earth of trees and plants, all of it in order, arrangement and subjection that astonishes minds and is beyond the comprehension of the most capable men. All of this indicates the power of the One who directs them, His knowledge, His wisdom, His vast mercy, His all-encompassing kindness, His management and governance which He alone possesses, His greatness and the greatness of His dominion and sovereignty. This necessitates that He be worshipped as God, served, and singled out with love, glorification, fear, hope, and exertion in seeking what He loves and what pleases Him.

In {the ships that run in the sea}, which are boats, vessels and the like, which God inspired His servants to build, and created for them the internal and external instruments that enable them to do so; then He subjected to them this great sea and the winds that carry them, with what is in them of passengers, wealth and merchandise which are of benefit to people and by which their interests are upheld and their livelihoods regulated. So who inspired them to build these, and empowered them to do so, and created for them the tools with which they work? Or who subjected the sea for them, so that they run upon it by His permission and His subjugation, and the winds? Or who created for land and sea vessels the fire and the metals that aid in carrying them and carrying what is in them of wealth? Did these matters happen by chance, or did this weak, incapable creature, who came out of his mother's belly knowing nothing and having no power, independently accomplish them, and then his Lord granted him power and taught him what He willed to teach him? Or is the One who subjects all of this a single, wise, all-knowing Lord, whom nothing can frustrate and nothing can resist? Rather, all things have submitted to His lordship, humbled themselves before His greatness, and yielded to His might.

The ultimate end of the weak servant is that God made him a part of the causes by which these great things came into being. This indicates God's mercy and care for His creation, and it necessitates that all love, fear, hope, complete obedience, humility and glorification be directed to Him alone. {And what God sends down from the sky of water}; namely, the rain descending from the clouds, {and gives life thereby to the earth after its death}; so it brings forth kinds of sustenance and varieties of plants that are necessities of creatures, without which they cannot live. Is this not a proof of the power of the One who sent it down and brought forth by it what He brought forth, and of His mercy, kindness to His servants, His care for their welfare, and their great need and necessity for Him in every respect? Does this not necessitate that He alone be their worshipped one and their God? Is this not a proof of the resurrection of the dead and of their recompense for their deeds?

{And He scattered therein}; that is, in the earth {of every creature}; namely, He spread across the regions of the earth diverse creatures which are a proof of His power, greatness, oneness and mighty sovereignty, and He subjected them to people so that they benefit from them in all ways of benefit: some of them they eat from their flesh and drink from their milk; some they ride; some serve their interests and guard them; and some serve as lessons for them. And among them is that He scattered in it every kind of creature, for He, glorified is He, is the One who sustains their provision and undertakes their sustenance. There is no creature on the earth but that its provision is upon God, and He knows its place of settlement and its place of storage.

In {the changing of the winds}: cold and hot, from the south and the north, from the east and the west (dabur), and between these; and at times they stir up the clouds, at times they gather them together, at times they fertilize them, at times they make them flow with rain, at times they tear them apart and remove their harm; at times they are a mercy, and at times they are sent as punishment. So who directed them in this direction and deposited in them benefits for the servants on which they cannot do without, and subjected them so that all animals may live in them and bodies, trees, grains and plants may be made right, except the Mighty, the Wise, the Merciful, the Gentle toward His servants, who deserves all submission, humility, love, repentance and worship? And in the subjugation of the clouds between heaven and earth, despite their lightness and delicacy, carrying much water, God drives them wherever He wills, giving life thereby to lands and servants, watering the hills and valleys, and sending them down upon creatures at the time of their need. When their abundance would harm them, He withholds it from them; He sends it down as mercy and kindness, and turns it away out of care and tenderness. How great is His dominion, how abundant His goodness, how gentle His bounty! Is it not shameful for servants to enjoy His provision and live by His goodness while using that to aid themselves in displeasing Him and in disobedience to Him? Is this not a proof of His forbearance, patience, pardon, forgiveness and great gentleness? So to Him belongs praise, first and last, outwardly and inwardly.

In summary, whenever the intelligent person reflects upon these creations, and his thought penetrates the marvels of what has been brought into existence, and his contemplation of the craftsmanship and of what has been deposited in it of subtle goodness and wisdom increases, he knows thereby that they were created for truth and by truth, that they are pages of signs and books of proofs for what God has told of Himself, of His oneness, and of what the messengers have reported about the Last Day; and that they are subjected, having no management of their own and no resistance against their Manager and Director. Thus he knows that the higher and lower worlds are all in need of Him, and all depend on Him, and that He is self-sufficient, independent of all creatures. There is no god but God, and no lord besides Him.

Then He, may He be exalted, said:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verses 165–167:

{165 – 166 – 167} How excellent is the connection of this verse with the one before it. For when He, exalted is He, explained His oneness, the decisive proofs for it, and the shining evidence for it, which connect to the knowledge of certainty and remove every doubt, He mentioned here that ﴿among mankind﴾, despite this complete clarification, ﴿there are those who take﴾ creatures ﴿as equals﴾ to God, that is, counterparts and likes who are equal to Him in worship, love, glorification, and obedience.

Whoever is in this state, after the establishment of proof and the explanation of monotheism, is known to be an opponent of God, one who defies Him, or one who turns away from pondering His signs and reflecting on His creation. He has no excuse whatsoever in that, and indeed the word of punishment has become binding upon him. These people who take equals with God do not make them equal to Him in creating, providing, or governing. They only make them equal to Him in worship, so they worship them in order to draw near to Him. In His saying ﴿took﴾ is evidence that God has no equal, and that the polytheists only made some of the creatures equals to Him by mere naming, a word empty of meaning. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they have made partners with God. Say: Name them. Or will you inform Him of what He does not know on earth, or [is it] an outward saying?﴾ And: ﴿They are not but names you have named, you and your fathers, for which God has sent down no authority. They follow only assumption.﴾

So the creature is not an equal to God, because God is the Creator and other than Him is created; the Lord is the Provider and whatever is other than Him is provided for. God is the Self-Sufficient, while you are the poor; He is perfect in every respect, while the servants are deficient in every respect. God is the One who benefits and harms, while the creature has no share in benefit, harm, or command. Thus the falsity of the saying of one who takes, besides God, gods and equals is known with certainty, whether that is a king, a prophet, a righteous person, an idol, or something else. God is the One deserving of complete love and utter humility. Therefore God praised the believers by His saying: ﴿But those who believe are stronger in love for God﴾, that is, than the people of equals are for their equals, because they have made their love sincerely for Him, while these have associated others with it. And because they love the One who truly deserves love, whose love is itself the very righteousness, happiness, and success of the servant. The polytheists love one who does not deserve any love, and whose love is itself the misery, corruption, and dispersal of the servant's affairs.

Therefore God threatened them by His saying: ﴿And if only those who wronged would see﴾, by taking equals and submitting to other than the Lord of the worlds, and who wronged the creation by barring them from the way of God and striving in what harms them, ﴿when they see the punishment﴾, that is, on the Day of Resurrection, directly with their eyes, ﴿that power belongs to God entirely, and that God is severe in punishment﴾, that is, they would know with firm certainty that all power and capability belong to God, and that their equals have no share of power whatsoever. Thus on that Day their weakness and incapacity become clear to them, not as it was confused for them in this world, when they thought that these had some share in the command and that they would bring them near to Him and connect them to Him. Their assumption proved false, their striving came to nothing, the severity of punishment became binding upon them, their equals did not repel anything from them, and they were not made to benefit by even an atom's weight. Rather, harm comes to them from the very things whose benefit they had assumed.

The followers disown those they followed, and the bonds that existed between them in the world are severed, because those bonds were for other than God and not according to God's command, and were attached to falsehood that has no reality. Thus their deeds are rendered void, their conditions dissolve, and it becomes clear to them that they had been liars, and that their deeds, whose benefit and outcome they hoped for, turned against them as regret and remorse, and that they will abide forever in the Fire and never come out of it. So is there, after this loss, any further loss? That is because they followed falsehood, did the false deed, hoped for what was not to be hoped for, and clung to what was not a true object of attachment. Thus deeds were nullified by the nullification of their object, and when they were nullified, regret fell upon them for what they had missed of hope in them, and it harmed them with the utmost harm. This is in contrast to one who has attached himself to God, the King, the Manifest Truth, sincerely made his deed for His sake, and hoped for His benefit. Such a person has placed the truth in its proper place, so his deeds are true because they are attached to the Truth. He attains the result of his deed and finds his reward with his Lord, unending, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those who disbelieved and barred from the way of God, He has sent their deeds astray. And those who believed and did righteous deeds and believed in what was sent down upon Muhammad (ﷺ), and it is the truth from their Lord, He will remove from them their misdeeds and set right their affairs. That is because those who disbelieved followed falsehood, and those who believed followed the truth from their Lord. Thus God presents to people their examples.﴾

At that time the followers will wish to be returned to the world so that they may disown their leaders by abandoning association with God and devoting their deeds sincerely to God. But how far off! The matter has passed, and it is not a time for respite or delay. Moreover, they are liars: even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden. Their words are only a saying they utter and wishes they desire, out of rage and fury against the leaders who disowned them, while the sin is their own. The head of the leaders in evil is Iblis, and yet he says to his followers: ﴿When the matter is decided, indeed God promised you a true promise, and I promised you, but I broke it to you. I had no authority over you except that I called you and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves.﴾

The followers disown those they followed, and the bonds that existed between them in the world are severed, because those bonds were for other than God and not according to God's command, and were attached to falsehood that has no reality. Thus their deeds are rendered void, their conditions dissolve, and it becomes clear to them that they had been liars, and that their deeds, whose benefit and outcome they hoped for, turned against them as regret and remorse, and that they will abide forever in the Fire and never come out of it. So is there, after this loss, any further loss? That is because they followed falsehood, did the false deed, hoped for what was not to be hoped for, and clung to what was not a true object of attachment. Thus deeds were nullified by the nullification of their object, and when they were nullified, regret fell upon them for what they had missed of hope in them, and it harmed them with the utmost harm. This is in contrast to one who has attached himself to God, the King, the Manifest Truth, sincerely made his deed for His sake, and hoped for His benefit. Such a person has placed the truth in its proper place, so his deeds are true because they are attached to the Truth. He attains the result of his deed and finds his reward with his Lord, unending, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those who disbelieved and barred from the way of God, He has sent their deeds astray. And those who believed and did righteous deeds and believed in what was sent down upon Muhammad (ﷺ), and it is the truth from their Lord, He will remove from them their misdeeds and set right their affairs. That is because those who disbelieved followed falsehood, and those who believed followed the truth from their Lord. Thus God presents to people their examples.﴾

At that time the followers will wish to be returned to the world so that they may disown their leaders by abandoning association with God and devoting their deeds sincerely to God. But how far off! The matter has passed, and it is not a time for respite or delay. Moreover, they are liars: even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden. Their words are only a saying they utter and wishes they desire, out of rage and fury against the leaders who disowned them, while the sin is their own. The head of the leaders in evil is Iblis, and yet he says to his followers: ﴿When the matter is decided, indeed God promised you a true promise, and I promised you, but I broke it to you. I had no authority over you except that I called you and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves.﴾

They only make them equal to Him in worship, so they worship them in order to draw near to Him. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 168–170:

{168} This is an address to all people, both believers and disbelievers. He bestows favor upon them by commanding them to eat from everything on the earth of grains, fruits, fruits and animals, being {halal} (lawful); that is, permitted for you to consume, not obtained by usurpation, theft, nor through a forbidden transaction, nor in a forbidden manner, nor by aiding in something forbidden, and {tayyib} (good); that is, not impure (khabith) like carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and all impure things. In this verse there is evidence that the original ruling concerning physical things is permissibility, both in eating and in benefiting from them, and that what is forbidden is of two kinds: either forbidden in itself, which is the impure (khabith), the opposite of the good (tayyib); or forbidden due to an external circumstance, which is what is forbidden because the right of God or the right of His servants is attached to it, and this is the opposite of the lawful (halal).

There is also evidence that eating what sustains the body is obligatory, and whoever abandons it is sinful, based on the apparent sense of the command. And when He commanded them to follow what is beneficial for them, since it is the very essence of their wellbeing, He forbade them from following {khatawat al-shaytan} (the footsteps of Satan); that is, his paths to which he calls, which comprise all sins: disbelief, transgression, and wrongdoing. Included in this is the prohibition of the sawa'ib (free-roaming camels) and the ham (certain beasts) and the like, and included in it [also] is the consumption of forbidden foods.

{Innahu lakum aduwwun mubin} (Indeed, he is a manifest enemy to you); that is, clearly hostile. He desires by his command to you only your deception and that you become among the companions of the blaze. Our Lord did not suffice with forbidding us from following his footsteps until He informed us of this, and He is the most truthful of speakers about his enmity, which calls for caution against him. Then He did not suffice with that until He informed us of the details of what he commands, and that it is the most abominable of things and the greatest in corruption. So He said:

{169} {Innama ya'murukum bil-su'} (He only commands you to evil); that is, the wrong which harms its doer. This includes all sins, and His saying {wal-fahsha'} (and immorality) is by way of mentioning the specific after the general, since fahsha' are those sins whose ugliness is extreme, such as adultery, drinking wine, murder, slander, miserliness, and the like, which whoever has intellect considers abominable. {Wa an taqulu 'alallahi ma la ta'lamun} (and that you say about Allah what you do not know). This includes speaking about Allah without knowledge concerning His law and His decree. Whoever describes Allah with other than what He described Himself with, or what His Messenger described Him with, or negates from Him what He affirmed for Himself, or affirms for Him what He negated from Himself, has spoken about Allah without knowledge. Whoever claims that Allah has rivals (nidd) and idols that bring those who worship them closer to Allah has spoken about Allah without knowledge. Whoever says that Allah has permitted such-and-such, or forbidden such-and-such, or commanded such-and-such, or forbade such-and-such without insight, has spoken about Allah without knowledge. Whoever says that Allah created this category of creatures for such-and-such a reason, without any proof for that, has spoken about Allah without knowledge.

Among the greatest sayings about Allah without knowledge is that an interpreter interprets his own speech or the speech of His Messenger according to meanings agreed upon by a sect of the sects of misguidance, and then says that Allah intended them. Speaking about Allah without knowledge is among the greatest and most comprehensive of prohibitions and among the greatest paths of Satan to which he calls. These are the paths of Satan to which he and his armies call, and they expend their cunning and deception in leading creation astray by whatever they are capable of. As for Allah, He commands justice, excellence, and giving to kinsmen, and forbids immorality, evil, and oppression.

So let the servant examine himself: with which of the two callers is he, and from which of the two parties is he? Will you follow the call of Allah, who desires for you good and the worldly and otherworldly happiness, in whose obedience is all success, in whose service is all triumph, and in whose dealings with the Bestower of apparent and hidden blessings are all profits, who commands only good and forbids only evil? Or will you follow the call of Satan, the enemy of man, who desires evil for you and strives with all his effort to destroy you in this world and the Hereafter, in whose obedience is all evil and in whose guardianship is all loss, who commands only evil and forbids only good?

Then Allah, exalted is He, informs about the state of the polytheists when they are commanded to follow what Allah sent down to His Messenger, of what has been described above: they turn away from that and say:

{170} {Bal nattabi'u ma alfayna 'alayhi aba'ana} (Nay, we follow what we found our fathers upon). So they sufficed themselves with imitating their fathers and shunned faith in the prophets. Yet despite this, their fathers were the most ignorant of people and the most intensely misguided.

This is a feeble pretext to reject the truth, and it is evidence of their turning away from the truth, their aversion to it, and their failure to be fair. Had they been guided to right guidance and sound intention, the truth would have been their aim. Whoever makes the truth his aim, and weighs it against other things, will clearly perceive the truth with certainty and follow it, if he is fair-minded. Then Allah, exalted is He, said:

{171} When Allah the Exalted explained their refusal to submit to what the messengers brought, and their rejection of it through blind imitation (taqlid), it became known that they were neither receptive to the truth nor responsive to it. Indeed, it was known to everyone that they would never abandon their obstinacy. Allah the Exalted informed us that their likeness, when a caller calls them to faith, is like the likeness of the animals to which their shepherd shouts, while they have no understanding of what their caller and summoner says. They hear merely the sound, by which the proof is established against them, but they do not comprehend it with a understanding that benefits them. Therefore they are deaf, not hearing the truth with understanding and acceptance; blind, not looking with reflection (i'tibar); and mute, not speaking what is good for them. The cause that necessitates all of this is that they have no sound intellect; rather, they are the most foolish of the foolish and the most ignorant of the ignorant. Can an intelligent person doubt that one who is called to right guidance, warned away from corruption, forbidden from plunging into punishment, and commanded to do what is good for his welfare, success and bliss, yet disobeys the adviser, turns away from the command of his Lord, plunges into the Fire with open eyes, follows falsehood and casts aside the truth, has no sliver of intellect; and that even if he is characterized by cunning, deceit and shrewdness, he is among the most foolish of fools?

{172} This is a command to the believers specifically, after the general command, because it is they who truly benefit from the commands and prohibitions by virtue of their faith. So He commanded them to eat of the good things of provision and to give thanks to God for His bounty by using them in obedience to Him and by strengthening themselves through them for what leads to Him. Thus He commanded them with what He commanded the Messengers in His saying: ﴿O Messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds﴾. So gratitude in this verse is righteous deeds. Here He did not say "lawful" (halal), because Allah permitted the believer the good things of provision, free of any burden of accountability, and because his faith restrains him from taking what is not his. His saying: ﴿if it is Him you worship﴾ means: so give thanks to Him. This indicates that whoever does not thank God has not worshipped Him alone, just as whoever thanks Him has worshipped Him and carried out what he was commanded. It also indicates that eating what is good is a cause for righteous deeds and for their acceptance.

The command to give thanks follows the bestowal of blessings, because gratitude preserves existing blessings and attracts lost blessings, just as disbelief repels lost blessings and removes existing ones.

{173} When He mentioned the permission of good things, He mentioned the prohibition of foul things, saying: ﴿He has only forbidden you carrion﴾; that is, what dies without lawful slaughter (tadhkiyah shar'iyyah). This is because carrion is foul and harmful in its own nature, and because it is most often the result of illness, and so would add to sickness. The Lawgiver excepted from this generality the carrion of locusts and the fish of the sea, for they are lawful and good. ﴿And blood﴾; that is, flowing blood, as restricted in the other verse. ﴿And that over which the name of other than Allah has been invoked﴾; that is, what is slaughtered for other than Allah, like what is slaughtered for idols and images, whether stones, graves, or the like. This mention is not exhaustive of the prohibited things; it was made to clarify the categories of foul things implied by the implication of His saying: ﴿good things﴾. The generality of prohibited things is derived from the previous verse, His saying: ﴿lawful and good﴾, as has preceded. He forbade us these foul things and their like only out of kindness toward us and to keep us free from what is harmful. Yet, ﴿whoever is compelled﴾; that is, forced to the forbidden by hunger, lack of food, or coercion, ﴿without desiring it﴾; that is, not seeking the forbidden while able to obtain the lawful, or while not hungry, ﴿nor transgressing﴾; that is, exceeding the limit in consuming what was permitted to him out of necessity. So whoever is compelled, being unable to obtain the lawful, and eats only as much as necessity requires, and does not exceed it, ﴿there is no sin upon him﴾; that is, no blame. When sin is lifted, the matter returns to its original state. A person in this condition is commanded to eat, and indeed is forbidden to cast himself into destruction or to kill himself. Therefore it is obligatory for him to eat, and he sins if he abstains from eating until he dies, becoming a killer of himself. This permission and leniency are from His mercy toward His servants, and so He concluded it with these two noble names, which are most fitting to it: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Since permissibility is conditioned on these two conditions, and since a person in this state may not fully investigate their fulfillment, He informed [that He is] Forgiving, so He forgives [him] for what he erred in this particular state, especially since necessity has overcome him and hardship has dulled his senses.

In this verse is evidence for the well-known legal maxim: "necessities permit prohibited things." Thus every prohibited thing to which a person is compelled, the Merciful King has permitted to him. To Him belongs praise and thanks, first and last, outwardly and inwardly.

{173} When He mentioned the permission of good things, He mentioned the prohibition of foul things, saying: ﴿He has only forbidden you carrion﴾; that is, what dies without lawful slaughter (tadhkiyah shar'iyyah). This is because carrion is foul and harmful in its own nature, and because it is most often the result of illness, and so would add to sickness. The Lawgiver excepted from this generality the carrion of locusts and the fish of the sea, for they are lawful and good. ﴿And blood﴾; that is, flowing blood, as restricted in the other verse. ﴿And that over which the name of other than Allah has been invoked﴾; that is, what is slaughtered for other than Allah, like what is slaughtered for idols and images, whether stones, graves, or the like. This mention is not exhaustive of the prohibited things; it was made to clarify the categories of foul things implied by the implication of His saying: ﴿good things﴾. The generality of prohibited things is derived from the previous verse, His saying: ﴿lawful and good﴾, as has preceded. He forbade us these foul things and their like only out of kindness toward us and to keep us free from what is harmful. Yet, ﴿whoever is compelled﴾; that is, forced to the forbidden by hunger, lack of food, or coercion, ﴿without desiring it﴾; that is, not seeking the forbidden while able to obtain the lawful, or while not hungry, ﴿nor transgressing﴾; that is, exceeding the limit in consuming what was permitted to him out of necessity. So whoever is compelled, being unable to obtain the lawful, and eats only as much as necessity requires, and does not exceed it, ﴿there is no sin upon him﴾; that is, no blame. When sin is lifted, the matter returns to its original state. A person in this condition is commanded to eat, and indeed is forbidden to cast himself into destruction or to kill himself. Therefore it is obligatory for him to eat, and he sins if he abstains from eating until he dies, becoming a killer of himself. This permission and leniency are from His mercy toward His servants, and so He concluded it with these two noble names, which are most fitting to it: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Since permissibility is conditioned on these two conditions, and since a person in this state may not fully investigate their fulfillment, He informed [that He is] Forgiving, so He forgives [him] for what he erred in this particular state, especially since necessity has overcome him and hardship has dulled his senses.

In this verse is evidence for the well-known legal maxim: "necessities permit prohibited things." Thus every prohibited thing to which a person is compelled, the Merciful King has permitted to him. To Him belongs praise and thanks, first and last, outwardly and inwardly.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 174–176:

{174–175} This is a severe warning for those who conceal what Allah sent down to His messengers of knowledge, which Allah took a covenant from its people to make clear to the people and not to conceal. Whoever takes in exchange for it the worldly trash and casts aside the command of Allah, those are {they eat nothing into their bellies except the Fire}; because this price they have acquired came to them through the most vile gains and the greatest of forbidden things, so their recompense is of the same kind as their deeds. {And Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection}; rather, He has become displeased with them and turned away from them, and this is greater for them than the torment of the Fire. {Nor will He purify them}; that is, He will not cleanse them from vile character traits, and they have no deeds fit for praise, approval, or reward. Allah did not purify them because they committed the causes of non-purification, the greatest of which is acting upon the Book of Allah, being guided by it, and calling to it. These people cast aside the Book of Allah, turned away from it, and chose error over guidance and punishment over forgiveness. For these, nothing is fitting but the Fire. So how will they endure it? And how will they have the strength to bear it?

{176} {That} refers to what was mentioned, namely recompensing them with justice and withholding the means of guidance from those who refuse it and choose otherwise, {because Allah sent down the Book with truth}. Among truth is recompensing the good-doer for his goodness and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing. Moreover, in His saying {He sent down the Book with truth} is an indication that Allah sent it down to guide His creation and to make clear the truth from falsehood and guidance from error. Whoever turns it away from its purpose deserves to be recompensed with the greatest punishment. {Indeed, those who differ concerning the Book are in far-reaching dissension}; that is, those who differ concerning the Book, believing in part of it and disbelieving in part of it, and those who have distorted it and turned it according to their desires and aims, {are in dissension}; that is, opposition {far} from the truth, because they have contradicted the Book which came with truth, which necessitates agreement and the absence of contradiction. So their affair became confused, their dissension multiplied, and their separation followed from that. This contrasts with the People of the Book who believed in it and judged by it in everything; they agreed, and they enjoyed harmony through love and unity upon it.

These verses contain a warning to those who conceal what Allah has sent down and who prefer the goods of this world over it, with punishment and displeasure, and that Allah will not purify them through success or forgiveness. The reason for this is mentioned: their preference of error over guidance, which results in choosing punishment over forgiveness. Then there is a lament over them for the severity of their patience in the Fire, given their practice of the means which they know lead to it, and that the Book includes truth which necessitates agreement upon it and the absence of division, and that whoever opposes it is at the furthest extreme from truth, contention, and dispute. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 177:

{177} He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿It is not righteousness that you turn your faces toward the east or the west﴾; that is: this is not the righteousness intended from the servants, so that much searching into it and disputation about it would be a toil that yields nothing but discord and disagreement. This is similar to the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The strong man is not the one who overthrows others, but the strong man is the one who controls himself when angry," and the like.

﴿But righteousness is [in] one who believes in Allah﴾; that is: [believes] that He is one God, described by every attribute of perfection, free of every deficiency. ﴿And the Last Day﴾; which is everything Allah has informed of in His Book, or that the Messenger has informed of, of what will occur after death. ﴿And the angels﴾; whom Allah has described to us in His Book and whom His Messenger (ﷺ) described. ﴿And the Book﴾; that is, the category of books that Allah sent down to His messengers, the greatest of which is the Qur'an, so one believes in what it contains of reports and rulings. ﴿And the prophets﴾; in general, and especially their seal and best, Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And gives wealth﴾; which is everything a person possesses as property, whether little or much; that is, he gives wealth ﴿in spite of love for it﴾; that is, love of wealth. By this He shows that wealth is beloved to souls, so a servant hardly parts with it. Whoever gives it while loving it, seeking nearness to Allah, this is a proof of his faith. Among giving wealth in spite of love for it is that one gives charity while healthy and miserly, hoping for riches and fearing poverty. Likewise, if the charity is from little, it is better, because in that state he loves to hold on to it, fearing destitution and poverty. Likewise, giving out the choicest of one's wealth and what one loves of one's property, as Allah, may He be exalted, says: ﴿You will not attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love﴾. All of these are among those who give wealth in spite of their love for it.

Then He mentions the recipients of the spending: they are the people most deserving of your righteousness and kindness, the relatives, whose misfortunes you feel pain for and whose happiness brings you joy, who support one another and share blood-money. Among the best and most fitting righteousness is attending to relatives with financial and verbal kindness according to their closeness and need. And ﴿the orphans﴾, who have no earner and no strength by which they can be self-sufficient. This is from His mercy toward the servants, indicating that He, may He be exalted, is more merciful to them than a father to his child. Allah has enjoined upon the servants and obligated them, regarding their wealth, to show kindness to those whose fathers have died, so that they become like one who has not lost his parents. And because the recompense is of the same kind as the deed: whoever shows mercy to the orphan of another will be shown mercy regarding his own orphan.

﴿And the needy﴾; they are those whom need has made dwell in poverty and whom destitution has humbled. They have a right upon the wealthy to repel their neediness or lessen it, according to what they are able to do and what is easy. ﴿And the wayfarer﴾; he is the stranger cut off from his own land. Allah urged His servants to give him wealth that helps him on his journey, because he is the subject of need and many expenses. So whoever Allah has blessed with a homeland, comfort, and favor from His bounty should show mercy to his brother who is a stranger in this state, according to his ability, even if only by providing him with provisions, or giving him the means for his journey, or paying what befalls him of injustices and other things. ﴿And the beggars﴾; that is, those who face some need that compels asking, such as one afflicted with a compensation for a crime or a tax imposed on him by rulers, or one who asks people to build public benefits such as mosques, schools, bridges, and the like. For such a person there is a right even if he is wealthy. ﴿And in [freeing] slaves﴾; this includes manumission, assisting in it, giving wealth to a mukatab (slave contracted to buy his freedom) so he can pay his master, and ransoming captives held by the disbelievers or by oppressors.

﴿And establishes prayer and gives zakah﴾; it has been mentioned repeatedly that Allah joins prayer and zakah because they are the best of acts of worship and the most complete acts of nearness, being acts of the heart, body, and wealth, and by them faith is weighed and the certainty possessed by its bearer is known. ﴿And those who fulfill their promise when they promise﴾; a promise is a commitment, either by Allah's obligation or by a servant's obligation upon himself. This includes all of Allah's rights, because Allah obligated His servants to them and they committed to them, entered under their responsibility, and it became obligatory upon them to fulfill them; and the rights of the servants that Allah made obligatory upon them, and the rights that the servant has committed to himself, such as oaths and vows and the like.

﴿And the patient in poverty﴾; that is, hardship, because the poor person needs patience in many respects, since he undergoes constant pains of heart and body that others do not. If the wealthy enjoy what he cannot afford, he feels pain; if he or his dependents go hungry, he feels pain; if he eats food that does not suit his taste, he feels pain; if he is naked or nearly so, he feels pain; if he looks at what is before him and imagines the future for which he must prepare, he feels pain; if the cold reaches him and he cannot repel it, he feels pain. All of these and the like are calamities for which he is commanded to be patient, seeking reward and hoping for Allah's recompense. ﴿And in adversity﴾; that is, illness in its various kinds: fever, sores, wind, pain in a limb, even a tooth or a finger, and the like, for it requires patience, because the soul weakens and the body suffers, and that is of extreme hardship to souls, especially when it is prolonged; so he is commanded to be patient, seeking the reward of Allah, may He be exalted. ﴿And during battle﴾; that is, the time of fighting against enemies whom one is commanded to fight, because combat is extremely difficult for the soul, and a person recoils from death, wounds, or capture; so patience is needed in that, seeking and hoping for the reward of Allah, may He be exalted, from which comes victory and the help He promised to the patient.

﴿Those﴾; that is, those characterized by what was mentioned of good beliefs and deeds, which are the effects and proof and light of faith, and the morals that are the beauty of a person and the reality of humanity. ﴿Those are the ones who have been true﴾; in their faith, because their deeds confirmed their faith. ﴿And those are the righteous﴾; because they abandoned what is forbidden and did what is commanded. These matters comprise all kinds of good, implicitly and by necessity, since fulfilling the promise encompasses the whole religion, and the acts of worship mentioned in this verse are the greatest acts of worship, and whoever upholds them is more upright in everything else. So these are the righteous, the truthful, the God-fearing.

It is known what reward Allah has ordained for these three matters, both in this world and in the Hereafter, which cannot be detailed in a place such as this.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 178–179:

{178} Allah, may He be exalted, bestows favor upon His believing servants by making retaliation (qisas) for the slain obligatory upon them; that is, equality in it, and that the killer be killed in the same manner in which he killed the victim, in order to establish justice and fairness among the servants. The address to all believers in it is evidence that it is obligatory upon all of them, including the guardians of the killer, and even the killer himself, to help the guardian of the victim when he seeks retaliation and to enable him to reach the killer. It is not permitted for them to stand between this legal limit and prevent the guardian from exacting retaliation, as was the custom of the Jahiliyyah and those resembling them in sheltering the wrongdoers (al-muhdithin).

Then He explained the details of this, saying: {the free for the free}. By its explicit meaning it includes male for male and female for female, and female for male and male for female. Its explicit wording takes precedence over the implication of His saying "the female for the female," along with the Sunnah's indication that a male is killed for a female. Excluded from the generality of this are parents, however far up they go, who are not killed for their child, because of a Sunnah text to that effect. Also, His saying {retaliation} indicates that it is not just for a father to be killed for his child, and because what is in a father's heart of compassion and mercy prevents him from killing his child, unless there is a severe derangement of his mind or an extremely grave harm inflicted on him by the child. Also excluded from the generality is the disbeliever, by the Sunnah, although the verse is addressed specifically to believers. Furthermore, it is not just for the friend of Allah to be killed by His enemy. {And the slave for the slave}, whether male or female, whether their values are equal or different; and its implication indicates that a free person is not killed for a slave, because he is not equal to him. {And the female for the female}: some scholars took its implication and did not permit killing a man for a woman, and the reason for this has already passed.

In this verse is evidence that the original ruling is the obligation of retaliation for killing, and that the blood-money (diyah) is a substitute for it. Therefore He said: {But if he is granted some remission by his brother}; that is, if the guardian of the victim pardons the killer in favor of blood-money, or some of the guardians pardon, then retaliation is dropped and blood-money becomes obligatory, and the choice between retaliation and accepting blood-money rests with the guardian. When he pardons him, it becomes obligatory upon the guardian, that is, the guardian of the victim, to pursue the killer {with fairness}, without causing him hardship or burdening him with what he cannot bear, but rather by demanding it in a good manner without embarrassing him. And upon the killer, {to pay him with kindness}, without delay, deficiency, or any bad conduct in deed or word. Is there any reward for kindness shown to him by pardon other than kindness in repayment? This is commanded in everything that is established in people's obligations: the one who holds the right is commanded to pursue it fairly, and the one who owes is commanded to pay with kindness. In His saying {from his brother}, there is softening and encouragement toward pardoning in exchange for blood-money, and better than that is pardoning freely.

In His saying {his brother} is evidence that the killer does not become a disbeliever, because the brotherhood meant here is the brotherhood of faith, and he is not removed from it by the killing. Still less do other sins that fall short of disbelief make their doer a disbeliever; rather, his faith is diminished thereby. When the guardians of the victim, or some of them, pardon, the killer's blood is protected and becomes inviolable from them and from others. Therefore He said: {Whoever transgresses after that}; that is, after the pardon, {for him is a painful punishment}; that is, in the Hereafter. As for his being killed or not, it is derived from what has passed, because he killed one equal to him, so he must be killed for that. As for those who interpreted the painful punishment as killing, and that the verse indicates that his killing is required and pardoning him is not permitted, some scholars said this, but the correct view is the first, because his crime does not exceed the crime of others.

Then Allah, may He be exalted, explained His great wisdom in legislating retaliation, saying:

{179} {And for you in retaliation is life}; that is, blood is protected by it and wretched people are restrained by it, because whoever knows that he will be killed if he kills hardly commits murder, and when a killer is seen being killed, others are terrified and restrained. Had the punishment for the killer been other than death, the prevention of evil achieved by killing would not have been achieved. Likewise, all the legal prescribed punishments contain such deterrence and restraint as indicate the wisdom of the All-Wise, the Ever-Forgiving. The word "life" is indefinite to indicate magnitude and abundance. Since this ruling is not truly understood except by people of complete intellects and sound minds, He addressed them specifically rather than others, and this indicates that Allah, may He be exalted, loves for His servants to employ their thoughts and minds in reflecting on the wisdoms and benefits contained in His rulings, which indicate His perfection, the perfection of His wisdom, His praiseworthiness, His justice, and His vast mercy. Whoever is in this position deserves praise as being among the people of understanding (ulul-albab) to whom the address was directed and whom the Lord of lords called, and that is sufficient honor and nobility for "a people who reason."

His saying {so that you may become righteous} means that whoever knows his Lord and knows what is in His religion and legislation of great secrets, wondrous wisdoms, and sublime signs, this necessarily makes him submit to the command of Allah, magnify His prohibitions, and abandon them; thereby he deserves to be among the righteous (al-muttaqun).

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 180–182:

{180} That is: Allah has prescribed for you, O company of believers, {when death approaches one of you}; that is, its causes, such as an illness bringing one close to destruction and the presence of the causes of perils. And if he has left {wealth}, which is abundant wealth by common custom, then he must make a bequest to his parents and nearest relatives {in kindness}, in an amount according to his means, without extravagance and without restricting it to the more distant at the expense of the nearer, but rather ordering them according to closeness and need. For this reason the comparative form (af'al al-tafdil) is used in it. His saying {a duty upon the mindful} indicates that this is obligatory, because the haqq (duty/right) is that which is established, and Allah has made it one of the requirements of taqwa (God-consciousness).

Know that the majority of the exegetes hold that this verse has been abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of inheritance (ayat al-mawarith). Some of them hold that it concerns the parents and the relatives who do not inherit, though no evidence has indicated that it is restricted to that. The best view on this is to say that this bequest to parents and relatives is general (mujmal), which Allah the Exalted referred back to the customary practice in force. Then Allah the Exalted specified this customary practice for the parents and relatives who do inherit, and other relatives who inherit, in the verses of inheritance, after it had been general. The ruling remains for those parents and relatives who do not inherit, because they are barred from inheritance, and for others who have been excluded by a person or by a characteristic. A person is commanded to make a bequest to these, and they are the people most entitled to his kindness. Since the testator may refrain from bequeathing out of fear that whoever comes after him might change what he has bequeathed, Allah the Exalted said:

{181–182} {So whoever alters it}; that is, alters the bequest to those mentioned or others, {after he has heard it}; that is, after he has understood it, known its procedures and its execution, {then its sin is only upon those who alter it}. Otherwise, the testator's reward has fallen upon Allah, and the sin lies only upon the one who changes and alters it. {Indeed, Allah is Hearing}; He hears all voices, and among that is His hearing the testator's speech and his bequest. Therefore he should be mindful of who hears and sees him and not act unjustly in his bequest. {Knowing}; of his intention and knowing of the deed of the one to whom the bequest is made. So if the testator strives and Allah knows of him that intention, He rewards him even if he errs. And in it is a warning to the one to whom the bequest is made against altering it, for Allah knows of it and is aware of what he has done, so let him beware of Allah. This is the ruling for a just bequest. As for a bequest in which there is injustice (haif), deviation (janf) and sin, then whoever is present with the testator at the time of the bequest should advise him toward what is best and most just, and forbid him from injustice and deviation, which is inclining the bequest away from it by error without intent, and sin, which is doing so deliberately. If he does not do that, then he should work to reconcile the beneficiaries and reach justice among them by way of mutual consent and conciliation, and admonish them to clear the liability of their deceased. Such a person has done a great good and bears no sin as the one who alters a permissible bequest bears. For this reason He said: {Indeed, Allah is Forgiving}; that is, He forgives all faults and pardons obligations toward those who repent to Him, and among that is His forgiveness of one who sets aside some of his own right and forgoes part of his right for his brother, for whoever is lenient, Allah is lenient with him. {Forgiving} of their deceased who was unjust in his bequest, when they seek reward by forgiving one another for the sake of clearing his liability. {Merciful}; to His servants, in that He legislated for them every matter by which they show mercy and compassion to one another.

Thus these verses indicate encouragement to make a bequest, clarify to whom it is due, warn against altering a just bequest, and encourage reconciliation in an unjust bequest.
