{183} He, exalted is He, informs of the favor Allah has bestowed upon His servants: He has prescribed fasting for them, as He prescribed it for the earlier nations, because it is among the laws and commands that serve the interests of creation in every age. It also encourages this nation, meaning that you should compete with others in perfecting deeds and hastening to good qualities, and that fasting is not one of the burdens peculiar to others that you have been singled out for.

Then He mentioned His wisdom in prescribing fasting, saying: ﴿So that you may become righteous﴾. Fasting is among the greatest causes of taqwa (God-consciousness), because it involves carrying out Allah's command and avoiding His prohibition. Among the forms of taqwa it contains is that the fasting person abstains from what Allah has forbidden him, such as eating, drinking, intercourse and the like, which the soul inclines toward, seeking nearness to Allah by this and hoping for His reward through abandoning them. This is taqwa. Another is that the fasting person trains himself to be mindful of Allah, abandoning what his soul desires while he is able to obtain it, because he knows that Allah sees him. Another is that fasting constricts the channels of Satan, for he runs through the son of Adam as blood runs, so by fasting his influence weakens and sins decrease from him. Another is that the fasting person, in most cases, increases in obedience, and acts of obedience are among the qualities of taqwa. Another is that when the wealthy person tastes the pain of hunger, this makes him sympathize with the destitute poor. This too is among the qualities of taqwa.

{184} When He mentioned that He had prescribed fasting for them, He informed that it is ﴿a certain number of days﴾, meaning few, and extremely easy. Then He eased it further by saying: ﴿So whoever among you is ill or on a journey, then [an equal number] of other days﴾. Because hardship usually accompanies these two states, Allah granted them permission to break the fast. Since every believer must still obtain the benefit of fasting, He commanded them to make it up on other days when the illness ends, the journey is over, and they have rest. In His saying ﴿a number of other days﴾ there is evidence that one makes up the number of Ramadan days, whether the month was complete or incomplete, and that it is permissible to make up short cool days in place of long hot days, and the reverse. His saying ﴿And for those who are able to [fast] it﴾, meaning those who are able to fast, ﴿a ransom﴾ for each day they break the fast, ﴿[is] the feeding of a poor person﴾. This was at the beginning of the prescription of fasting, when they were not accustomed to fasting and it was obligatory, which involved hardship for them. The Wise Lord eased it for them by the easiest way. He gave the one who was able to fast the choice between fasting, which is better, and feeding [a poor person]. This is why He said: ﴿And that you fast is better for you﴾. Then after that He made fasting obligatory upon the one able to fast, while the one unable to fast breaks it and makes it up on other days. It has also been said that the meaning of ﴿those who are able to [fast] it﴾ is those who strain to do it, and for whom it is an unbearable hardship, such as the very old man; for him [the requirement is] a ransom of one poor person for each day. This is the sound opinion.

{185} ﴿The month of Ramadan [is that] in which the Qur'an was revealed﴾, meaning: the fasting prescribed for you is the month of Ramadan, the great month in which Allah has bestowed upon you great favor, namely the noble Qur'an, which contains guidance for your religious and worldly interests, a clarification of the truth with the clearest explanation, and a criterion (furqan) between truth and falsehood, guidance and misguidance, and the people of happiness and the people of misery. This month, with such virtue, and this favor of Allah upon you in it, is deserving that it be a season for the servants, in which fasting is made obligatory. When He established it, explained its excellence and the wisdom of Allah in singling it out, He said: ﴿So whoever of you witnesses the month, let him fast it﴾. This contains the specification of fasting upon the one who is able, healthy and present. Since the abrogation applied only to the choice between fasting and the ransom, He restated the concession for the ill person and the traveler, lest it be supposed that the concession was also abrogated, so He said: ﴿Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship﴾, meaning: Allah, exalted is He, intends to make the paths that lead to His good pleasure easy for you in the greatest ease, and to facilitate them in the most complete manner. This is why all that Allah has commanded His servants is extremely easy in its origin, and when some circumstances arise that make it burdensome, He eases it further, either by dropping it or lightening it through various kinds of concessions. This is a general principle that cannot be detailed, since its details comprise all the legal rulings (shar'iyyat) and include all the concessions and facilitations.

﴿And that you complete the period﴾. This, and Allah knows best, is so that no one supposes that the purpose of fasting Ramadan is achieved by only part of it. This supposition is removed by the command to complete its number, and by giving thanks to Allah, exalted is He, upon completing it for His granting success, facilitating it, and making it clear to His servants, and by glorifying Him (takbir) upon its conclusion. This includes glorifying Allah when the crescent of Shawwal is sighted until the end of the Eid sermon.

{186} This is an answer to a question. Some of his Companions asked the Prophet ﷺ, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, is our Lord near so that we may whisper to Him, or is He far so that we must call out to Him?"

So the verse was revealed: ﴿And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near﴾. For He, exalted is He, is the Watchful, the Witness, who knows the secret and what is more hidden, who knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal. Thus He is also near to the one who calls upon Him, by answering him. For this reason He said: ﴿I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me﴾. Supplication is of two kinds: the supplication of worship (du'a al-'ibadah) and the supplication of request (du'a al-mas'alah).

Nearness is of two kinds: nearness by His knowledge to all of His creation, and nearness to those who worship Him and call upon Him, by answering, aiding, and granting success.

So whoever calls upon his Lord with a present heart and a lawful supplication, and no obstacle prevents the answer to the supplication, such as eating what is unlawful and the like, then Allah has indeed promised him an answer. This is especially so if he brings the means of having his supplication answered, which are responding to Allah, the Exalted, by submitting to His commands and prohibitions, both verbal and practical, and faith in Him, which necessitates the response. For this reason He said: ﴿So let them respond to Me and believe in Me, that they may be guided﴾; that is, that there may be attained for them the right guidance (rushd), which is the guidance to faith and righteous deeds, and that the misguidance (ghayy) which contradicts faith and righteous deeds may be removed from them. Moreover, faith in Allah and responding to His command is a cause for the attainment of knowledge, as the Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, if you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion (furqan)﴾. Then the Exalted said:

{187} At the beginning of the obligation of fasting, eating, drinking and sexual intercourse were forbidden to the Muslims during the night after sleep. Hardship befell some of them, so God Most High lightened this for them and permitted eating, drinking and sexual intercourse throughout all the nights of fasting, whether one had slept or not, because they had been betraying themselves by neglecting some of what they had been commanded. {So He turned} toward {you} in mercy, by widening for you a matter which, had He not widened it, would have been a cause of sin, {and pardoned you} for what had passed of such betrayal. {So now} after this concession and ease from God, {lie with them} in intercourse, touching and whatever else is included, {and seek what God has prescribed for you}. That is: intend, in your intimacy with your wives, nearness to God Most High, and the greatest purpose of intercourse, namely the begetting of offspring, preserving your chastity and that of your wives, and attaining the aims of marriage, and [seek] what God has prescribed for you, the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr) which coincides with the nights of the fast of Ramadan. So it is not fitting for you to busy yourselves with this pleasure to the neglect of that night and to lose it, for pleasure is always attainable, whereas if the Night of Decree passes, it cannot be recovered.
{And eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of dawn}. This is the limit for eating, drinking and intercourse. It indicates that if one eats or does the like while doubtful about the rising of dawn, there is no blame upon him. It also indicates the recommendation of suhur (the pre-dawn meal), by the command, and that it is recommended to delay it, drawing from the meaning of God's concession and facilitation for His servants. It also indicates that it is permissible for a person to be overtaken by dawn while in a state of janabah (ritual impurity) from intercourse before performing the ghusl, and his fast is valid, because the necessary implication of permitting intercourse until dawn is that dawn may overtake him in a state of janabah, and what is necessary for the truth is itself true. {Then} when dawn has risen, {complete the fast} – that is, abstention from the things that break the fast – {until the night}, which is the setting of the sun. Since the permission of intercourse during the nights of fasting is not a general permission for everyone, the one in i'tikaf is excluded from it, so He said: {and do not lie with them while you are devoting yourselves to i'tikaf in the mosques}. That is: while you are characterized by that state.
The verse indicates the legislation of i'tikaf, which is remaining in the mosque for the sake of obeying God Most High and devoting oneself to Him, and that i'tikaf is valid only in a mosque. It is understood from the definite article on "the mosques" that these are the well-known mosques, namely those where the five daily prayers are established. It also indicates that intercourse invalidates i'tikaf.
{Those are the limits of God}: those mentioned, namely the prohibition of eating, drinking and intercourse and the like of what breaks the fast during fasting, the prohibition of breaking the fast for one without a valid excuse, the prohibition of intercourse for the one in i'tikaf, and the like of prohibited matters, {which God has set as limits for His servants and forbade them, so He said: {do not approach them}}. This is more emphatic than His saying "do not do them", because approaching ("qurban") includes prohibition of doing the forbidden act itself and prohibition of the means that lead to it.
The servant is commanded to abandon what is forbidden and to keep as far from it as he can, and to abandon every cause that calls to it. As for the commands, God says regarding them: {Those are the limits of God, so do not transgress them}, thereby forbidding crossing over them. {Thus} – that is, God has made clear to His servants the previous rulings in the most complete and clearest explanation {God makes His signs clear to people that they may be righteous} – for when the truth becomes evident to them they follow it, and when falsehood becomes evident to them they avoid it. A person may commit a prohibited act out of ignorance that it is prohibited, and had he known its prohibition he would not have done it; so when God makes His signs clear to people, they have no excuse or argument left, and this becomes a cause of taqwa (God-consciousness).

{188} That is: "And do not consume your wealth [amwalakum] among yourselves by false means" — meaning, do not take one another's wealth. He attributed it to them (as "your wealth") because a Muslim should love for his brother what he loves for himself, and should respect his brother's property as he respects his own. Also, consuming another's property emboldens others to consume his property when they are able to do so. Since consuming wealth is of two kinds, one by right (bi-haqq) and one by falsehood (bi-batil), and what is forbidden is only consuming it by falsehood, Allah, exalted is He, restricted it with that qualifier. Included in this is consuming it by way of usurpation (ghasb), theft (sariqah), and breach of trust in a deposit (wadi'ah), a loan (ariyah), or the like. Also included is taking it through a forbidden exchange (mu'awadah muharramah), such as all contracts of usury (riba) and gambling (qimar), for these are consuming wealth by falsehood, since they are not in return for a permissible consideration. Included as well is taking it by means of deception (ghish) in buying, selling, leasing, and the like. Included too is employing workers and consuming their wages, as well as taking a wage for work they have not performed its obligations in. Included also is taking a wage for acts of worship and devotional acts that are not valid unless performed seeking the Face of Allah, exalted is He. Included in this is taking from zakat, charitable endowments (sadaqat), awqaf (endowments), and bequests (wasaya) by one who has no right to them or who takes more than his right. All of this and the like is consuming wealth by falsehood, and it is not permissible in any way, even if a dispute arises over it and the matter is brought before a judge of the Shari'ah, and the one who wants to consume it by falsehood presents a proof that overcomes the proof of the one who is in the right, and the judge rules in his favor. For the ruling of a judge does not make lawful what is unlawful, nor render permissible what is forbidden; he only judges according to what is heard, and otherwise the realities of matters remain as they are. Thus there is no comfort, no legitimacy, and no ease in the judge's ruling for the wrongdoer. Whoever presents a false proof to the judge and is ruled in his favor by it, it is not lawful for him, and he is one who consumes another's wealth by falsehood and sin, knowing this, so his punishment is more severe and his retribution more grievous.

Based on this: if an agent (wakil) knows that his principal (muwakkil) is in the wrong in his claim, it is not lawful for him to dispute on behalf of the treacherous one, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And do not be an advocate for the treacherous.﴾

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 189:

{189} Then His saying, Exalted is He: {They ask you about the new moons}; (the plural of hilal (crescent)): what is their benefit and wisdom, or about their essence? {Say: They are times (mawaqit) for the people}; i.e., Allah, Exalted is He, by His kindness and mercy, ordained this arrangement: the crescent appears weak at the beginning of the month, then grows until it reaches half, then begins to wane until it is complete, and so on. Thus people know by it the appointed times of their acts of worship: fasting, the times of zakat and expiations (kaffarat), and the times of Hajj. Since Hajj takes place in known months and extends over many days, He said: {and the Hajj}. Likewise, by it are known the times of deferred debts, the duration of leases, the period of the waiting time ('iddah) and of pregnancy, and other things that are among the needs of creation. He, Exalted is He, made it a reckoning that everyone knows, young and old, scholar and ignorant. Had the reckoning been by the solar year, only the rare few among people would have known it.
{It is not righteousness that you enter the houses from their backs}; This is what the Ansar and other Arabs used to do: when they entered the state of ihram, they would not enter the houses through their doors, as an act of worship and thinking it to be righteousness. So Allah, Exalted is He, informed them that it is not part of righteousness, because Allah did not prescribe it for them. Whoever worships by an act that Allah and His Messenger did not prescribe is worshipping by an innovation (bid'ah). He commanded them to enter the houses through their doors, because of the ease it brings them, which is one of the principles of the Sharia.
It may be derived from the indication of the verse that in every matter a person should approach it by the easy, near path that has been made to lead to it. So the one who enjoins good and forbids evil should consider the condition of the one he addresses and employ with him gentleness and wise policy by which the aim, or part of it, is achieved. The student and the teacher should take the nearest and easiest path by which their goal is attained. Likewise, whoever attempts any matter, approaches it through its doors, and persists in it, will surely attain the goal by the help of the Sovereign, the Worshipped One.
{And fear Allah}; this is the righteousness that Allah has commanded: it is to hold firmly to His taqwa at all times, by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, for it is the cause of success (falah), which is attaining what is sought and being saved from what is feared. Whoever does not fear Allah, Exalted is He, has no path to success, and whoever fears Him attains success and triumph.

{190} These verses contain the command to fight in the way of Allah. This was after the Hijrah to Madinah; when the Muslims became strong enough to fight, Allah commanded them to do so, after they had been commanded to restrain their hands. In specifying fighting "in the way of Allah," there is an exhortation to sincerity and a prohibition against fighting among the Muslims in civil strife. "Those who fight you" means: those who are prepared to fight you, and they are the men who are legally responsible (mukallaf), not the elderly who have no opinion and do not fight. The prohibition of aggression includes all kinds of aggression: killing those who do not fight, such as women, the insane, children, monks and the like; mutilating the slain; killing animals; and cutting down trees and the like, without a benefit accruing to the Muslims. Among aggression is also fighting those from whom the jizyah (poll tax) is accepted, if they have offered it; this is not permissible.

{191–192} "And kill them wherever you encounter them." This is a command to fight them wherever they are found, at all times and in every era, both defensive fighting and offensive fighting. Then He excepted from this generality fighting them "at al-Masjid al-Haram" (the Sacred Mosque), and that it is not permissible unless they begin the fighting, in which case they are fought as a requital for their aggression. This continues at all times until they cease their disbelief and submit to Islam, for Allah accepts their repentance, even though what has occurred from them of disbelief in Allah and polytheism in the Sacred Mosque and their obstruction of the Messenger and the believers from it. This is from His mercy and generosity toward His servants. Since fighting at the Sacred Mosque might be imagined to be a corruption in this sacred city, Allah, exalted is He, informed that the corruption of strife (fitnah) by polytheism and obstruction from His religion there is worse than the corruption of killing; so there is no blame upon you, O Muslims, in fighting them. This verse is cited as evidence for the well-known principle that one bears the lesser of two harms to avert the greater of them.

{193} Then He mentioned the purpose of fighting in His way: that its purpose is not the shedding of the blood of disbelievers or the seizing of their property, but rather that "religion be for Allah," exalted is He, so that the religion of Allah is made to prevail over all other religions, and every opposition to it, such as polytheism and other things, is repelled; and this is what is meant by fitnah. When this purpose is achieved, there is no killing and no fighting. "And if they desist" means: from fighting you at al-Masjid al-Haram, "then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers," meaning: there is no aggression upon them from you except against those among them who commit wrongdoing; for such a person deserves punishment in proportion to his wrongdoing.

{194} He, exalted is He, says: {The sacred month for the sacred month}.

It is possible that what is meant is the obstruction by the polytheists of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions in the year of al-Hudaybiyah from entering Makkah, and their agreement with them to enter it the following year. The obstruction and the agreement took place in a sacred month, which is Dhu al-Qa'dah, so this is {for} that. In it there is consolation for the hearts of the Companions regarding the completion and perfection of their rites (nusuk). It is also possible that the meaning is: if you fight them in the sacred month, they have already fought you in it, and they are the aggressors, so there is no blame upon you in that. On this interpretation, His saying {and sacred things are subject to retaliation} is a case of the general being joined to the specific (ʿatf al-ʿamm ʿala al-khass), meaning: everything that is to be respected, whether a sacred month, a sacred land, or a state of ihram, or what is more general than that, all that the Shariah has commanded to be respected. Whoever violates them is retaliated against. Whoever fights in the sacred month is fought; whoever violates the sacred land is subjected to the prescribed penalty (hadd), and it has no sanctity for him; whoever kills an equal is killed for it; whoever wounds another or cuts off a limb of his is subjected to retaliation (qisas); and whoever takes the property of another that is protected, he is made to restore its equivalent. However, is it permissible for the rightful owner to take from the property of the wrongdoer an amount equal to his right or not? There is disagreement among the scholars. The preferred view on this is that if the cause of the right is apparent, such as a guest whom no one else hosts, or a wife or relative whose maintenance is obligatory upon a person who refuses to provide for them, then it is permissible to take from his property. But if the cause is hidden, such as one who denies another's debt, or betrays him regarding a deposit, or steals from him and the like, then it is not permissible for him to take from the wrongdoer's property as recompense, in harmonizing the evidences. Therefore, God, exalted is He, said, emphasizing and reinforcing what preceded: {So whoever has aggressed against you, then aggress against him in the same way as he has aggressed against you}. This is an explanation of the nature of retaliation (muqasah), that it is equality in response to the aggressor.

And since souls, generally, do not stop at its limit when permission is given to them for retaliation, because they seek to satisfy their vengeance, God, exalted is He, commanded them to adhere to His piety (taqwa), which is standing at His limits and not transgressing them, and He informed that He is {with the righteous}, meaning: with help, victory, support and success. Whoever God is with attains eternal happiness. Whoever does not adhere to piety, his protector forsakes him, and He leaves him to himself, so his destruction becomes closer to him than the jugular vein.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 195:

{195} God commands His servants to spend in His cause, which means expending wealth on the paths that lead to God. These are all the paths of goodness: giving charity to a needy person or a relative, or spending on those whose maintenance is obligatory. The greatest of these, and the first to enter this category, is spending in jihad for the cause of God, for spending in it is jihad with wealth, and it is an obligation just as jihad with the body is. Among its great benefits is that it helps strengthen the Muslims, weakens shirk (polytheism) and its adherents, and establishes the religion of God and exalts it. Jihad in the cause of God can only stand upon the leg of spending; spending for it is like the spirit, whose existence is impossible without it. Abandoning spending in the cause of God means nullifying jihad, giving power over the enemies, and intensifying their assault. Therefore, His saying, ﴿And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾, serves as the reason for this.

Throwing oneself into destruction returns to two matters: abandoning what a servant has been commanded to do, when abandoning it causes or nearly causes the destruction of the body or the spirit; and doing what is a means leading to the loss of the self or the spirit. Many things fall under this. Among them is abandoning jihad in the cause of God, or abandoning spending in it, which leads to the domination of the enemies. Among them is a person exposing himself to danger in battle, or on a dangerous journey, or in a place where there are wild beasts or snakes, or climbing a tree or a perilous building, or entering something hazardous, and the like. Whoever does these things or similar ones has thrown himself with his own hands into destruction. Among them also is persisting in the disobedience of God and despairing of repentance, and among them is abandoning the obligatory duties God has commanded, the abandonment of which is destruction for the spirit and the religion.

Since spending in the cause of God is a kind of excellence (ihsan), He commanded excellence in general, saying: ﴿And do good; indeed, God loves the good-doers﴾. This encompasses all kinds of excellence, since He did not restrict it to anything in particular. It includes excellence with wealth, as previously mentioned; it includes excellence with one's standing, through intercession and the like; and it includes enjoining what is good and forbidding what is evil, and teaching beneficial knowledge. It also includes meeting the needs of people, relieving their distresses, removing their hardships, visiting their sick, following their funeral processions, guiding those who have gone astray, helping one who is working, and working for one who cannot work well, and the like, which is part of the excellence God has commanded. Excellence also includes excellence in the worship of God, as the Prophet (ﷺ) described it: "That you worship God as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, indeed He sees you." Whoever is characterized by these qualities is among those of whom God said: ﴿For those who have done good is the best [reward] and an increase﴾, and God will be with him, guiding him, directing him, and helping him in all his affairs.

When God finished mentioning the rulings of fasting and jihad, He mentioned the rulings of Hajj, saying:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 196:

{196} From His saying, ﴿And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah﴾, it is deduced that: First, the Hajj and the 'Umrah are obligatory and mandatory. Second, their completion is obligatory with their pillars and obligatory acts, which are indicated by the action of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his saying: "Take your rites from me." Third, this is evidence for those who hold that the 'Umrah is obligatory. Fourth, the Hajj and 'Umrah must be completed once one has begun them, even if they are voluntary. Fifth, the command to perfect them and do them well, which is an addition beyond performing what is required for them. Sixth, it contains the command to make them sincerely ﴿for Allah﴾, the Exalted. Seventh, the one who is in the state of ihram for them may not exit it by anything until he completes them, except for what Allah has excepted, which is the obstruction (ihsar). Therefore He said: ﴿But if you are prevented﴾; that is, you are prevented from reaching the House from completing them, by illness, an injury, or an enemy, and the like of the kinds of obstruction, which is prevention. ﴿Then what is feasible of offering﴾; that is, slaughter what is feasible of offering, which is a sheep, or a cow, or a camel, that the one who is obstructed slaughters; he shaves his head and exits his ihram because of the obstruction, as the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions did when the polytheists prevented them in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah. If he does not find an offering, then he should fast ten days instead, as with the tamattu' pilgrim, and then he exits ihram.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And do not shave your heads until the offering reaches its place﴾. This is among the prohibitions of ihram: removing hair, by shaving or otherwise, because the meaning is the same whether it is from the head or from the body, since the purpose of this is the occurrence of disheveledness and the prevention of indulgence by removing it, and this is present in the rest of the hair. Many scholars analogized the trimming of nails to the removal of hair, by the common factor of indulgence. The prohibition of the above continues until the offering reaches its place, which is the Day of Sacrifice (yawm al-nahr). It is best that the shaving be after the sacrifice, as the verse indicates.

This verse is used as evidence that the tamattu' pilgrim who brings an offering does not exit from his 'Umrah before the Day of Sacrifice. So when he has circumambulated and performed sa'y for the 'Umrah, he enters ihram for Hajj, and there is no exit for him because of bringing the offering. Allah, blessed and exalted, only prohibited this because of what it contains of humility, submission to Allah, brokenness before Him, and modesty, which is the very benefit of the servant. There is no harm for him in this. But if harm occurs, such as if he has an affliction from illness, for which shaving his head benefits him, or sores, or lice, and the like, then it is permissible for him to shave his head, but he must pay a ransom (fidyah): either fasting three days, or feeding six needy persons, or sacrificing an offering that is sufficient for a sacrificial animal. He may choose, and sacrifice is best, then charity, then fasting. Similarly, everything that is in the same sense as this, such as trimming nails, covering the head, wearing sewn garments, or using perfume, is permissible in cases of necessity, with the aforementioned ransom obligatory, because the purpose of all of these is the removal of that by which one indulges.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So when you are secure﴾; that is, when you are able to reach the House without an enemy or other obstacle. ﴿Then whoever enjoys [the benefit of] 'Umrah until Hajj﴾; by connecting it to it, and benefiting from his enjoyment after finishing it. ﴿Then what is feasible of offering﴾; that is, upon him is what is feasible of offering, which is what is sufficient for a sacrificial animal. This is a blood sacrifice of worship in exchange for his acquiring both rites in a single journey, and as a blessing from Allah upon him in obtaining the benefit of tamattu' after finishing the 'Umrah and before beginning the Hajj. Similar to it is the qiran, for his acquiring both rites. The implication of the verse indicates that the one performing only Hajj (ifrad) has no offering upon him. The verse indicates the permissibility, indeed the virtue, of tamattu', and its permissibility during the months of Hajj. ﴿But whoever does not find﴾; that is, the offering or its price, ﴿then [he must fast] three days during Hajj﴾; its beginning is permissible from the time of entering ihram for 'Umrah, and its end is three days after the sacrifice, the days of stoning the pillars and staying overnight in Mina. But the better of them is that he fast on the seventh, eighth, and ninth. ﴿And seven when you return﴾; that is, when you have finished the acts of Hajj. It is permissible to perform them in Makkah, on the way, and upon reaching his family. This is the aforementioned obligation of the offering upon the tamattu' pilgrim ﴿for one whose family is not present at al-Masjid al-Haram﴾; that is, who is at a distance of a shortened journey or more, or who is far from it by custom. This is the one upon whom the offering is obligatory, because he acquires both rites in a single journey. As for one whose family is present at al-Masjid al-Haram, there is no offering upon him, since there is no cause for it.

﴿And fear Allah﴾; that is, in all your affairs, by complying with His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, and among that is your compliance with these commanded acts and avoidance of these prohibited matters mentioned in this verse. ﴿And know that Allah is severe in penalty﴾; that is, to whoever disobeys Him. This is what necessitates piety, for whoever fears the punishment of Allah refrains from what necessitates punishment, just as whoever hopes for the reward of Allah acts toward what leads him to reward. As for one who does not fear punishment and does not hope for reward, he rushes into the prohibitions and boldly abandons the obligations.

{197} He, exalted is He, informs that Hajj (the pilgrimage) takes place in {well-known months}, which are famous among those addressed, such that they need no specification—just as fasting needed its month to be specified, and just as He, exalted is He, explained the times of the five prayers. As for Hajj, it was part of the creed of Ibrahim (Abraham), which continued uninterrupted among his descendants and was known among them. The {well-known months} are, according to the majority of scholars, Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah, for these are the months in which entering the state of ihram for Hajj usually occurs. {Whoever undertakes Hajj therein}; that is, enters into ihram for it, because beginning it makes it obligatory (fard), even if it was a voluntary (nafl) act.

Al-Shafi'i and those who follow him derived from this verse that it is not permissible to enter into ihram for Hajj before its months. I say: If it were said that the verse contains an indication in favor of the majority's view that entering into ihram for Hajj before its months is valid, that would be close to the truth, for His saying {whoever undertakes Hajj therein} is evidence that the obligation may occur within the mentioned months and may not occur in them; otherwise He would not have restricted it. His saying {there shall be no obscenity, nor wickedness, nor disputing during Hajj} means: you must honor the ihram for Hajj, especially when it occurs during its months, and guard it against everything that spoils or diminishes it, namely obscenity (rafath), which is sexual intercourse and its preliminaries, both physical and verbal, especially in the presence of women; wickedness (fusuq), which is all acts of disobedience, including the prohibitions of ihram; and disputing (jidal), which is contention, quarreling, and hostile argument, because these stir up evil and provoke enmity. The purpose of Hajj is humility and submission before Allah and drawing near to Him through as many acts of devotion as possible, and keeping oneself free from committing evil deeds, for by this it becomes an accepted (mabrur) pilgrimage, and the reward of the accepted pilgrimage is nothing but Paradise. Although these things are forbidden in every place and time, the prohibition against them is made more severe during Hajj.

Know that drawing near to Allah through abandoning sins is not complete until one performs the commands. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: {And whatever good you do, Allah knows it}; He used "min" (whatever) to make the generality explicit, so every good deed, act of devotion, and worship is included in this, meaning that Allah has knowledge of it. This contains the utmost encouragement toward good deeds, especially in those noble places and sacred precincts, for one should make up, as far as possible, whatever can be made up there of prayer, fasting, charity, circumambulation, and good conduct in speech and action. Then He, exalted is He, commanded provisioning oneself for this blessed journey; for provisioning oneself in it means independence from created beings and refraining from their wealth, through asking and eagerly looking to them. Increasing it is beneficial and helps travelers, and increases nearness to the Lord of the worlds. This provision, which is intended to establish the body, is a sustenance and enjoyment. As for the true provision, whose benefit endures for its possessor in this world and the next, it is the provision of piety (taqwa), which is a provision for the journey to the abode of settlement, and which leads to the most perfect pleasure and the most exalted bliss, forever and ever. Whoever abandons this provision is cut off, exposed to every evil, and prevented from reaching the abode of the righteous. This is praise of piety. Then He commanded it to those of sound intellect, saying: {And fear Me, O people of understanding}; that is, O people of sound minds, fear your Lord, whose fear is the greatest thing intellects command, and abandoning it is a sign of ignorance and corrupt judgment.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verses 198–202:

{198} When Allah the Exalted commanded taqwa (God-consciousness), He informed that seeking Allah's bounty through trade during the seasons of Hajj and at other times is not blameworthy, provided it does not distract one from what is loved, when the intention is Hajj and the earning is lawful and attributed to Allah's bounty, not attributed to the servant's own cleverness while fixing one's gaze on the means and forgetting the Causer. This latter is blameworthy in itself. In His words: ﴿So when you pour forth from Arafat, remember Allah at al-Mash'ar al-Haram﴾, there is an indication of several matters:

The first: standing at Arafat, and that it was well known to be one of the pillars of Hajj, since pouring forth from Arafat is only after standing there.

The second: the command to remember Allah at al-Mash'ar al-Haram, which is Muzdalifah. This too was well known: one spends the night of the sacrifice (Nahr) there, and after the Fajr prayer one stands at Muzdalifah supplicating until it is fully light. Included in remembering Allah there is performing the obligatory and voluntary prayers there.

The third: that standing at Muzdalifah comes after standing at Arafat, as indicated by the particle fa' (then) and the sequential order.

The fourth and fifth: that both Arafat and Muzdalifah are among the sites of Hajj whose performance and display are intended.

The sixth: that Muzdalifah is within the Sacred Precinct (Haram), as indicated by the qualifier "al-Haram" attached to it.

The seventh: that Arafat is outside the Sacred Precinct (Hill), as implied by the qualification applied to Muzdalifah.

﴿And remember Him as He has guided you, though before it you were indeed among the astray﴾; i.e., remember Allah the Exalted as He has bestowed on you guidance after misguidance, and as He taught you what you did not know. These are among the greatest blessings, which must be met with gratitude by remembering the Benefactor with the heart and the tongue.

{199} ﴿Then pour forth from where the people pour forth﴾; i.e., then pour forth from Muzdalifah from the place from which the people have poured forth from the time of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) until now. The purpose of this pouring forth was well known to them: throwing the pebbles (ramy al-jimar), sacrificing the offerings (hadyi), circumambulation (tawaf), running between Safa and Marwa (sa'y), spending the nights at Mina during the days of tashriq, and completing the remaining rites. Since this pouring forth is aimed at what has been mentioned, and these acts are the last of the rites, Allah the Exalted commanded, upon completing them, that one seek His forgiveness and increase in remembering Him. Seeking forgiveness is for the deficiencies that occur in the servant's performance of his worship and his shortcoming in it, and remembering Allah is thanking Allah for His favour upon him in granting him success in this great act of worship and this immense grace. Thus it is fitting for the servant, whenever he finishes an act of worship, to seek Allah's forgiveness for shortcoming and to thank Him for the success, not like one who thinks he has perfected the worship and bestowed a favour upon his Lord, and believes it has earned him a lofty station and rank. The latter is deserving of abhorrence and rejection of his deed, just as the former is deserving of acceptance and of success in other deeds.

{200–201–202} Then Allah the Exalted informed about the states of creation: that all of them ask Him for their needs and seek to ward off what harms them, but their aims differ. Among them is the one who says: ﴿Our Lord, give us in this world﴾; i.e., he asks Him for worldly aims that are among his desires, and he has no share in the Hereafter because of his aversion to it and the limiting of his aspiration to this world. Among them is one who calls upon Allah for the welfare of both abodes and who turns to Him in the matters of his religion and his worldly life. Each of these has a share of what they have earned and done, and Allah the Exalted will recompense them according to their deeds, aims and intentions, with a recompense that lies between justice and bounty, for which He is praised with the most complete and perfect praise.

In this verse there is evidence that Allah answers the supplication of every supplicant, whether Muslim, disbelieving or sinful. However, His answering the supplication of one who calls upon Him is not a proof of His love for him or of his nearness to Him, except in the matters of the Hereafter and the great matters of religion. The good sought in this world includes everything that is pleasing to the servant: wholesome, abundant, lawful provision; a righteous wife; offspring that gladden the eye; comfort; beneficial knowledge; righteous deeds; and similar beloved and permissible desires. The good of the Hereafter is safety from punishment in the grave, at the place of standing and in the Fire, the attainment of Allah's pleasure, success in everlasting bliss, and nearness to the Merciful Lord. Thus this supplication becomes the most comprehensive and complete of supplications and the most deserving of being preferred. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) would frequently make this supplication and urge others to make it.

{203} Almighty God commands remembrance of Him during the numbered days, which are the three days of tashriq (the days of drying meat) following the 'Eid, because of their excellence and honour, because the rest of the rites of Hajj are performed during them, and because people are the guests of God during them. For this reason fasting on them is prohibited. Therefore remembrance of God during them has a distinction that it does not have at other times. This is why the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The days of tashriq are days of eating, drinking, and remembrance of God."

Remembrance of God during them includes remembering Him when throwing the pebbles (rami al-jamarat), when slaughtering, and the specific remembrance following the obligatory prayers. Indeed, some scholars said that unrestricted takbir is recommended during them, as in the ten days, and this is not far-fetched.

﴿So whoever hastens in two days﴾; that is, leaves Mina and departs from it before the sun sets on the second day, ﴿there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays﴾; by spending the night there on the third night and throwing the pebbles on the following day, ﴿there is no sin upon him﴾. This is a concession from God to His servants in permitting both of these two options. However, it is well known that when both options are permitted, delaying is better, because it involves more worship.

Since the negation of blame might be understood as negating blame in that which was mentioned and in other matters, the summary is that blame is negated only for the one who hastens and the one who delays. He restricted it with His words: ﴿for him who fears God﴾; that is, who fears God in all his affairs and the circumstances of Hajj. Whoever fears God in everything, the negation of blame is attained for him in everything, and whoever fears Him in some things but not others, the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. ﴿And fear God﴾; by complying with His commands and avoiding His prohibitions. ﴿And know that you will be gathered unto Him﴾; so He will recompense you for your deeds. Whoever fears Him will find the reward of piety with Him, and whoever does not fear Him, He will punish with the severest punishment. Knowledge of the recompense is among the greatest motives for fearing God, and for this reason God urged knowledge of that.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verses 204–206:

{204} When God, exalted is He, commanded that His remembrance be increased, especially in the excellent times, which is good, beneficial and righteous, He informed us of the state of the one who speaks with his tongue while his actions contradict his words. Speech either elevates a person or lowers him, so He said: {And among the people is one whose speech about the life of this world pleases you}; that is, when he speaks, his speech delights the listener, and when he talks you think he is speaking words that are beneficial. He confirms what he says by {calling God to witness what is in his heart}; that is, he claims that God knows that what is in his heart agrees with what he utters, while he is lying in that, because his actions contradict his words. Had he been truthful, his words and deeds would have agreed, as is the case with the believer who is not a hypocrite. For this reason He said: {and he is the most contentious of opponents}; that is, when you dispute with him, you find in him obstinacy, harshness and partisanship, along with what results from that of ugly qualities, unlike the characters of the believers, who have made ease their mount, submission to the truth their duty and generosity their nature.

{205} {And when he turns away}; this one whose speech pleases you, when he leaves your presence, {he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein}; that is, he exerts himself in acts of disobedience, which are corruption in the land, and thereby {destroys the crops and the animals}; so the crops, fruits and livestock are ruined, diminished, and their blessing decreases because of working in disobedience. {And God does not like corruption}. So, since He does not like corruption, He utterly hates the servant who causes corruption in the land, even if he speaks fine words with his tongue.

In this verse there is evidence that the statements issued by persons are not proof of truthfulness, falsehood, righteousness or wickedness, until the deed that confirms and vouches for them is found, and that one should test the conditions of witnesses, and of the one who is in the right and the one who is in the wrong, among people, by the righteousness of their deeds and by considering the indicators of their states, and not be deceived by their deception or by their praise of themselves. Then He mentioned that this one who causes corruption in the land through disobedience to God, when he is commanded to fear God, becomes arrogant and disdainful.

{206} {But sinful pride seizes him}; so he combines working in disobedience with arrogance toward those who advise him. {Hell will suffice him}; which is the abode of the disobedient and the arrogant. {And how wretched is the resting place}; that is, the dwelling and abode: a constant punishment, unceasing anxiety, and continuous despair, with the punishment not lightened for them and no hope of reward, as recompense for their crime and in return for their deeds. So we seek refuge in God from their states.
