{207} [These are the ones who are granted success, who have sold their souls, cheapened them, and expended them seeking the pleasure of Allah and hoping for His reward. They have paid the price to the Rich, the Faithful, the Compassionate toward His servants, who, out of His compassion and mercy, granted them success in doing so. He has promised to fulfill this, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their souls and their properties in exchange for that they will have Paradise...﴾ to the end of the verse. In this verse, He informs that they have bought their souls and expended them, and He informs of His compassion, which necessitates the attainment of what they sought and the expenditure of what they desired. So do not ask after this about the generosity that they will receive, nor about the success and honor that will reach them.]

{208} This is a command from Allah the Exalted to the believers that they enter {into Islam completely} (al-silm); that is, into all the laws of the religion, leaving none of them aside, and that they not be among those who have taken their own desire as their god. If the prescribed command agrees with their desire, they do it; and if it opposes it, they abandon it. Rather, it is obligatory that desire be subordinate to the religion, that they do every act of goodness they are able to do, and for what they are unable to do, they commit themselves to it and intend it, so that they attain it by their intention. And since entering into Islam completely cannot be achieved or conceived except by opposing the paths of Satan, He said: {And do not follow the steps of Satan}; that is, in doing acts of disobedience to Allah. {Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy}; and a clear enemy only commands evil and immorality and what harms you.

And since the servant is bound to fall into some error and lapse, the Exalted said:

{209} {And if you slip after clear evidence has come to you}; that is, with knowledge and certainty, {then know that Allah is Exalted in Might, Wise}. In this is a severe warning and intimidation that necessitates abandoning lapses. For the Exalted in Might, the Wise, when the disobedient one disobeys Him, overpowers him with His strength and punishes him according to the requirement of His wisdom, for among His wisdom is the punishment of the disobedient and the criminals.

{208} This is a command from Allah the Exalted to the believers that they enter {into Islam completely} (al-silm); that is, into all the laws of the religion, leaving none of them aside, and that they not be among those who have taken their own desire as their god. If the prescribed command agrees with their desire, they do it; and if it opposes it, they abandon it. Rather, it is obligatory that desire be subordinate to the religion, that they do every act of goodness they are able to do, and for what they are unable to do, they commit themselves to it and intend it, so that they attain it by their intention. And since entering into Islam completely cannot be achieved or conceived except by opposing the paths of Satan, He said: {And do not follow the steps of Satan}; that is, in doing acts of disobedience to Allah. {Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy}; and a clear enemy only commands evil and immorality and what harms you.

And since the servant is bound to fall into some error and lapse, the Exalted said:

{209} {And if you slip after clear evidence has come to you}; that is, with knowledge and certainty, {then know that Allah is Exalted in Might, Wise}. In this is a severe warning and intimidation that necessitates abandoning lapses. For the Exalted in Might, the Wise, when the disobedient one disobeys Him, overpowers him with His strength and punishes him according to the requirement of His wisdom, for among His wisdom is the punishment of the disobedient and the criminals.

(210) There is in this verse a severe warning and threat, such that hearts are struck with dread. Allah, exalted is He, says: Do those who spread corruption on the earth, who follow the steps of Satan and reject the command of Allah, await anything but the Day of Recompense for their deeds? That Day is filled with terrors, hardships and horrors that shake the hearts of the wrongdoers, and the evil recompense is realized for the corrupters. On that Day, Allah folds up the heavens and the earth, the stars are scattered, the sun and the moon are wound up, the noble angels descend and surround the creatures, and the Lord, blessed and exalted is He, comes down ﴿in canopies of clouds﴾ to judge between His servants with a just decision. The scales are set up, the records are spread out, the faces of the people of happiness turn bright, and the faces of the people of misery turn dark. The people of good are distinguished from the people of evil, and each is repaid for his deeds. Then the wrongdoer will bite his hands when he comes to know the reality of his state.

This verse and others like it are evidence for the doctrine of Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah (the People of the Sunnah and the Community), who affirm the attributes of will and volition (al-sifat al-ikhtiyariyyah), such as istiwa' (being established above the Throne), nuzul (descent), maji' (coming), and similar attributes which Allah has reported about Himself, or which His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, has reported about Him. They affirm these attributes in a manner befitting the majesty and greatness of Allah, without likening them to creation (tashbih) and without distorting their meanings (tahrif). This stands in opposition to the Mu'attilah (those who deny the attributes) of various kinds, including the Jahmiyyah, the Mu'tazilah, the Ash'ariyyah and others like them, who deny these attributes and interpret the verses to fit these denials with interpretations for which Allah has sent down no authority. Their true position amounts to impugning the clarity of the explanation of Allah and of His Messenger, and claiming that their own speech is what brings guidance in this matter. These people have no textual proof, nor any rational proof.

As for the textual evidence, they have acknowledged that the texts in the Book and the Sunnah, in their apparent and even explicit meaning, indicate the doctrine of Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah, and that to make them indicate their false doctrine they must depart from their apparent meaning, add to them and subtract from them. As you can see, no one in whose heart is an atom's weight of faith would accept this.

As for reason, there is nothing in reason that indicates the negation of these attributes. Rather, reason indicates that the one who acts is more perfect than the one who is unable to act, and that His action, both that which is related to Himself and that which is related to His creation, is a perfection. If they claim that affirming these attributes implies likeness to His creation, it is said to them: discourse on the attributes follows discourse on the Essence. Just as Allah has an Essence that essences do not resemble, so He has attributes that attributes do not resemble. His attributes follow His Essence, and the attributes of His creatures follow their essences. Therefore there is nothing in affirming them that implies tashbih in any way.

It is also said to those who affirm some attributes and deny others, or who affirm the names but not the attributes: either you affirm all of them as Allah affirmed them for Himself and as His Messenger affirmed them, or you deny all of them and become a denier of the Lord of the worlds. Your affirming some and denying others is a contradiction. So differentiate between what you affirmed and what you denied, and you will never find a way to make that distinction. If you say, "What I affirmed does not imply tashbih," the People of the Sunnah and affirmation say to you, "What you denied does not imply tashbih either." If you say, "I understand from what I denied nothing but tashbih," the deniers say to you, "And we understand from what you affirmed nothing but tashbih." Thus whatever the People of the Sunnah answer the deniers, the deniers answer them with regard to what the Sunnah denies.

The conclusion is that whoever denies something and affirms something of what the Book and the Sunnah have indicated should be affirmed is self-contradictory. He has no legitimate textual proof and no rational proof. Rather, he has opposed both reason and transmitted text.

{211} The Exalted says: {Ask the Children of Israel how many clear signs We gave them}, which indicate the truth and the veracity of the messengers. So they were certain of them and recognized them, yet they did not carry out the thanks for this blessing which requires that it be acted upon. Rather, they disbelieved in them, and {changed the blessing of Allah into disbelief}. For this reason they deserved that Allah send down His punishment upon them, and deprive them of His reward.

Allah, the Exalted, called the disbelief in a blessing a "changing" of it, because whoever is blessed by Allah with a blessing, whether religious or worldly, and does not thank Him for it, and does not fulfill its obligation, it vanishes from him, departs, and is exchanged for disbelief and sins. Thus disbelief becomes the replacement for the blessing. As for one who thanks Allah, the Exalted, and fulfills its due, it remains, continues, and Allah increases it for him.

{212} God, exalted is He, informs us that those who disbelieve in God, His signs and His messengers, and who do not submit to His law, have had the life of this world made attractive to them. It has been made appealing in their eyes and hearts, so they are content with it and at rest in it. Thus their desires, their intentions and all their actions become devoted to it. They turn toward it, apply themselves wholeheartedly to acquiring it, exalt it, and exalt those who share their conduct, while they belittle the believers, mock them, and say: "Are these the ones whom God has favored from among us?" This reflects the weakness of their intellects and their limited outlook, for the world is a place of trial and testing. Misery in it will befall both the people of faith and the people of disbelief. Indeed, the believer in this world, even if some hardship befalls him, is patient and seeks reward, so God lightens for him through his faith and patience what He does not lighten for others. The true concern and the real preference lie entirely in the everlasting abode. For this reason God, exalted is He, said: {But those who are godfearing will be above them on the Day of Resurrection}. So the God-fearing will be in the highest ranks, enjoying all kinds of bliss, joy, delight and happiness, while the disbelievers will be beneath them in the lowest depths, tormented with all kinds of punishment, humiliation and everlasting misery without end. In this verse there is consolation for the believers and a reproach to the disbelievers. Since worldly and otherworldly provisions are obtained only by God's decree and can be attained only by God's will, God, exalted is He, said: {And God provides for whom He wills without reckoning}. Worldly provision is therefore granted to both believer and disbeliever. As for the provision of the hearts, namely knowledge, faith, love of God, fear of Him, hope in Him and the like, God gives it only to those whom He loves.

{213} [Meaning: they were united upon guidance, and that was ten centuries after Noah, peace be upon him. Then, when they differed regarding the religion, a group of them disbelieved, and the other group remained upon guidance, and dispute arose, so God sent the messengers to judge between the creatures and establish the proof against them. It was said: rather, they were]; that is, the people were united upon disbelief, misguidance and wretchedness, having no light and no faith, so God, exalted is He, showed them mercy by sending messengers to them {as bringers of good news}: to whoever obeys God, with the fruits of obedience, such as provision, strength of body and heart, and a good life, and the highest of these is attaining the good pleasure of God and Paradise; {and as warners}: to whoever disobeys God, with the fruits of disobedience, such as deprivation of provision, weakness, humiliation and a constricted life, and the most severe of these is the wrath of God and the Fire. And He sent down the Books to them with truth, which are true reports and just commands.

Everything contained in the Books is truth that judges between those who differ concerning the fundamentals and the subsidiary matters. This is what is obligatory when disagreement and dispute arise: that the difference be referred back to God and His Messenger. Had it not been that His Book and the Sunnah of His Messenger contain the decisive judgment of disputes, He would not have commanded referral to them, nor would He have mentioned His great blessing of sending down the Books to the People of the Book. This would require their agreement upon them and their unity, yet He, exalted is He, informed that some of them transgressed against others, and dispute, contention and great divergence arose, so they differed concerning the Book upon which they should have been most united. This happened after they had known it and been certain of it through clear signs and decisive proofs, and by that they went far astray. God guided {those who believed} of this Ummah {to the truth concerning which they differed}. So whatever the People of the Book differed about and erred in regarding truth and correctness, God guided this Ummah to the truth in it {by His permission}, by His facilitation for them and His mercy.

{And God guides whom He wills to a straight path}: thus God, exalted is He, made the creation universally called to the straight path, as an act of justice from Him and to establish proof against the creatures, lest they say, "There came to us neither bringer of good news nor warner." And He guided, by His bounty, mercy, aid and kindness, whomever He willed of His servants. This is His grace and favor, and that is His justice and wisdom, blessed and exalted is He.

{215} That is: they ask you about spending, and this covers the question of what is spent and upon whom it is spent. So He answered them about it, saying: ﴿Say: Whatever wealth you spend for good﴾; that is, whether it is little or much. The people most deserving of it, and most entitled to being given precedence, are those with the greatest right over you, namely your parents, whose honoring is obligatory and whose disobedience is forbidden. Among the greatest ways of honoring them is spending on them, and among the greatest forms of disobedience is abandoning spending on them. For this reason, spending on them is obligatory upon a wealthy child. After the parents come the nearest relatives according to their different degrees: the nearer first, then the next nearest, in accordance with closeness and need. Spending on them is both charity and maintaining family ties. ﴿And the orphans﴾: these are the young children who have no earner, so they are in a state of likely need, since they are not able to manage their own affairs and have no one to earn for them. Therefore God enjoined His servants to care for them, out of His mercy and kindness toward them. ﴿And the needy﴾: these are the people of want and the possessors of dire necessity, whom need has reduced to dwelling in poverty; so they are spent upon to remove their needs and make them self-sufficient. ﴿And the wayfarer﴾: that is, the stranger cut off from his means in a land other than his own, so he is helped on his journey with the expense that will bring him to his destination.

When God specified these categories because of the intensity of their need, He then generalized, saying: ﴿And whatever good you do﴾; from charity to these and others, and indeed from all kinds of acts of obedience and devotion, since they all fall under the name of good. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of it﴾; He will reward you for it and preserve it for you, each according to his intention and sincerity, the abundance or scarcity of his expense, the intensity of the need for it, and the greatness of its effect and benefit.

{216} This verse prescribes fighting in the way of Allah, after the believers had been commanded to refrain from it because of their weakness and their inability to bear it. When the Prophet (ﷺ) migrated to Madinah, and the Muslims increased in number and grew strong, Allah the Exalted commanded them to fight. He informed them that it is disliked by the souls, because of the hardship and difficulty it entails, the occurrence of various kinds of fear, and exposure to destruction. Yet despite this, it is pure good, because of the great reward it contains, the protection from the painful punishment, victory over the enemies, the gaining of spoils, and other benefits that far outweigh the dislike within it. ﴿And perhaps you dislike a thing and it is bad for you﴾; and this is like sitting back from jihad in pursuit of ease, which is evil, because it results in humiliation, the domination of the enemies over Islam and its people, the occurrence of disgrace and degradation, the loss of a great reward, and the incurring of punishment.

These verses establish a general and consistent principle: acts of good that the souls dislike because of the hardship in them are undoubtedly good, and acts of evil that the souls love because of the ease and pleasure they imagine in them are undoubtedly evil. As for the affairs of this world, the matter is not consistent; yet it is generally the case for the believing servant that when he loves a matter and Allah decrees for him causes that turn him away from it, it is good for him. The most suitable response for him in this is to thank Allah and to believe that the good lies in what actually occurred, for he knows that Allah, the Exalted, is more merciful to the servant than he is to himself, more capable of securing his welfare than he is, and more knowledgeable of his interest than he is, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But Allah knows, and you know not.﴾ Therefore, it is fitting for you to submit to His decrees, whether they please you or displease you.

Since the command to fight, if left unrestricted, would include the sacred months and others, Allah the Exalted made an exception for fighting in the sacred months, saying:

{217} The majority of scholars hold that the prohibition of fighting in the sacred months (al-ashhur al-hurum) was abrogated (mansukh) by the command to fight the polytheists wherever they are found. Some exegetes said: it was not abrogated, because the absolute (mutlaq) is to be understood in light of the restricted (muqayyad), and this verse restricts the general command to fight absolutely; and because among the distinctions of the sacred months, indeed the greatest of their distinctions, is the prohibition of fighting in them. This applies only to offensive fighting (qital al-ibtida'), whereas defensive fighting (qital al-daf') is permitted in the sacred months just as it is permitted in the Sacred Precinct (al-balad al-haram).

When this verse was revealed concerning what befell the expedition of ʿAbdullah ibn Jahsh, when they killed ʿAmr ibn al-Hadrami and seized his property, which was, as it is said, in the month of Rajab, the polytheists reproached them for fighting in the sacred months. In their reproach they were wrongdoers, for they had among them abominations, some of which were greater than what they reproached the Muslims with. God, Exalted is He, stated what was among them: {and hindering from the way of God}; that is, they hindered those who wished to believe in God and His Messenger, tempted those who believed in Him, and strove to turn them back from their religion; and their disbelief occurring in the sacred month and the sacred precinct, which by itself is sufficient for evil, so how much more so when it was in a sacred month and a sacred precinct. {and expelling its people}; that is, the people of the Sacred Mosque, namely the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions, for they had more right to it than the polytheists, and they were its true inhabitants, yet they expelled them {from it} and did not allow them to reach it, although this House is equal for the one who dwells in it and the visitor from the desert. Each of these matters {is greater than killing} in the sacred month, {how much more so when all of them were combined in them}. Thus it is known that they were wicked wrongdoers in their reproach of the believers.

Then God, Exalted is He, informed that they will not cease fighting the believers, and their aim is not their wealth or killing them; rather, their aim is to turn them back from their religion and make them disbelievers after their belief, {until they are among the companions of the Blaze}. They expend their power in that and strive with whatever they can, {but God refuses except to perfect His light, though the disbelievers dislike it}. This description is general for all disbelievers, who will not cease fighting others until they turn them back from their religion, and especially the People of the Book, the Jews and Christians, who have expended effort in organizations, spread missionaries, dispatched doctors, built schools to attract nations to their religion, and introduced into them every doubt they could use to cast suspicion upon their religion. But what is hoped from God, Exalted, who bestowed His favor upon the believers with Islam, chose for them His upright religion, and perfected His religion for them, is that He complete His blessing upon them by their upholding it in the most complete manner, that He humiliate everyone who wishes to extinguish His light, make their plotting recoil upon their own necks, support His religion, and exalt His word. This verse is true of these disbelievers present today just as it was true of those before them: {Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to hinder from the way of God; they will spend it, then it will become a regret for them, then they will be overcome. And those who disbelieve will be gathered into Hell}.

Then God, Exalted is He, informed that whoever apostatizes from Islam, by choosing disbelief over it and persisting in that until he dies a disbeliever, {those, their deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter}, because the condition for their validity, which is Islam, is not present, {and those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever}.

The verse indicates by its implication (mafhum) that whoever apostatizes and then returns to Islam, his deeds [that preceded his apostasy] return to him; and likewise whoever repents of sins, his previous deeds return to him.

{218} These three deeds are the emblem of happiness and the pivot of servitude, and by them one can know what profit and loss a person has. As for faith (al-iman), do not ask about its excellence, for how could one ask about something that is the dividing line between the people of happiness and the people of misery, and between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire? It is the thing that, when present in a servant, causes his good deeds to be accepted, and when it is absent, no voluntary or obligatory act of his is accepted. As for emigration (al-hijrah), it is the leaving of what is loved and familiar for the sake of Allah's pleasure: the emigrant leaves his homeland, his wealth, his family and his friends, seeking nearness to Allah and support for His religion. As for striving (al-jihad), it is the exertion of effort in combating the enemies and the complete striving to support the religion of Allah and to suppress the religion of Satan. It is the peak of righteous deeds, its reward is the best of rewards, and it is the greatest cause for the expansion of the domain of Islam, the humiliation of the worshippers of idols, and the security of the Muslims for their selves, their wealth and their children. Whoever performs these three deeds despite their hardship and difficulty will be even more diligent in performing other deeds and in perfecting them. It is therefore fitting that these people be the ones who hope for the mercy of Allah, because they have brought about the cause that necessitates mercy. In this is evidence that hope is only valid after one has undertaken the causes of happiness. As for hope accompanied by laziness and neglect of the means, this is incapacity, wishful thinking and delusion, and it indicates weakness of its possessor's resolve and deficiency of his intellect, like one who hopes for a child without marriage, or for a harvest without seed, watering and the like.

In His saying: ﴿Those hope for the mercy of Allah﴾, there is an indication that the servant, even if he performs such deeds as these, should not rely upon them or depend on them. Rather, he should hope for the mercy of his Lord, and hope that his deeds are accepted, his sins forgiven and his faults covered. For this reason He said: ﴿And Allah is Forgiving﴾; i.e., to whoever repents sincerely, ﴿Merciful﴾; His mercy encompasses everything, and His bounty and kindness cover every living thing. In this is evidence that whoever performs these mentioned deeds obtains Allah's forgiveness, since good deeds erase bad deeds, and obtains Allah's mercy. When he obtains forgiveness, the punishments of this world and the Hereafter, which are the effects of sins that have been forgiven and whose effects have vanished, are repelled from him. And when he obtains mercy, he attains every good in this world and the Hereafter. Indeed, these mentioned deeds are themselves a mercy from Allah toward them: had He not granted them success, they would not have intended them; had He not enabled them, they would not have been able to perform them; and had He not favored them, He would not have completed them and accepted them from them. So to Him belongs the favor, first and last, and He is the one who bestowed both the means and the result. Then He, exalted is He, said:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 219:

{219} That is: they ask you, O Messenger, the believers, about the rulings concerning wine (khamr) and gambling (maysir). Both were practiced in the Jahiliyyah and in the early days of Islam, so it seems a difficulty had arisen regarding them, and for this reason they asked about their ruling. So Allah the Exalted commanded His Prophet to explain to them the benefits and harms of both, so that this would serve as a preface to their prohibition and the making obligatory of abandoning them. He informed that their sin and harms, and what proceeds from them of loss of intellect and wealth, of turning away from the remembrance of Allah and from the prayer, of enmity and hatred, are greater than the benefit they imagine: gaining wealth through trading in wine, acquiring it through gambling, and the delight that souls feel when indulging in them. This explanation was a deterrent for souls from them, because the intelligent person prefers what its benefit outweighs and avoids what its harm outweighs. But since they had become accustomed to them, and abandoning them by prohibition at the first moment would be difficult, He placed this verse as a preface to the prohibition that He mentioned in His saying: {O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone alters, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan; so avoid it that you may be successful} up to His saying: {So will you not desist?} And this is of His gentleness, mercy and wisdom. For this reason, when it was revealed, ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "We have desisted, we have desisted."

As for khamr, it is every intoxicant that covers and conceals the intellect, of whatever kind it may be. As for maysir, it is every contest in which there is a return from both parties, such as backgammon (nard) and chess, and every verbal or physical contest with a stake, except racing of horses, camels and archery, for these are permitted because they aid in jihad; [therefore] the Lawgiver granted a concession regarding them.

{And they ask you what they should spend. Say, "The excess." Thus Allah makes clear to you the verses that you may give thought, [Concerning] this world and the Hereafter.}

This is a question about the amount that they should spend of their wealth, so Allah made the matter easy for them and commanded them to spend the excess (al-'afw), which is what is easily available of their wealth and on which their need and necessity do not depend. This applies to each person according to his circumstances, whether rich, poor or middling; each has the ability to spend what is surplus of his wealth, even if it is half a date. For this reason Allah commanded His Messenger - may Allah bless him and grant him peace - to take the excess of people's dispositions and charities, and not to burden them with what is difficult for them. That is because Allah the Exalted did not command us with what He commanded us out of any need of His for us, nor as an imposition upon us of what is hardship; rather He commanded us with what is in our happiness, what eases us, and what brings benefit to us and to our brethren, and for this He deserves the most complete praise.

When Allah the Exalted had explained this clear explanation and informed the servants of the secrets of His legislation, He said: {Thus Allah makes clear to you the verses}; that is, the signs that indicate the truth and produce beneficial knowledge and discernment, {that you may give thought [concerning] this world and the Hereafter}; that is, so that you may employ your thoughts upon the secrets of His legislation, and know that His commands contain the benefits of this world and the Hereafter. And also so that you may reflect upon this world and the swiftness of its passing, so that you renounce it, and upon the Hereafter and its permanence, and that it is the abode of recompense, so that you cultivate it.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 220:

{220} When the words of the Most High were revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly are only consuming fire into their bellies, and they will burn in a Blaze﴾, it weighed heavily upon the Muslims, and they separated their food from the food of the orphans, fearing for themselves that they might partake of it, even in this situation in which it was customary to share. They asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about that, and the Most High informed them that the intent is to reform the property of orphans by preserving and safeguarding it and trading with it, and that mixing with them in food and other things is permissible in a manner that does not harm the orphans, because they are your brothers, and it is the nature of a brother to mix with his brother. The determining factor in this is intention and action. Whoever Allah knows, from his intention, is reforming the orphan and has no desire for his wealth, then if something enters into it without intent, there is no blame upon him. Whoever Allah knows, from his intention, that his purpose in mixing is to reach its consumption [and taking it], that is the one who is burdened and sinful, and means have the rulings of their ends.

In this verse is evidence for the permissibility of various kinds of mixing in food, drink, contracts and other matters. This concession is a kindness from the Most High, a benevolence and an expansion upon the believers. Otherwise, ﴿if Allah had willed, He would have put you in difficulty﴾; that is, He would have burdened you by not granting this concession, so you would have been constrained, burdened and sinful. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Mighty﴾; that is, He possesses complete strength and dominance over everything, but along with that ﴿He is Wise﴾; He does not act except in accordance with the requirement of His perfect wisdom and complete care. His might does not contradict His wisdom, so it is not said that He wills a thing and it happens to accord with wisdom or to oppose it. Rather, it is said that His acts, and likewise His rulings, follow His wisdom. He does not create anything in vain; rather, there must be a wisdom in it, whether we know it or not. Likewise, He has not legislated for His servants anything devoid of wisdom. He commands only what contains pure or predominant benefit, and forbids only what contains pure or predominant harm, for the completeness of His wisdom and His mercy.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 221:

{221} That is: {And do not marry} [women] {polytheistic women} (as long as they remain upon their polytheism) {until they believe}. Because a believing woman, however plain she may be, is better than a polytheistic woman, however beautiful she may be. This is general, covering all polytheistic women, but the verse of al-Ma'idah specified it with regard to permitting the women of the People of the Book, as He, the Exalted, said: {And [lawful to you are] chaste women from those who were given the Scripture} [5:5]; and {And do not marry polytheistic men until they believe} [2:221]. This latter is general, with no specification in it. Then He, the Exalted, mentioned the wisdom behind the prohibition of a Muslim man or woman marrying one who differs with them in religion, saying: {Those invite to the Fire} [2:221], that is, in their statements, their actions and their conditions. So associating with them is a danger, and the danger is not one of worldly harms, but rather everlasting wretchedness.

It is derived from the reasoning of the verse that it forbids associating with every polytheist and innovator; for if marriage is not permissible even though it contains many benefits, then mere association is more deserving of prohibition, especially association in which the polytheist or the like rises above the Muslim, such as in service and the like.

In His saying: {And do not marry polytheistic men} there is evidence for the requirement of a guardian (wali) in marriage. {But Allah invites to Paradise and forgiveness}, that is, He invites His servants to attain Paradise and forgiveness, of which among the effects is the averting of punishments; and this is by inviting to their causes, from righteous deeds, sincere repentance, beneficial knowledge and righteous action. {And He makes clear His verses}, that is, His rulings and their wisdom, {to the people, that they may remember} [2:221]; so that this remembrance obliges them to recall what they had forgotten, to know what they had been ignorant of, and to comply with what they had neglected. Then He, the Exalted, said:

Ibn Sa'di's commentary on verses 222–223:

{222} Allah, exalted is He, informs us about their question concerning menstruation: whether a woman remains as she was after her menses as she was before them, or whether she must be avoided entirely, as the Jews did. He, exalted is He, informed them that menstruation is harm (adha). Since it is harm, it is part of wisdom that Allah, exalted is He, should prohibit His servants from the harm alone. For this reason He said: ﴿So keep away from women during menstruation﴾; that is, from the place of menstruation, which is intercourse in the private part specifically. This is prohibited by consensus (ijma'). The specification of keeping away during menstruation indicates that physical contact and touching a menstruating woman, other than intercourse in the private part, is permissible. However, His saying ﴿and do not approach them until they are purified﴾ indicates that one should abstain from physical contact in what is close to the private part, which is the area between the navel and the knee. This should be avoided, just as the Prophet (ﷺ), when he wished to be intimate with his wife while she was menstruating, would order her to wrap a waist-wrapper (izar) and then he would be intimate with her. The limit of this keeping away and not approaching during menstruation is ﴿until they are purified﴾; that is, until their blood stops. When the blood stops, the prohibition that existed during its flow is lifted. The permissibility of intercourse depends on two conditions: the cessation of blood and the ritual bath (ghusl) after it. When the blood stopped, the first condition was lifted and the second remained. For this reason He said: ﴿And when they have purified themselves﴾; that is, have bathed, ﴿then come to them as Allah has commanded you﴾; that is, in the front passage and not in the rear, because the rear is not the place of tilth (harth). This is evidence for the obligation of the menstruating woman's ritual bath, and that the cessation of blood is a condition for its validity. Since this prohibition was a kindness from Him toward His servants and a safeguard from harm, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are constantly repentant﴾; that is, who repent from their sins continually, ﴿and He loves those who purify themselves﴾; that is, who keep themselves far from sins. This includes sensory purity from impurities and ritual states of minor and major impurity (ahdath), and in it is the legislation of purity in general, because Allah, exalted is He, loves the one who is characterized by it. For this reason, purity in general is a condition for the validity of prayer, circumambulation of the House (tawaf), and permissibility of touching the mushaf. It also includes spiritual purity from base character traits, ugly attributes, and vile deeds.

{223} ﴿Your women are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish﴾; facing forward or backward, provided that it is only in the front passage, because it is the place of tilth, which is the place from which children come. This is evidence for the prohibition of intercourse in the rear, because Allah has permitted approaching women only in the place from which tilth comes. Many hadiths have been transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning the prohibition of this and the curse upon the one who does it. ﴿And put forward for yourselves﴾; that is, by drawing near to Allah through good deeds. Among these is that a man be intimate with his wife and have intercourse with her seeking nearness to Allah, with intention of reward, and hoping to bring about offspring through whom Allah benefits. ﴿And fear Allah﴾; that is, in all your circumstances, remain constant in God-consciousness (taqwa), seeking help in that through your knowledge. ﴿And know that you will meet Him﴾; and that He will recompense you for your righteous deeds and others. [Then he said]: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾. He did not mention what the good tidings are, to indicate generality, and that for them there are good tidings in this worldly life and in the Hereafter. Every good and every removal of harm that is arranged upon faith is included in this glad tidings. It also includes the love of Allah for the believers, the love for what gladdens them, and the recommendation of encouraging them and inspiring their eagerness with what Allah has prepared for them of worldly and otherworldly reward.

The purpose of oath and swearing is to glorify the one sworn by and to confirm the matter sworn to. Allah, exalted is He, had commanded the keeping of oaths, and the requirement of this would be keeping them in every matter. However, Allah, exalted is He, made an exception to this: when fulfilling an oath entails abandoning what is more beloved to Him. So He forbade His servants from making their oaths "ʿurḍah" (an obstacle), meaning a barrier and a hindrance, preventing them from being righteous (yabarru), that is, from doing good, from being mindful of God (yattaqū) and avoiding evil, and from reconciling between people (yuṣliḥū). Thus, whoever swears to abandon an obligation, it becomes obligatory to break that oath (ḥinth), and it is forbidden to persist in his oath. Whoever swears to abandon a recommended act, breaking it is recommended for him. Whoever swears to do a forbidden act, breaking it is obligatory, or to do a disliked act, breaking it is recommended. As for what is permissible, it is preferable to keep the oath and not break it.

This verse is used as evidence for the well-known principle that when benefits conflict, the more important of them is given precedence. Here, fulfilling an oath is a benefit, and carrying out the commands of Allah in these matters is a greater benefit than that, so it is given precedence. Then He concluded the verse with these two noble names, saying: {And Allah is All-Hearing}; that is, of all voices, {All-Knowing}; of intentions and intents. Included in this is His hearing the words of those who swear and His knowledge of their purposes, whether they are good or evil. Within this is a warning against requiting them, and that your deeds and intentions have been firmly recorded in His knowledge. Then He, exalted is He, said:

{225} That is: He will not hold you to account for what slips from your tongues of oaths that are void, which a person utters without intending them and without any resolve of the heart, but which simply pass over his tongue, such as a man's saying in the course of his speech: "No, by Allah," and "Yes, by Allah," and his swearing to a matter of the past that he believes to be true of himself. Accountability attaches only to what the heart intends. In this there is evidence for the consideration of intentions in statements just as they are considered in deeds. And Allah is Forgiving to whoever turns back to Him in repentance, and Forbearing toward whoever disobeys Him, in that He does not hasten to punish him, but shows forbearance toward him, veils his fault, and pardons him, although He is able to act against him and he is in His presence.

{226} This is one of the oaths specific to wives, concerning a particular matter: a man's oath to abstain from having intercourse with his wife, whether absolutely or limited to a period of less than four months or more. If a man makes an ila' (oath of abstention, ila') against his wife specifically, then if the period is less than four months, it is like other oaths: if he breaks it, he must make expiation (kaffarah), and if he fulfils his oath, nothing is owed on him. His wife has no recourse against him, for he has been granted four months. If the oath is for an indefinite period, or for a period exceeding four months, a period of four months from his oath is imposed upon him when his wife requests it, because it is her right. When that period is complete, he is ordered to return (fi'ah), which means intercourse. If he has intercourse, nothing is owed on him beyond the expiation of the oath. If he refuses, he is compelled to divorce, and if he still refuses, the judge (hakim) pronounces the divorce upon him. Yet returning and resuming relations with his wife is more beloved to Allah the Exalted. For this reason He said: ﴿And if they return﴾, meaning: if they go back to what they swore to abandon, which is intercourse. ﴿Then indeed Allah is Forgiving﴾, who forgives them what occurred from them of the oath because of their return. ﴿Merciful﴾, in that He made for their oaths an expiation and a dissolution (tahillah) and did not make them a binding obligation that cannot be undone. And He is also merciful toward them in that they returned to their wives, showed them tenderness (hunuww), and had mercy on them.

{227} ﴿And if they resolve upon divorce﴾, meaning: if they refrain from the return, and that is evidence of their aversion to them and their lack of desire for their wives. This does not occur except as a resolve to divorce. If this obligatory right is fulfilled by him directly, well and good; otherwise the judge compels him to it or carries it out himself. ﴿Then indeed Allah is Hearing, Knowing﴾. In this is a warning and threat to whoever makes this oath intending by it harm (mudarrah) and hostility (mushaqqah).

This verse is used as evidence that ila' is specific to wives, based on His saying ﴿from their women﴾, and that intercourse is obligatory once every four months, because after four months he is compelled either to intercourse or to divorce, and this would not be the case unless abstaining from it were obligatory.

{228} That is: the women whom their husbands have divorced, {shall wait for three periods} — that is, they shall observe a waiting period (ʿiddah) of three qurūʾ, that is, menstrual periods or periods of purity, according to the scholars' differing interpretations of the term, although the sound view is that qurʾ means menstruation. This waiting period has several wisdoms. Among them is knowing that the womb is clear: when three qurūʾ have passed over her, it is known that there is no pregnancy in her womb, so that mixing of lineages does not result. For this reason God made it obligatory upon them to report {what God has created in their wombs}, and He forbade them to conceal that, whether pregnancy or menstruation, because concealing it leads to many corruptions. Concealing a pregnancy requires that it be attributed to someone other than its true father, out of desire for him or in haste to end the waiting period. If she attributes it to other than its father, there results the severing of kinship ties, the loss of inheritance, and the veiling of her close relatives (maḥārim) and kin from him. It may even lead to his marrying women who are within the prohibited degrees, and in exchange for this there is attributing the child to other than its father and the establishment of the consequences of that, such as inheritance from him and to him, and making the relatives of the one to whom he is attributed into his relatives. The evil and corruption in this are known only to the Lord of the worlds. Even if there were nothing in it but her remaining with one whose marriage to her is void with respect to him, and her persisting in the great sin of fornication (zinā), that alone would be evil enough.

As for concealing menstruation: if she hastens to report it while lying, there results the cutting off of the husband's right over her and her being made lawful to another, and what branches from that of evil, as we have mentioned. If she lies and reports that there is no menstruation, in order to prolong the waiting period so that she takes maintenance from him that is not obligatory upon him, then it is unlawful gain (suḥt) for her, forbidden on two counts: from the fact that she does not deserve it, and from the fact that she attributes to the Shariʿah a ruling while she is lying. He may take her back after the waiting period ends, and that would be fornication (sifāḥ), since she would then be a stranger to him. For this reason God said: {And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs, if they believe in God and the Last Day}.

The occurrence of concealment from them is evidence of their lack of belief in God and the Last Day. Otherwise, if they believed in God and the Last Day and knew that they would be recompensed for their deeds, none of that would proceed from them. In this there is evidence for accepting a woman's report about what only she can know concerning herself, such as pregnancy, menstruation, and the like.

Then He said: {And their husbands have more right to take them back in that [period], if they desire reconciliation}, that is: their husbands have the right, for as long as she remains in that waiting period, to return them to their marriage, {if they desire reconciliation} — that is, desire for union, affection and love. The implication of the verse is that if they do not desire reconciliation, they have no greater right to take them back, and it is not lawful for them to take them back with the intent of harming her and prolonging the waiting period upon her. Does he still possess that right with this intent? There are two opinions. The majority hold that he possesses it despite the prohibition. The sound view is that if he does not desire reconciliation, he does not possess it, as is apparent from the noble verse. This is another wisdom of this waiting period: perhaps her husband regrets parting from her, so this period is set so that he may reflect and cut off his gaze. This shows His love for harmony between spouses and His dislike of separation, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "The most hateful of lawful things to God is divorce." This applies to revocable divorce. As for irrevocable divorce, the husband has no right to take her back; rather, if both agree to return, there must be a new contract with all its conditions fulfilled.

Then He said: {And they have rights similar to what is incumbent upon them, according to what is reasonable}, that is: women have rights over their husbands of the kind that the husbands have over them, both obligatory and recommended. The reference for rights between spouses is to what is reasonable (maʿrūf), which is the custom prevailing in that land and at that time concerning the like of such a matter for such a person. This varies with the times, places, circumstances, individuals and customs. In this there is evidence that maintenance, clothing, companionship, housing, and likewise intercourse, all refer to what is reasonable. This is the requirement of a general contract; but where there is a stipulation, it is according to their stipulation, except a condition that makes lawful what is forbidden or forbids what is lawful.

{And the men have a degree over them}, that is: a rank, leadership, and an increase of right over them, as God said: {Men are the protectors and maintainers of women, because God has given the one more than the other, and because they spend from their wealth}. The prophethood, judgeship, the lesser and greater imamate, and all other authorities are specific to men, and he has twice what she has in many matters, such as inheritance and the like. {And God is Mighty and Wise} — that is, He possesses overpowering might and great dominion, to which all things submit; yet with His might He is wise in His dispositions.

Excluded from the generality of this verse are pregnant women, whose waiting period is the delivery of the child; and those who have not been consummated with, who have no waiting period; and female slaves, whose waiting period is two menstrual periods, as is the view of the Companions, may God be pleased with them. The context of the verse indicates that what is meant by it is the free woman.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 229:

{229} Divorce in the pre-Islamic period (jahiliyyah) was unlimited, and this continued at the beginning of Islam: a man would divorce his wife without any limit. Whenever he wished to harm her, he would divorce her, and when her waiting period (iddah) was about to end, he would take her back, then divorce her again and do the same with her endlessly. Thus she would suffer harm that only God knows. So God, exalted is He, informed that divorce {twice}, meaning the divorce by which the return (ruj'ah) is possible, is the limit, so that the husband, if he does not intend harm, has the opportunity to take her back and reconsider his decision during this period. As for what exceeds this, it is not a place for that, because whoever exceeds two divorces is either audacious toward what is forbidden or has no desire to keep her, but rather intends harm. For this reason God commanded the husband to keep his wife {with kindness}, meaning good companionship, and to proceed in the manner of others with their wives; this is the more preferred view. Otherwise, {release her with good treatment}, meaning he parts from her. Among good treatment is that he should not take anything of her property upon separating from her, because that is injustice and taking wealth without any exchange. Therefore He said: {And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them, unless both fear that they will not keep within the limits of God}, which is khul' (divorce initiated by the wife through compensation) conducted in a proper manner, when the wife dislikes her husband because of his character, his appearance, or deficiency in his religion, and fears that she will not obey God regarding him. {And if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of God, then there is no blame upon them for what she gives up therewith}, because it is a compensation for achieving her aim of separation. In this is the legitimacy of khul' when this wisdom is present. {These} meaning what preceded of the legal rulings, {are the limits of God}, meaning His rulings which He legislated for you and commanded you to observe {And whoever transgresses the limits of God, then it is those who are the wrongdoers}.

And what greater wrongdoing is there than that of one who rushes into the lawful and passes from it to the unlawful, so that what God has made lawful does not suffice him?

Injustice is of three kinds: the servant's injustice between himself and God; the greatest injustice of the servant, which is shirk (associating partners with God); and the servant's injustice between himself and the creatures.

Shirk, God does not forgive except through repentance, and God does not leave any of the rights of the servants unaddressed. As for the injustice between the servant and his Lord short of shirk, it is under God's will and wisdom.

{230} He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And if he divorces her﴾, i.e., the third pronouncement, ﴿then she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband﴾, i.e., a valid marriage, and he consummates it, because a legally valid marriage (nikah shar'i) is only valid marriage, and it includes the contract (aqd) and intercourse (wat'), and this is by consensus. It is required that the second husband's marriage be a marriage of desire; if it is intended as a means of making her lawful to the first husband (tahlil), then it is not a marriage and does not make her lawful, and the owner's intercourse with a slave-woman does not count either, because he is not a husband. So if the second husband marries her with genuine desire, has intercourse with her, then divorces her and her waiting period (iddah) ends, ﴿there is no blame upon the two of them﴾, i.e., upon the first husband and the wife, ﴿for them to return to one another﴾, i.e., to renew a new contract between them, since He attributed the returning to both of them, which indicates the consideration of mutual consent. However, it is required in the returning that they both think ﴿that they will keep within the limits of Allah﴾, by each of them fulfilling the rights of the other. This is when they regret their previous companionship which necessitated the separation, and they resolve to replace it with good companionship; in this case there is no blame upon them in returning.

The implication of the noble verse is that if they do not think they will keep within the limits of Allah, meaning that it predominates in their assessment that the previous situation remains and the bad companionship has not ended, then there is blame upon them in that, because all matters in which the command of Allah is not established and in which His obedience is not pursued, it is not lawful to undertake them. This indicates that when a person wishes to enter into any matter, especially great or small responsibilities, he should examine himself: if he sees in himself the strength for it and trusts it, he proceeds, otherwise he holds back.

When He, exalted is He, had clarified these great rulings, He said: ﴿And these are the limits of Allah﴾, i.e., His laws which He has defined, clarified and made evident, ﴿He makes them clear to a people who know﴾, because they are the ones who benefit from them and who benefit others. In this is the excellence of the people of knowledge which is not hidden, because Allah, exalted is He, made His clarification of His limits specific to them, and that they are the ones intended by it. It also indicates that Allah, exalted is He, loves from His servants knowledge of the limits of what He has sent down to His Messenger and understanding (tafaqquh) of them.

{231} Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when you divorce women﴾, i.e., a revocable divorce with one or two pronouncements, ﴿and they reach their term﴾, i.e., they approach the end of their waiting period, ﴿then either retain them in an honourable manner or release them in an honourable manner﴾, i.e., either you take them back with the intention of fulfilling their rights, or you leave them without return and without harm. For this reason He said: ﴿And do not retain them to harm them﴾, i.e., to inflict injury upon them, ﴿so that you transgress﴾ in this action of yours from the lawful to the unlawful. So the lawful is retaining with honour and the unlawful is harm. ﴿And whoever does that has wronged himself﴾. Even if the right returns to the created being, the harm returns to the one who intended the harm. ﴿And do not take the signs of Allah in jest﴾. When He, exalted is He, had clarified His limits with utmost clarity, and the intended aim was knowledge of them, acting upon them, standing by them and not transgressing them, because He, exalted is He, did not send them down in vain but sent them down with truth, sincerity and seriousness, He forbade taking them in jest, i.e., playing with them, which is presumption against them and not complying with their obligations, such as: using harm in retaining or separating, or excessive divorce, or combining the three pronouncements. Allah, in His mercy, made it one pronouncement after another, out of gentleness toward him and striving for his benefit.

﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾, generally: by the tongue in praise and commendation, by the heart in acknowledgment and affirmation, and by the limbs in employing it in obedience to Allah; ﴿and what He has sent down to you of the Book and wisdom﴾, i.e., the Sunnah, by which He has clarified for you the paths of good and made you desire them, and the paths of evil and warned you against them, and made known to you Himself and His dealings with His friends and enemies, and taught you what you did not know. It has been said that by wisdom is meant the secrets of the Sharia: the Book contains the rulings, and wisdom contains the clarification of Allah's wisdom in His commands and prohibitions. Both meanings are correct. For this reason He said: ﴿He admonishes you thereby﴾, i.e., by what He has sent down to you. This strengthens the view that by wisdom is meant the secrets of the Sharia, because admonition is by clarifying rulings and wisdom, and by encouragement or warning. The rulings clarify and remove ignorance, and wisdom together with encouragement produces desire, and wisdom together with warning produces awe. ﴿And fear Allah﴾ in all your affairs, ﴿and know that Allah is Knowing of all things﴾. Therefore He clarified these rulings for you with utmost perfection and firmness, which run in accordance with the interests in every time and place. So to Him belong praise and grace.

This is an address to the guardians of a divorced woman whose divorce was less than three pronouncements, when she has come out of her waiting period (iddah), her husband wishes to marry her again, and she consents to that. It is not permissible for her guardian, whether her father or other, to prevent her (ya'dulha, "to obstruct") from marrying him, out of spite, anger, and aversion toward what he did in the first divorce. He mentioned that whoever believes in God and the Last Day, his faith prevents him from obstructing her: ﴿That is more virtuous for you and purer﴾; and better than what the guardian may think, that not marrying her is the sound and proper opinion, and that by withholding his marriage he repays the first divorce, as is the habit of the haughty and arrogant. If he thinks that the benefit lies in not marrying her, then ﴿God knows, and you do not know﴾; so obey the One who knows your interests, who desires them, who is able to bring them about, and who facilitates them for you by ways you know and by others.

In this verse there is evidence that a guardian is necessary in marriage, because He forbade the guardians from obstructing (al-'adl), and He forbids them only from a matter that is under their management and in which they have a right. Then He, exalted is He, said:

{233} This is a statement carrying the meaning of a command, sent down as though it were an established matter that needs no command: "Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two full years." Since "hawl" (year) may refer to a complete year or to most of a year, He said: "for those who wish to complete the nursing." So when the infant has completed two years, its nursing is complete, and the milk thereafter becomes like the rest of the foods. Therefore nursing after the two years is not counted and does not establish prohibition (tahrim).

From this verse and from His saying, "And his carrying and his weaning is thirty months," it is derived that the minimum period of pregnancy is six months, and that a child can exist within it. "And upon the father of the child (al-mawlud lahu)," that is, the father, "is their provision and their clothing according to what is reasonable." This includes both the case where the mother is in his marriage and the case where she is divorced, for the father is obligated to provide for her, that is, her maintenance and clothing, and this is the wage for nursing. This indicates that if she is in his marriage, she is owed no wage other than maintenance and clothing, and each is according to his means. Therefore He said: "No soul is burdened except according to its capacity." So the poor man is not obligated to spend at the level of the rich man, nor is one who has found nothing obligated to spend until he finds something.

"No mother shall be harmed through her child, nor a father through his child": that is, it is not lawful to harm the mother on account of her child, either by preventing her from nursing him or by not giving her what is owed to her of maintenance, clothing, or wage. "Nor a father through his child": by her refusing to nurse him in a manner intended to harm [him], or by demanding more than what is obligatory, and other kinds of harm. The phrase "al-mawlud lahu" indicates that the child belongs to his father, because he is granted to him and because he is from his earnings; therefore he is permitted to take from his property whether or not she consents, unlike the mother.

His saying, "And upon the heir is the like of that," means: upon the heir of the infant if the father is absent, and if the infant has no property, is the like of what is upon the father of maintenance and clothing for the nursing mother. This indicates the obligation of maintaining indigent relatives upon the wealthy heir relative.

"If they both desire" (fa-in aradaa): that is, the two parents, "weaning" (fisalan): that is, the weaning of the child before two years, "by mutual consent from both of them" (an tarađin minhuma): that is, that both be content, "and consultation" (wa tashawur): between them, whether it is beneficial for the child or not. If it is beneficial and both are content, "there is no blame upon them" in weaning him before two years. The verse thus indicates by its implication that if one of them consents without the other, or if it is not beneficial for the child, then weaning him is not permitted.

His saying, "And if you wish to seek wet-nurses for your children" means: to seek for them nurses other than their mothers, without intent to harm, "there is no blame upon you if you pay what you give in accordance with what is reasonable" – that is, to the nurses. "And Allah is Seeing of what you do": so He will recompense you for that with good or evil.

{234} That is: when the husband dies, his wife must remain in waiting (mutarabbisa) for four months and ten days, as an obligation. The wisdom in this is that the pregnancy becomes evident within the period of four months, and movement of the fetus begins in the fifth month. This general ruling is specific to pregnant women, for their waiting period ends with the delivery of the child. Likewise, the waiting period of a slave woman is half that of a free woman: two months and five days. And His saying: ﴿And when they have reached their term﴾; that is, when their waiting period has ended, ﴿there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves﴾; that is, of beautifying themselves and using perfume, ﴿in an acceptable manner﴾; that is, in a manner that is neither prohibited nor disliked. In this is the obligation of mourning (ihdad) for the entire waiting period upon a woman whose husband has died, to the exclusion of other divorced or separated women, and this is agreed upon among the scholars. ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾; that is, He knows your deeds, outward and inward, apparent and hidden, and will recompense you for them. In His address to the guardians with His saying: ﴿there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves﴾, there is evidence that the guardian (wali) supervises the woman, prevents her from what is not permissible to do, compels her to what is obligatory, and that his being addressed with this is an obligation upon him.

{235} This is the ruling concerning a woman in her waiting period (iddah) following the death of her husband, or one who has been divorced irrevocably during his lifetime. It is forbidden for anyone other than her former husband to state explicitly to her a proposal of marriage, and this is what is meant by His words: ﴿But do not promise them secretly﴾. As for allusion (ta'ridh), God has removed blame for it, as He said:

The difference between the two is that explicit speech admits of no meaning other than marriage, and therefore it is forbidden, out of concern for hastening her and lying about the end of her waiting period in eagerness for marriage. In this there is an indication of the prohibition of the means to what is forbidden, and the fulfilment of the right of her first husband by not promising her to another during her waiting period. As for allusion (ta'ridh), which admits of marriage and other than marriage, it is permitted to the irrevocably divorced woman, such as a man saying [to her]: "I intend to marry, and I would love for you to consult me when your waiting period ends," and similar words. This is permitted, because it is not of the same status as explicit speech, and within souls there is a strong inclination toward it. Likewise is a person's concealing within himself the intention to marry someone who is in her waiting period once it has ended. For this reason He said: ﴿Or you concealed within yourselves. God knows that you will remember them﴾.

This whole detail concerns preliminary proposals; as for the contract of marriage, it is not lawful, ﴿until the decreed term reaches its end﴾; that is, until the waiting period is completed.

﴿And know that God knows what is in your souls﴾; that is, intend good and do not intend evil, out of fear of His punishment and hope for His reward. ﴿And know that God is Forgiving﴾ to whoever has committed sins and then repented of them and returned to his Lord, ﴿Forbearing﴾; in that He does not hasten to punish the disobedient for their disobedience, despite His power over them.

{236} That is: there is no blame or sin upon you, O husbands, in divorcing women before consummation and before the dower has been fixed, even though this may cause them some hurt. Their hurt is made good by the provision (mut'ah), so you must provide for them, by giving them some wealth to comfort their hearts: {according to the wealthy man's means and according to the poor man's means}; that is, the one in straitened circumstances, {according to his means}. This returns to what is customary, and it varies with the circumstances, which is why He said: {a provision in accordance with what is reasonable}; this is an obligatory right {upon the doers of good}, who are not to diminish it for them. Since they caused them to hope, to long, and to have their hearts attached, and then did not give them what they desired, they must, in return for that, give them the provision (mut'ah).

How excellent is this divine ruling, and how clearly it points to the wisdom and mercy of the One who legislated it! And who is better than Allah in judgment for a people who are certain?

This is the ruling concerning divorced women before consummation and before the dower has been fixed. Then he mentioned the ruling concerning those for whom a dower has been fixed, saying:

{237} That is: if you divorce women before consummation and after the dowry has been fixed, then the divorced women are entitled to half of the dowry fixed, and you are entitled to the other half. This is the obligation, unless there is pardon and forgiveness in it, by which she forgoes her half for her husband, if her forgiveness is valid. ﴿Or the one in whose hand is the marriage tie﴾; this is the husband according to the correct view, because he is the one in whose hand is the dissolution of its tie. Also, the guardian's pardon is not valid concerning what is owed to the woman, because he is neither its owner nor its agent. It was said that it refers to the father, and this is what the wording of the noble verse indicates.

Then he encouraged pardon, and that whoever pardons is nearer to piety, because it is a kindness that brings about expansion of the breast, and because a person should not neglect himself from kindness and good conduct, and forget the favour, which is the highest level of dealing. For people's dealings among themselves are of two degrees: either justice and equity, which is obligatory, namely taking what is due and giving what is due; or favour and kindness, which is giving what is not obligatory and being lenient regarding rights and restraining what is in the self. So a person should not forget this degree, even at some times, especially toward those with whom you have dealings or association. For indeed Allah rewards the doers of good with favour and generosity. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾ Then He, the Exalted, said:

{238} He, exalted is He, commands the preservation of "the prayers," in general, and of "the middle prayer," in particular, which is the 'Asr prayer. Preserving it means performing it at its proper time, with its conditions, its pillars, its humility (khushu'), and all that belongs to it of obligatory and recommended acts. By preserving the prayers one attains the preservation of all other acts of worship, and it brings about the prohibition of indecency and wrongdoing, especially when one perfects it as He commands in His words: ﴿And stand before Allah in devotion﴾; that is, humbled, sincere, and submissive, for qunut (devout obedience) is the continuance of obedience together with humility.

{239} His words "if you fear" omit the object of the fear so that it includes fear of an enemy, of a beast, and of the loss of anything whose loss harms the servant. ﴿Then pray on foot﴾, walking on your feet, ﴿or riding﴾, on horses, camels, and all other mounts. In this state, facing the qibla is not obligatory. This is the description of the prayer of one excused due to fear. When security is restored, he should pray the complete prayer. Included in His words ﴿then remember Allah when you are secure﴾ is the completion of the prayers. Also included is the abundant remembrance of Allah, in thanks for the blessing of security and for the blessing of teaching, which is what brings the servant happiness.

In the noble verse there is the virtue of knowledge, and that upon the one whom Allah has taught what he did not know is to remember Allah abundantly. It also indicates that abundant remembrance of Him is a cause for being taught other sciences, because thanks is linked with increase. Then He, exalted is He, said:

It also indicates that abundant remembrance of Him is a cause for being taught other sciences, because thanks is linked with increase. Then He, exalted is He, said:

{240} It is well known among many exegetes that this noble verse was abrogated (naskh) by the verse preceding it, namely His saying, exalted is He: {Those of you who die and leave wives behind - they, the wives, shall wait four months and ten days}. They say that the ruling was that the wife must observe a full year (ḥawl kāmil), and that this was abrogated by four months and ten days. As for the fact that the abrogating verse comes first, they answer that this precedence is in the order of arrangement (al-waḍʿ), not in the order of revelation (al-nuzūl), because a condition of the abrogating text (nāsikh) is that it be later than the abrogated text (mansūkh). But this view has no evidence to support it. Whoever reflects on the two verses will see clearly that the other opinion regarding this verse is the correct one: the first verse concerns the obligation of waiting four months and ten days, in the sense of a binding requirement upon the woman, whereas this verse is a bequest (waṣiyya) to the family of the deceased that they keep the deceased's wife with them for a full year, as a way of consoling her and showing kindness to their deceased relative. For this reason He said: {A bequest for their wives}; that is, a bequest from God to the family of the deceased that they treat the wife well, provide for her maintenance (yumattiʿūhā), and not expel her. If she wishes, she may remain in fulfillment of the bequest; and if she wishes to leave, there is no blame upon her. For this reason He said: {But if they leave, there is no blame on you for what they do with themselves}; that is, regarding adornment (tajammul) and clothing, provided that it is in accordance with what is acceptable (al-maʿrūf), which does not take her beyond the bounds of religion and propriety. He concluded the verse with these two great names, which indicate perfect might (ʿizza) and perfect wisdom (ḥikma), because these are rulings that issued from His might, and they demonstrate the perfection of His wisdom in placing them in their fitting positions.

{241–242} Having explained in the previous verse the provision (mut'ah) for a woman who is separated by death, He here mentions that every divorced woman is owed by her husband a provision, that he should give her what suits his circumstances and hers. This is a right which only the God-fearing (al-muttaqun) carry out, so it is among the qualities of taqwa (God-consciousness), whether obligatory or recommended. If a woman was not assigned a dowry (sadaq) and he divorces her before consummation, it has already been stated that he is obliged to provide according to his means and his straitness. If a dowry was assigned to her, her provision is half of the assigned dowry. If she has been consummated, the provision becomes recommended according to the opinion of the majority of scholars, while some scholars held it obligatory, relying on His saying: ﴿a right upon the God-conscious﴾. The basic meaning of "right" (haqq) is that it is obligatory, especially since He attributed it to the God-conscious, and the essence of taqwa is obligatory. When the Exalted explained these weighty rulings concerning the spouses, He praised His rulings, His clarification and elucidation of them, and their agreement with sound intellects, and that the purpose of His explaining them to His servants is that they should understand from Him what He has made clear, so they comprehend them, memorize them, grasp them, and act upon them, for that is the completion of their reason ('aql).

{243} That is: Have you not heard of this wondrous story that happened to those before you, the Children of Israel, when a plague struck their homes, and they went out in such great numbers fleeing from death? Flight did not save them, nor did it avail them against the occurrence of what they were wary of. So He dealt with them in the opposite of what they intended, and God caused them all to die. Then He bestowed His favour upon them and brought them back to life, either by the supplication of a prophet, as many of the exegetes have said, or by other means. But that was by His bounty and kindness, and His favour upon people is ever continuous, and that necessitates their gratitude for God's blessings by acknowledging them and expending them in what pleases God. Yet most people have fallen short in the obligation of gratitude.

In this story is a lesson that He is powerful over all things, and it is a tangible sign of the Resurrection; for this story is well known and transmitted by mass transmission (tawatur) among the Children of Israel and those connected with them. For this reason, God related it in the form of a command, which is established among the addressees. It is also possible that those who went out of their homes did so out of fear of enemies and cowardice in facing them. This is supported by the fact that God mentioned after it the command to fight, and informed about the Children of Israel that they had been expelled from their homes and their sons. In both interpretations, there is encouragement toward jihad and a warning against shirking from it, and that flight does not avail against death at all.

{قل لو كنتم في بيوتكم لبرز الذين كتب عليهم القتل إلى مضاجعهم}
["Say: Even if you had been in your houses, those decreed to be slain would have come forth to their places of death."]

Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verses 244–245:

{244–245} Allah combined the command to fight in His cause with both wealth and person, because jihad cannot be established except with both. He urged sincerity in it, that the servant fight so that the word of Allah may be the highest. Indeed, Allah is {All-Hearing} of statements, even if they are concealed, and {All-Knowing} of what the hearts contain of good intentions and their opposites. Furthermore, when the one who strives in His cause knows that Allah is All-Hearing and All-Knowing, it becomes easier for him, and he knows that Allah surely knows exactly what those who bear hardships bear for His sake, and that He will certainly support them with His help and His kindness.

Consider this gentle urging to spend, and that the one who spends has lent to Allah, the Rich and Generous, who promised him multiplication, many times over, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a seed that grows seven spikes; in every spike is a hundred grains. And Allah multiplies for whom He wills. And Allah is All-Encompassing and All-Knowing.﴾

And since the greatest obstacle to spending is the fear of poverty, Allah, the Exalted, informed that wealth and poverty are in the hand of Allah, and that He withholds provision from whom He wills and extends it to whom He wills. So the one who wants to spend should not hold back out of fear of poverty, nor think that his spending is lost. Rather, the return of all servants is to Allah, and those who spend and those who work will find their reward with Him, stored up, at a time when they need it most, and it will have a tremendous effect that cannot be described.

By "the goodly loan" is meant that which combines the qualities of goodness: a good intention, a generous soul in spending, the spending being placed in its proper place, and that the spender does not follow it with reproach, harm, or nullifying and diminishing it.
