God recounts this story to the Muslim community so that they may take heed, be eager for jihad (struggle in the way of God), and not shrink from it. Those who are patient attain good outcomes in this world and the next, while those who shrink back lose both. God informs us that the people of judgment and authority among the Children of Israel consulted together about jihad and agreed to ask their prophet to appoint a king for them, so that disputes would end with his appointment, complete obedience would be achieved, and no one would have any objection to make. Their prophet feared that this request was mere words without action behind it. They answered him with firm resolve and fully committed themselves to it. Fighting became obligatory upon them, since it was the means of recovering their homes and returning to their settlement and homeland. Their prophet appointed Talut (Saul) as king to lead them in this matter, for a campaign must have a leader who manages it well. They were surprised at his appointment, since there were others more worthy than him by lineage and wealthier. Their prophet answered them: "God has chosen him over you, and has given him breadth of knowledge in statecraft and physical strength, which are the instruments of courage, valor and sound management. Kingship does not depend on abundant wealth, nor on its holder being from a family that has held power and leadership." "God gives His kingdom to whom He wills."

Then that noble prophet did not stop at persuading them with the qualifications of Talut and the combination of the required attributes in him. He said to them:

﴿Indeed, the sign of his kingship is that the chest (al-tabut) will come to you, containing tranquility from your Lord and remnants left by the family of Moses and the family of Aaron﴾.

This chest had been seized by the enemies. They were not satisfied with the inner qualities of Talut, nor with God's appointment of him through the tongue of their prophet, so this miracle was to confirm it. Hence He said: ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign for you, if you are believers﴾. At that point they submitted and obeyed. When Talut took command over them, arranged their troops and ranks, and set out with them to fight their enemy, he saw among them such weakness of resolve and determination that a test was needed to separate the patient from the one who shrinks back. So he said:

﴿Indeed, God is going to test you with a river﴾,
which you will pass at a time when you need water. ﴿Whoever drinks from it is not of me﴾, meaning he does not follow me, because that is evidence of little patience and excessive impatience. ﴿And whoever does not taste it is of me﴾, for his sincerity and patience. ﴿Except one who takes a handful with his hand﴾, meaning that he is excused in that. When they reached that river and were in need of water, they all drank from it ﴿except a few of them﴾, who were patient and did not drink. ﴿When he crossed it, along with those who believed with him, they said﴾, meaning: the ones who shrank back, or those who crossed: ﴿We have no strength today against Jalut (Goliath) and his troops﴾. If those who spoke were the ones who shrank back, then this is a statement by which they justify their backing out. If those who spoke were those who crossed with Talut, then a kind of self-belittlement had occurred among them. But those of complete faith encouraged them to stand firm and advance, saying: ﴿How many a small company has overcome a large company by the permission of God; and God is with the patient﴾, meaning with His help, support and victory. So they stood firm and were patient in fighting their enemy, Jalut and his troops.

﴿And David killed Jalut﴾ (peace be upon him). Thereby came conquest and victory over their enemy. ﴿And God gave him the kingdom and wisdom﴾, meaning David: prophethood, beneficial knowledge, and wisdom and decisive speech. Then God explained the benefit of jihad, saying: ﴿Had God not repelled some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted﴾, by the domination of disbelievers, the wicked and the people of evil and corruption. ﴿But God is full of bounty to the worlds﴾, in that He is gentle with the believers and defends them and their religion through what He has legislated and what He has decreed. When He had explained this story, He said to His Messenger (peace be upon him):

﴿These are the verses of God, which We recite to you in truth, and indeed you are among the messengers﴾.

Among the proofs of his messengership is this story, as he related it by revelation from God, in accordance with the reality.

In this story there are many lessons for the community:

Among them: the virtue of jihad in His cause, its benefits and fruits, and that it is the sole means of preserving religion, homelands, bodies and wealth. Those who strive, even if matters are hard for them, have good outcomes, just as those who shrink back, even if they rest a little, will suffer for a long time.

Among them: appointing to leadership the one who has the competence, and that competence rests on two things: knowledge, which is the knowledge of politics and management, and strength, by which the truth is enforced. Whoever combines both is more worthy than others.

Among them: the use of this story to support what the scholars have said, that a commander of armies should inspect them at their assembly points, and prevent from fighting those who are unfit, whether men, horses or riders, because of weakness, weak patience, discouragement, or fear of harm from their company, for such a category is pure harm to the people.

Among them: that when the time of severe danger arrives, it is necessary to strengthen the fighters, encourage them, urge them toward faith-based strength, complete reliance upon God and dependence upon Him, and ask God for steadfastness, help in patience, and victory over the enemies.

Among them: that the resolve to fight and to strive is not the same as its reality. A person may resolve, but when the moment comes his resolve may dissolve. For this reason, among the supplications of the Prophet (peace be upon him) is: "I ask You for steadfastness in the matter and resolve upon right guidance." Those who resolved to fight and spoke words indicating firm determination, yet when the time came most of them backed out. Similar to this is his saying (peace be upon him): "And I ask You for contentment after the decree." For contentment after the occurrence of a decree that is hateful to the souls is the true contentment.

Then God explained the benefit of jihad, saying: ﴿Had God not repelled some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted﴾, by the domination of disbelievers, the wicked and the people of evil and corruption. ﴿But God is full of bounty to the worlds﴾, in that He is gentle with the believers and defends them and their religion through what He has legislated and what He has decreed. When He had explained this story, He said to His Messenger (peace be upon him):

﴿These are the verses of God, which We recite to you in truth, and indeed you are among the messengers﴾.

Among the proofs of his messengership is this story, as he related it by revelation from God, in accordance with the reality.

In this story there are many lessons for the community:

Among them: the virtue of jihad in His cause, its benefits and fruits, and that it is the sole means of preserving religion, homelands, bodies and wealth. Those who strive, even if matters are hard for them, have good outcomes, just as those who shrink back, even if they rest a little, will suffer for a long time.

Among them: appointing to leadership the one who has the competence, and that competence rests on two things: knowledge, which is the knowledge of politics and management, and strength, by which the truth is enforced. Whoever combines both is more worthy than others.

Among them: the use of this story to support what the scholars have said, that a commander of armies should inspect them at their assembly points, and prevent from fighting those who are unfit, whether men, horses or riders, because of weakness, weak patience, discouragement, or fear of harm from their company, for such a category is pure harm to the people.

Among them: that when the time of severe danger arrives, it is necessary to strengthen the fighters, encourage them, urge them toward faith-based strength, complete reliance upon God and dependence upon Him, and ask God for steadfastness, help in patience, and victory over the enemies.

Among them: that the resolve to fight and to strive is not the same as its reality. A person may resolve, but when the moment comes his resolve may dissolve. For this reason, among the supplications of the Prophet (peace be upon him) is: "I ask You for steadfastness in the matter and resolve upon right guidance." Those who resolved to fight and spoke words indicating firm determination, yet when the time came most of them backed out. Similar to this is his saying (peace be upon him): "And I ask You for contentment after the decree." For contentment after the occurrence of a decree that is hateful to the souls is the true contentment.

God recounts this story to the Muslim community so that they may take heed, be eager for jihad (struggle in the way of God), and not shrink from it. Those who are patient attain good outcomes in this world and the next, while those who shrink back lose both. God informs us that the people of judgment and authority among the Children of Israel consulted together about jihad and agreed to ask their prophet to appoint a king for them, so that disputes would end with his appointment, complete obedience would be achieved, and no one would have any objection to make. Their prophet feared that this request was mere words without action behind it. They answered him with firm resolve and fully committed themselves to it. Fighting became obligatory upon them, since it was the means of recovering their homes and returning to their settlement and homeland. Their prophet appointed Talut (Saul) as king to lead them in this matter, for a campaign must have a leader who manages it well. They were surprised at his appointment, since there were others more worthy than him by lineage and wealthier. Their prophet answered them: "God has chosen him over you, and has given him breadth of knowledge in statecraft and physical strength, which are the instruments of courage, valor and sound management. Kingship does not depend on abundant wealth, nor on its holder being from a family that has held power and leadership." "God gives His kingdom to whom He wills."

Then that noble prophet did not stop at persuading them with the qualifications of Talut and the combination of the required attributes in him. He said to them:

﴿Indeed, the sign of his kingship is that the chest (al-tabut) will come to you, containing tranquility from your Lord and remnants left by the family of Moses and the family of Aaron﴾.

This chest had been seized by the enemies. They were not satisfied with the inner qualities of Talut, nor with God's appointment of him through the tongue of their prophet, so this miracle was to confirm it. Hence He said: ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign for you, if you are believers﴾. At that point they submitted and obeyed. When Talut took command over them, arranged their troops and ranks, and set out with them to fight their enemy, he saw among them such weakness of resolve and determination that a test was needed to separate the patient from the one who shrinks back. So he said:

﴿Indeed, God is going to test you with a river﴾,
which you will pass at a time when you need water. ﴿Whoever drinks from it is not of me﴾, meaning he does not follow me, because that is evidence of little patience and excessive impatience. ﴿And whoever does not taste it is of me﴾, for his sincerity and patience. ﴿Except one who takes a handful with his hand﴾, meaning that he is excused in that. When they reached that river and were in need of water, they all drank from it ﴿except a few of them﴾, who were patient and did not drink. ﴿When he crossed it, along with those who believed with him, they said﴾, meaning: the ones who shrank back, or those who crossed: ﴿We have no strength today against Jalut (Goliath) and his troops﴾. If those who spoke were the ones who shrank back, then this is a statement by which they justify their backing out. If those who spoke were those who crossed with Talut, then a kind of self-belittlement had occurred among them. But those of complete faith encouraged them to stand firm and advance, saying: ﴿How many a small company has overcome a large company by the permission of God; and God is with the patient﴾, meaning with His help, support and victory. So they stood firm and were patient in fighting their enemy, Jalut and his troops.

{253} The Creator informs that He has differentiated among the Messengers in their sublime virtues and their beautiful distinctions, according to what Allah bestowed upon them and what they upheld of complete faith, firm certainty, lofty character, exalted manners, the call (to Allah), teaching, and abundant benefit. Among them is the one whom He took as a close friend (khalil), and among them is the one to whom He spoke directly (kallama taklima), and among them is the one whom He raised above the creation by degrees. All of them, no human can reach their lofty virtue. And He singled out ʿIsa ibn Maryam, in that He gave him clear signs that show he was truly the Messenger of Allah, His servant in truth, and that what he brought was entirely from Allah and true. So He made him heal the blind and the leper and raise the dead by Allah's permission, and he spoke to people while in the cradle as a child. And He strengthened him with the Holy Spirit (ruh al-qudus), that is, the Spirit of faith, and He made his spirituality surpass the spirituality of others, so he gained through it strength and support. Although the basic support through this Spirit is general to every believer according to his faith, as He said: ﴿And He strengthened them with a Spirit from Himself﴾; yet what ʿIsa had is greater than what others had, and for this reason Allah singled him out by mention. It has been said that the Holy Spirit here is Jibril, whom Allah strengthened by his help and support, but the meaning is the first.

When He had informed of the perfection of the Messengers and what He gave them of virtue and distinctions, and that their religion is one and their call to good is one, and the consequence and requirement of that would be that the nations unite in affirming them and submitting to them, because of the clear signs He gave them, by the likes of which mankind believes, yet most of them deviated from the straight path, and disagreement arose among the nations, so some of them believed and some of them disbelieved, and fighting occurred because of that, which is the necessary result of disagreement and hostility. Had Allah willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance, and they would not have differed. And had Allah willed, after the disagreement that necessitated fighting had occurred, they would not have fought. But His wisdom required that affairs proceed in this order according to causes.

In this verse is the greatest evidence that He, the Exalted, disposes all the causes that necessitate their effects, and that if He wills He sustains them, and if He wills He prevents them, and all of that follows His wisdom alone, for He does whatever He intends. There is no one who can prevent His will and purpose, none who opposes it, and none who assists it.

Allah urges the believers to spend in every avenue of good, because omitting the object (of the verb) indicates generality. He also reminds them of His blessing upon them, that it is He who provided for them and diversified blessings for them, and that He did not command them to give away everything in their hands, but rather used "min" (from), which indicates partiality. This is among the things that calls them to spending. Also among the things that calls them to it is informing them that these expenditures are stored up with Allah for a Day on which exchanges by sale and the like are of no benefit, nor voluntary gifts, nor intercession. Every person will say, "What have I sent forward for my life?" Thus all means will be severed except the means connected to obedience to Allah and belief in Him, on a Day when neither wealth nor children will benefit, except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart. ﴿And it is not your wealth nor your children that bring you near to Us in position, except one who believes and does righteous deeds; those will have the recompense of double for what they did, and they will be in the upper chambers, secure.﴾ ﴿And whatever good you send forward for yourselves, you will find it with Allah, better and greater in reward.﴾ Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And the disbelievers—they are the wrongdoers.﴾ That is because Allah created them for His worship, provided for them, and granted them well-being, so that they might use that to aid them in His obedience. Instead, they departed from what Allah created them for, associated with Allah that for which He had sent down no authority, and used His blessings to aid them in disbelief, defiance, and disobedience. Thus they left no place for justice, and so absolute wrongdoing was restricted to them.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 255:

{255} The Prophet (ﷺ) informed that this verse is the greatest verse of the Qur'an because of what it contains of the meanings of tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness), greatness, and the vastness of the attributes of the Creator, exalted is He. He informed that He is {Allah}, the One who possesses all the meanings of divinity (uluhiyyah), and that none deserves divinity and worship except Him; so the divinity of any other and the worship of any other is false. And He is {the Ever-Living} (al-Hayy), who possesses all the meanings of perfect life, including hearing, seeing, power, will, and the other essential attributes. Likewise {the Self-Subsisting} (al-Qayyum) encompasses all the attributes of action, because He is the Self-Subsisting who subsists by Himself and is free of need of all His creatures, and who sustains all existing things, bringing them into being, preserving them, and supplying them with everything they need for their existence and their continuance. And from the perfection of His life and His self-subsistence is that {neither drowsiness overtakes Him}; that is, slumber, {nor sleep}; because drowsiness and sleep only befall the created being who is subject to weakness, incapacity, and dissolution, and they do not befall the One possessing greatness, majesty, and glory. He also informed that He is the Owner of all that is in the heavens and the earth, so they are all servants and possessions belonging to Allah; none of them goes outside this condition: {There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant} (Qur'an 19:93). He is the Owner of all dominions, and He possesses the attributes of kingship, disposal, authority, and majesty. And from the completeness of His dominion is that no one {intercedes with Him} {except by His permission}; so all the dignitaries and intercessors are servants and possessions of His, who do not venture to intercede until He permits them: {Say: To Allah belongs all intercession. His is the dominion of the heavens and the earth} (Qur'an 39:44). Allah does not permit anyone to intercede except for those whom He approves, and He approves only of their affirming His oneness and following His messengers; so whoever does not possess this has no share in intercession. Then He informed of His vast and all-encompassing knowledge, and that He knows what is before the creatures of matters yet to come, which have no end, {and what is behind them}, of past matters, which have no limit; and that nothing is hidden from Him: {He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal} (Qur'an 40:19). The creatures cannot encompass anything of Allah's knowledge or His objects of knowledge {except what He wills} of them, namely what He has made them aware of of legislative and decreed matters. This is a very small portion, utterly insignificant compared to the sciences and objects of knowledge of the Creator, as the one most knowledgeable of Him among creation, namely the messengers and the angels, said: {Glory be to You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us} (Qur'an 2:32). Then He informed of His greatness and majesty, and that His Chair (Kursi) encompasses the heavens and the earth, and that He has preserved them and whoever is in them of worlds through the causes and systems which Allah placed in the creatures; yet preserving them does not burden Him, because of the perfection of His greatness, His power, and the vastness of His wisdom in His judgments. {And He is the Most High} (al-Ali) in His essence above all His creatures, and He is the Most High in the greatness of His attributes, and He is the Most High who has subdued the creatures, to whom all existing things are subject, to whom hard things submit, and before whom necks are humbled. {The Mighty} (al-Azim), who combines all attributes of greatness, majesty, glory, and splendor, whom hearts love, and whom souls magnify; and those who know Him recognize that the greatness of everything, however sublime it may be in description, is nonetheless diminished beside the greatness of the Most High, the Mighty. Thus, a verse that contains these meanings, which are the most sublime of meanings, is fittingly the greatest verse of the Qur'an, and it is fitting that whoever recites it reflectively and with understanding should have his heart filled with certainty, recognition, and faith, and should be protected thereby from the evils of Satan.

{256} This is an explanation of the perfection of this Islamic religion, and that it is perfect in its proofs, clear in its signs, and that it is the religion of reason and knowledge, the religion of natural disposition (fitrah) and wisdom, the religion of righteousness and reform, and the religion of truth and right guidance. Because of its perfection and because natural dispositions accept it, it has no need for compulsion to be imposed upon it, for compulsion only occurs with regard to that which hearts recoil from and which contradicts reality and truth, or with regard to that whose proofs and signs are obscure. Otherwise, whoever receives this religion and rejects it and does not accept it, it is due to his obstinacy, for ﴿the right course has become clear from error﴾. So no one has any excuse or argument if he rejects it and does not accept it.

There is no contradiction between this meaning and the many verses that make jihad obligatory, for God commanded fighting so that the religion would be entirely for God, and to repel the aggression of aggressors against the religion. The Muslims have agreed that jihad continues alongside both the righteous and the wicked ruler, and that both verbal jihad and physical jihad are among the continuous obligations. As for those among the exegetes who thought that this verse contradicts the verses of jihad and therefore decided that it is abrogated (mansukh), his view is weak in wording and meaning, as is clear to anyone who reflects on the noble verse, as we have pointed out.

Then God mentioned the division of people into two categories: a category that believed in God alone, with no partner, and disbelieved in the taghut, which is everything that contradicts belief in God, such as polytheism and other things. This one has ﴿grasped the most trustworthy handhold﴾ which has no breaking, and indeed he is upright upon the correct religion until it brings him to God and to the abode of His honor. The second category is understood from the implication of the verse: whoever does not believe in God, but disbelieves in Him and believes in the taghut, will perish an everlasting perdition and be punished with a perpetual punishment. As for His saying ﴿And God is Hearing﴾, meaning: He hears all voices in their differing languages and varied needs, and He hears the supplications of those who call upon Him and the humility of the supplicants. ﴿Knowing﴾: of what the breasts conceal and what is hidden of the secrets of affairs, so He recompenses each person according to what He knows of his intentions and deeds.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 257:

{257} This verse is connected to the verse before it: the previous one is the foundation, and this one is the fruit. He, may He be exalted, informs that those who believe in Allah and make their faith true by performing the duties of faith and abandoning everything that contradicts it, Allah is their Wali (Protector), who takes them under His special protection and oversees their upbringing. He brings them out of the darkness of ignorance, disbelief, sins, heedlessness and turning away, into the light of knowledge, certainty, faith, obedience and complete turning toward their Lord. He illuminates their hearts with what He casts into them of the light of revelation and faith, He makes easy for them the ease (al-yusra), and He keeps them away from the hardship (al-usra). As for those who disbelieve, since they took as their guardians other than their true Wali, Allah leaves them to what they have taken for themselves, forsakes them, and entrusts them to the care of those they took as guardians, who possess neither benefit nor harm. So those guardians misguide them and bring them to misery, and deprive them of the guidance of beneficial knowledge and righteous action, and deprive them of happiness, and the Fire becomes their abode, wherein they abide forever. O Allah, make us Your protégés among those whom You have taken as protégés.

Ibn Sa'di's commentary on Surah 2, verse 258:

{258} Allah relates to us, from the accounts of the messengers and the earlier peoples, that by which the realities become clear and the various proofs for monotheism (tawhid) are established. So He, exalted is He, informs us about His intimate friend (khalil) Ibrahim, peace be upon him, when he argued with this tyrannical king, who was Nimrod the Babylonian, the one who denied and rejected the Lord of the worlds. He undertook to oppose Ibrahim the Friend and to dispute with him on this matter which admits of no doubt, no ambiguity, and no uncertainty, namely the oneness of Allah and His lordship, which is the most manifest and clear of matters. But this tyrant was deceived by his kingship and his arrogance led him to the point that he rejected [Allah]. He argued with Ibrahim, the great messenger whom Allah had granted knowledge and certainty greater than that granted to any of the messengers other than Muhammad, peace be upon him. So Ibrahim said, as a debater with him: {My Lord is He who gives life and causes death}; that is, He alone is the one who creates, disposes, gives life and causes death. He mentioned the most apparent of this kind, which is giving life and causing death. Then that tyrant said, in confusion: {I give life and cause death}; by this he meant: I kill whomever I wish to kill and spare whomever I wish to spare. It is well known that this is a deception and a distortion away from the intended point, and that the intended point is that Allah, exalted is He, alone brings life into the non-existent and restores it to the dead, and that He is the one who causes the servants and the animals to die at their appointed terms, by means of causes He has linked to death and without causes.

When the Friend saw him resorting to a deception that might pass over the ignorant and the common folk, Ibrahim said, binding him to affirm his statement if it were as he claimed: {Indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west}; then {the one who disbelieved was confounded}; that is, he stood still, his argument was cut off, and his doubt was dispelled.

This is not Ibrahim moving from one proof to another; rather it is a compelling challenge to Nimrod to extend his own argument, if he were truthful, and bring [the sun from the west], which admits of no fabrication, distortion, or deception. All the proofs, revealed, rational and innate, bear witness to the oneness of Allah, acknowledging His sole creation and governance, and that whoever has this attribute deserves worship only from Him. All the messengers agree upon this great foundation, and none denies it except a stubborn, arrogant person like this obstinate tyrant. Thus this is among the proofs of tawhid. Then [Allah] mentioned the proofs of complete power, resurrection, and recompense, saying:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 259–260:

{259} These are two great and tangible proofs in this world, before the Hereafter, of the Resurrection (al-ba'th) and of recompense. The first was performed by God at the hand of a man who doubted the Resurrection, according to the sound view, as the noble verse indicates. The second was performed at the hand of His intimate friend Ibrahim, just as the proof of Tawhid (Divine Oneness) mentioned earlier was performed at his hand. This man passed by a town that had been utterly destroyed, fallen upon its roofs, its people dead and its buildings in ruins. He said, in a manner of doubt and disbelief: ﴿How will Allah bring this to life after its death?﴾ That is, it is far-fetched while it is in this state, and likewise anything else like it, according to what arose in his heart at that moment. So Allah, in His mercy towards him and towards the people, caused him to die for a hundred years, and he had with him a donkey, which He caused to die with him, and with him food and drink, which Allah preserved in their state throughout all these long periods. When the hundred years had passed, He resurrected him and said: ﴿How long have you remained?﴾ He said: ﴿I have remained a day or part of a day﴾, according to what he supposed. Allah said: ﴿Rather, you have remained a hundred years.﴾ And it is apparent that this exchange was through one of the noble prophets.

And among the completeness of Allah's mercy towards him and towards the people is that He showed him the sign directly, so that he might be convinced by it. After he knew that he had been dead, Allah brought him back to life, and it was said to him: Look ﴿at your food and your drink, they have not spoiled﴾; that is, they had not changed over these long periods. This is one of the signs of Allah's power, for food and drink, especially what the exegetes mentioned as fruit and juice, do not remain unchanged for long, yet this was preserved by Allah for a hundred years. It was said to him: ﴿Look at your donkey﴾; and behold, it had been torn apart and scattered and had become decayed bones. ﴿And look at the bones, how We raise them﴾; that is, how We lift some of them up to others and join some of them to others after they had been scattered and torn apart, ﴿then We clothe them﴾; after their reassembly, ﴿with flesh﴾; then We restore life to them. ﴿So when it became clear to him﴾; by direct sight that admits no doubt in any way, ﴿he said: I know that Allah is over all things competent.﴾ So he acknowledged Allah's power over all things, and he became a sign for the people, for they had known of his death and the death of his donkey, and they had known his situation, then they witnessed this great sign. Then His words ﴿So when it became clear to him﴾ are explicit that it did not become clear to him except after he had witnessed this state, which indicates the completeness of His power by direct sight.

{260} As for the other proof, Ibrahim said, seeking from Allah that He show him how He gives life to the dead. Allah said to him: ﴿Have you not believed?﴾, to remove doubt from His intimate friend. ﴿He said﴾: Ibrahim: ﴿Yes﴾; O Lord, I have believed that You are over all things competent, and that You give life to the dead and recompense the servants; but I want my heart to be reassured and to reach the level of the certainty of sight. So Allah answered his supplication, as an honour to him and a mercy to the servants. ﴿He said: Take four birds﴾; and He did not specify which kinds of birds they were, since the sign is achieved with any type of them, and that is the aim. ﴿Then make them incline towards you﴾; that is, gather them to yourself, slaughter them and tear them apart. ﴿Then put on every mountain a portion of them, then call them, they will come to you in haste. This also contains an alert that in the Resurrection the complete might, wisdom, greatness, vast dominion, and perfect justice and grace of Allah become manifest to the servants.

{261} This is a great exhortation from God to His servants to spend their wealth in His way, which is the path that leads to Him. Included in this is spending on the advancement of beneficial knowledge, on preparation for jihad in His way, on equipping the mujahideen and outfitting them, and on all beneficial charitable projects for the Muslims. Next in rank is spending on the needy, the poor, and the destitute. Both aims may combine, so that the expenditure both meets needs and aids good deeds and acts of obedience. These expenditures are multiplied by this multiplication: seven hundred times, and to many times beyond that. This is why He said: ﴿And God multiplies [the reward] for whom He wills﴾. This varies according to what is present in the heart of the spender of faith, complete sincerity, and in the fruits and benefit of his expenditure, for some avenues of goodness entail a chain of benefits and diverse interests, so the reward is of the same kind as the deed.

{262} Then He mentions another reward for those who spend their wealth in His way, with an expenditure issued in full compliance with its conditions and free of its impediments. They do not follow their spending with reminders of their favor upon the recipient, nor with boasting of blessings, nor with harm to him, whether by word or deed. For these ﴿there is their reward with their Lord﴾, in accordance with what He knows of them, in accordance with their expenditures and their benefit, and by His bounty, which their charities cannot reach or attain. ﴿No fear will there be upon them, nor will they grieve﴾. He negated for them the past disliked matter by negating grief, and the future by negating fear for them. Thus they have attained what they love, and what they dislike has been repelled from them.

{263} God mentioned four levels of ihsan (doing good):

The highest level: spending that proceeds from a good intention, and which the giver does not follow with reminders of favor (mann) or with harm (adha).

Next after it is kind speech (qawl al-ma'ruf), which is beneficence in speech in all its forms that brings joy to the Muslim, and apologizing to the beggar when one does not have anything to give him, and other kinds of kind speech.

The third is beneficence through pardon and forgiveness toward one who has wronged you by word or deed.

These two are better than the fourth and superior to it. The fourth is that in which the giver follows his charity with harm to the recipient, for this spoils his beneficence. Such a person has done both good and evil.

Pure good, even if it is of lesser rank, is better than good mixed with evil, even if it is of greater rank. In this there is a great warning to whoever harms the one he gives charity to, as the people of meanness, folly and ignorance do. {And God} is {Ghani} (Self-Sufficient), {exalted}, free of need for their charity and for all of His servants, {Halim} (Forbearing): despite His complete self-sufficiency and vast bounty, He forbears toward the disobedient, does not hasten to punish them, but rather grants them well-being, provides for them, and pours out His goodness upon them, while they are defying Him through their sins.

Then He forbade in the strongest terms reminding of favor and causing harm, and He gave an example for that:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 264–266:

{264 – 266} God struck three examples in these verses: for the one who spends seeking His face and does not follow his spending with reminders of kindness or harm, for the one who follows it with reminders and harm, and for the one who does it to be seen (al-mura'i).

As for the first, since his spending is accepted and multiplied, because it proceeds from faith and complete sincerity, {seeking the pleasure of Allah and steadfastness of their souls}; that is: they spend while being firm in generosity and truthfulness. The likeness of such a deed is {like a garden on a height}; and this is an elevated place, because it is exposed to the winds and the sun, and its water is abundant. If the heavy rain does not reach it, a light rain suffices for it, because of the goodness of its soil, the excellence of its land, and the availability of all the abundant causes of its growth, flourishing and fruiting. Therefore {it yields its produce twofold}; that is, multiplied. This garden with this description is the best thing people seek, so this deed is in the highest of ranks.

As for the one who spends for Allah and then follows his spending with reminders of kindness and harm, or does a deed and then does something that nullifies it, his likeness is the likeness of the owner of this garden, but {a whirlwind} was sent against it; that is, a strong wind, {in which is fire, so it was burned}; and he has weak offspring, and he is weak, having been struck by old age. This condition is among the most dreadful conditions. Therefore this example begins with the words {Would any of you like...}, up to its end, with a question whose dreadfulness is established for the addressees. For its destruction all at once, after the lushness of its trees and the ripening of its fruit, is a great calamity; then the occurrence of this disaster while its owner is old, has become weak for work, and has weak offspring who give him no help and whose maintenance falls upon him, is another disaster. Thus the owner of this example, who did a deed for Allah and then nullified it with something contrary to it, resembles the condition of the owner of the garden, upon which befell what befell, at the time when he most needed it.

The third example is the one who shows off to people while having no faith in Allah and no expectation of His reward, whose heart is likened to a {smooth rock} (safwan), which is a smooth stone with some soil upon it; the observer thinks that if rain reaches it, it will grow as good lands grow. But it is like a stone which was struck by a heavy rain, which removed the soil upon it and left it bare ({saldan}). This is an exact likeness of the heart of the one who shows off, in which there is no faith, but rather it is hard and does not soften or humble itself. So his deeds and his spending have no root upon which to be founded and no end to which they lead; rather, whatever he does is void because its condition is lacking.

The one before it was nullified after the condition existed, because of the presence of an obstacle; and the first is accepted and multiplied because its condition exists, which is faith, sincerity, steadfastness, and the absence of corrupting obstacles. These three examples apply to all who act, so let the servant weigh himself and others by these just measures and exact likenesses: {And these examples We set forth for people, but none understands them except the knowing} (Q. 29:43).

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verses 267–268:

{267–268} The Creator (al-Bari) urges His servants to spend (infaq) from what they have earned through trade, and from what He has brought forth for them from the earth, such as grains and fruits. This includes the zakat on the two precious metals (gold and silver) and on all goods prepared for sale and purchase, as well as what comes out of the earth, such as grains and fruits. Its general wording encompasses both the obligatory (fard) and the voluntary (nafl) spending. He, exalted is He, commanded them to intend the good (tayyib) of these things and not to intend the bad (khabith), which is the inferior, base kind that they set aside for God, yet if someone who had a right over them offered it to them, they would not accept it, and would only take it grudgingly and with averted eyes. The obligation is to give out the middling (wasat) of these things, while the perfection is to give out the best (ali). What is forbidden is giving out the inferior, for this does not suffice for the obligation, and does not bring complete reward in the recommended (mandub) act.

{And know that God is Rich, Praiseworthy.} He is Rich above all created beings, and He is the One who is free of the expenditures of those who spend and of the acts of obedience of those who obey. He commanded them to it and urged them to it only for their benefit and out of pure grace and generosity toward them. Yet, with the perfection of His richness and the vastness of His bounties, He is Praiseworthy (al-Hamid) in what He legislates for His servants of rulings that lead them to the Abode of Peace (dar al-salam), and Praiseworthy in His actions, which never depart from grace, justice and wisdom, and Praiseworthy in His attributes, for all His attributes are perfections and excellences whose reality the servants cannot reach nor fully describe. When He urged them to beneficial spending, He forbade them from harmful withholding, and He explained to them that they stand between two callers: the caller of the Most Merciful (Dai al-Rahman), who calls them to good and promises them good, grace and reward, both immediate and deferred, and the replacement of what they spent; and the caller of Satan, who urges them to withhold and frightens them that if they spend they will become poor.

So whoever answers the call of the Most Merciful and spends from what God has provided him, let him be given good news of the forgiveness of sins and the attainment of every desired thing. And whoever answers the call of Satan, he is only calling his party so that they may be among the companions of the Blaze (al-sa'ir). So let the servant choose whichever of the two is more fitting for him.

He concluded the verse by saying {Vast, All-Knowing}; that is, vast in attributes and abundant in gifts, All-Knowing of who deserves multiplication among the doers, and All-Knowing of who is worthy, so that He grants him success in doing good and abandoning what is evil.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 269:

{269} When He mentioned the states of those who spend their wealth, and that Allah had given them and bestowed upon them wealth by which they are able to fund expenditures in good causes and attain lofty ranks, He mentioned what is better than that, namely that He gives wisdom (al-hikmah) to whomever He wills of His servants, and to whomever He intends good among His creation. Wisdom (al-hikmah) is beneficial knowledge, correct understanding, sound intellect, judicious minds, and hitting upon what is right in statements and actions. This is the best of gifts and the most magnificent of bestowals. For this reason He said: ﴿And whoever is given wisdom has certainly been given much good﴾, because he has come out of the darkness of ignorance into the light of guidance, and from the foolishness of deviation in statements and actions to hitting upon what is right in them and attaining rectitude. And because he has perfected himself with this great good and has readied himself to benefit creation with the greatest benefit in their religion and their worldly affairs. All matters are only set right by wisdom, which is placing things in their proper places, assigning affairs to their proper stations, advancing where advancing is due, and holding back where holding back is due.
But this great matter is not remembered, and the magnitude of this great gift is not recognized, ﴿except by those of understanding﴾; and they are the people of complete intellects and perfect forbearance, who recognize what is beneficial and do it, and recognize what is harmful and avoid it. These two matters, namely spending wealth and spending knowledge (al-hikmah al-'ilmiyyah), are the best means by which those who draw near to Allah draw near, and the highest means by which they reach the most honorable dignities. These are the two that the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned when he said: "There is no envy except in two: a man whom Allah has given wealth and has empowered him to spend it in truth, and a man whom Allah has given wisdom and he teaches it to the people."

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verses 270–271:

{270 – 271} He, may He be exalted, informs that whatever the spenders spend, or whatever the almsgivers give in charity, or whatever the vowers vow, indeed Allah knows it. The implication of the information about His knowledge indicates the recompense, and that Allah does not lose, in His sight, even the weight of an atom (mithqal dharra), and that He knows the good or bad intentions from which they proceed. And that the wrongdoers who withhold what Allah has made obligatory upon them, or who plunge into what He has forbidden to them, have no helpers besides Him who could aid them and protect them. And that punishments must surely befall them.

He informed that if the one giving charity displays it, then it is good; and if he conceals it and hands it to the poor person, that is better, because concealing it from the poor person is another form of kindness, and also because it indicates the strength of sincerity. Among the seven whom Allah will shade in His shade is the one who gives charity and conceals it until his left hand does not know what his right hand has spent.

In His saying: ﴿And if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you﴾, there is a subtle benefit: that concealing it is better than displaying it when it is given to the poor person.

As for when it is spent on a charitable public project, there is nothing in the verse indicating the virtue of concealing it. Rather, the rules of the Sharia here indicate observing the public interest, so displaying it may be better, because it results in setting an example, encouraging emulation, and stirring people's souls toward acts of goodness.

His saying: ﴿And He will remove from you some of your misdeeds﴾; in this there is that charities combine two matters: the attainment of good, which is the abundance of good deeds, reward and recompense; and the averting of evil and calamity, worldly and otherworldly, through the expiation of misdeeds.

﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾; so He will recompense each one according to his deed, in accordance with His wisdom.

{272} That is: Your duty, O Messenger, is only to convey (the message) and to urge people toward good and warn them against evil. As for guidance, it is in the hand of God, exalted is He.

He also states, as a sure truth, that the believers do not spend except seeking the pleasure of their Lord and expecting His reward, because their faith calls them to this. This is good news and a purification for the believers, and it contains a reminder to them of sincerity. And He repeated His knowledge of their spending to inform them that nothing is lost in His sight, not even the weight of an atom: ﴿and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it, and gives from Himself a great reward﴾.

{273} This means that you should direct your charity toward the poor who have confined themselves to the cause of God and to His obedience, and who have no will to earn or no ability to do so. They are restrained (in asking), so that the ignorant person thinks they are wealthy, {they do not ask people persistently}; rather, they do not ask at all, and even if they are compelled to ask, they do not press their request insistently. This category of the poor is the best recipient of expenditures, to relieve their need, to help them achieve their aim and the path of goodness, and in gratitude for their patience and for looking to the Creator rather than to creation. Nevertheless, spending in channels of benevolence and upon the needy wherever they are is good, a reward and a recompense with God. For this reason He said:

{274} {Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and openly, will have their reward with their Lord, and there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve}. His saying {will have their reward with their Lord} means: each one of them according to his state. The specification that it is "with their Lord" indicates the nobility of this condition and its occurring in the greatest station, as in the authentic hadith: «Indeed, a servant gives in charity a date from good earnings, and the Almighty receives it with His hand, and nurtures it for one of you just as one of you nurtures his foal, until it becomes like a great mountain» (ﷺ).

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 2, verse 275–281:

{275} When Allah mentioned the state of those who spend, and what they have from Allah of good things, and that He expiates their sins and misdeeds, He mentioned the wrongdoers, the people of riba (usury) and corrupt transactions, and informed that they will be recompensed according to their deeds. Just as, in the world, they were in pursuit of corrupt gains like madmen, so they are punished in the barzakh (intermediate realm) and on the Day of Resurrection by not rising from their graves until the day they are raised and resurrected. {Those who devour usury will not stand except as one stands whom Satan has driven to madness by his touch.} That is: from insanity and epilepsy. This is a punishment, disgrace and humiliation for them, and a recompense for their usury and their openly declaring, by their saying: {Trade is only like usury}. Thus they combined, through their audacity, between what Allah had made lawful and what Allah had made unlawful, and by this they permitted usury. Then Allah, exalted is He, offered repentance to the usurers and others, saying: {So whoever has received an admonition from his Lord} – an explanation accompanied by promise and warning – {and desists} from what he used to engage in of usury, {for him is what has passed} of what he had dared to do and repented from, {and his affair is up to Allah} regarding what lies ahead of his time. If he persists in his repentance, then Allah does not waste the reward of the good-doers. {But whoever returns} after Allah's clarification, reminder and warning against consuming usury, {those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally}. In this is evidence that usury necessitates entry into the Fire and eternal abiding therein, due to its heinousness, as long as no preventing factor from eternal abiding, which is faith, is present. This is among the rulings that depend on the existence of their conditions and the absence of their impediments. There is no proof in it for the Khawarij, as with other verses of warning. It is obligatory to affirm all the texts of the Book and the Sunnah, so the servant believes what the texts have transmitted with certainty concerning the exit from the Fire of whoever has in his heart even the least weight of a mustard seed of faith, and concerning the deserving of these grave sins of entry into the Fire if one does not repent from them.

{276} Then Allah informed that He eliminates the gains of the usurers and makes the charities of those who spend grow, the reverse of what occurs to the minds of many people, that spending diminishes wealth and usury increases it. For the source of provision and the attainment of its fruits is from Allah, exalted is He, and what is with Allah is not attained except by obeying Him and complying with His command. So the one who dares to engage in usury is punished with the opposite of his aim. This is observed by experience, and who is more truthful than Allah in speech? {Allah does not love every ungrateful sinner}; that is, one who denies the blessing of Allah, rejects the favour of his Lord, and sins by persisting in his disobedience. The implication of the verse is that Allah loves whoever is thankful for blessings and repentant from sins and wrongdoings. Then He placed this verse between the verses on usury, namely His saying:

{277–279} {Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds and establish prayer and give zakah} – the verse is to explain that the greatest means of avoiding what Allah has forbidden of usurious gains is the perfection of faith and its rights, especially establishing prayer and giving zakah, for prayer forbids immorality and wrongdoing, and zakah is kindness to creation which is incompatible with engaging in usury, which is injustice toward them and harm done to them. Then He addressed the believers and commanded them to be mindful of Allah and to leave what remains of the usurious transactions that they used to engage in before, and that if they do not do so, they are at war with Allah and His Messenger. This is among the greatest indications of the heinousness of usury, in that He made the one who persists in it a warrior against Allah and His Messenger. Then He said: {And if you repent} – meaning from usurious transactions – {then you have your capital; you do not wrong} the people by taking usury, {and you are not wronged} by having your capital diminished. So whoever repents from usury, if they were past transactions, then for him is what has passed and his matter is under review; and if they were existing transactions, it becomes obligatory upon him to restrict himself to his capital, and if he takes an excess, he has dared to engage in usury. In this verse is an explanation of the wisdom of prohibiting usury, and that it includes injustice toward the needy by taking the excess and multiplying usury upon them, whereas it is obligatory to grant them respite. For this reason He said:

{280–281} {And if the debtor is in hardship, then let there be postponement until a time of ease} – that is: if the one who owes the debt is insolvent and unable to pay, it is obligatory upon his creditor to grant him respite until a time of ease. It is obligatory upon him, when he obtains the means to pay by any lawful way, to pay what he owes. And if his creditor gives him charity by remitting the entire debt or part of it, that is better for him. This eases for the servant the undertaking of the legislated matters, avoiding usurious transactions, and kindness to the insolvent, through his knowledge that there is a day on which he will return to Allah, and He will repay him his deeds, and He will not wrong him by an atom's weight. As this verse was concluded by His saying: {And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah; then every soul will be fully compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.} Then Allah, exalted is He, said:

{282} These verses contain Allah's guidance to His servants in their transactions, directing them to protect their rights through beneficial means and sound arrangements, beyond which sensible people can propose nothing higher or more complete. They contain many benefits:

Among them: transactions involving debts are permitted, whether they are debts of salam (advance sale) or a purchase whose price is deferred. All of these are lawful, because Allah reports them of the believers, and what He reports of the believers is among the requirements of faith, and the Sovereign, the Judge, has approved it for them.

Among them: it is obligatory to specify the term (ajal) in all loans and to fix the terms of leases.

Among them: if the term is unknown, it is not permitted, because it involves gharar (uncertainty and risk), and so it falls under maysir (gambling).

Among them: Allah's command to write down debts. This command may be obligatory when preserving a right requires it, such as the wealth of orphans, endowments (awqaf), agents and trustees. It may also approach obligation where the right belongs purely to the servant; the obligation may grow stronger or the recommendation (istihbab) may grow stronger, according to the circumstances that call for it. In every case, writing is among the greatest means of safeguarding deferred transactions, because of how often people forget, how often disputes arise through confusion, and as a safeguard against treacherous people who do not fear Allah, the Exalted.

Among them: Allah's command to the scribe to write between the two parties with justice, so that he does not lean toward either of them out of kinship or any other reason, nor against either of them out of enmity or the like.

Among them: writing between the two parties is among the best deeds and a kindness to both of them, and it preserves their rights and clears their obligations, as Allah has commanded. Therefore, let the scribe seek reward from Allah for these matters among the people, so that he may obtain its recompense.

Among them: the scribe must know justice and be known for justice, for if he does not know justice he cannot carry it out, and if he is not trusted, upright and acceptable among people, his writing will not be reliable and the purpose for which it exists, which is the preservation of rights, will not be achieved.

Among them: part of the completeness of writing and of justice in it is that the scribe composes the document well and uses the wording appropriate to each transaction, and custom (urf) holds great weight in this matter.

Among them: writing is one of Allah's blessings upon His servants, without which neither their religious nor their worldly affairs are set right. Whoever Allah has taught writing has been granted a great favour. Part of thanking Allah for this blessing is that a person meets the needs of the servants through his writing and does not refuse to write. This is why He said: ﴿And let no scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him﴾.

Among them: what the scribe writes is the acknowledgment (iqrar) of the one who owes the right, if he can express clearly the right he owes. If he cannot do so, due to being a minor, foolish, insane, mute, or unable, then his guardian dictates on his behalf, and the guardian stands in his place in this matter.

Among them: acknowledgment is among the greatest means by which rights are established, since Allah commanded that the scribe write down what the one owing the right dictates to him.

Among them: the establishment of guardianship over those who lack capacity, such as minors, the insane, the foolish and the like.

Among them: the guardian stands in the place of the one under his guardianship in all acknowledgments relating to that person's rights.

Among them: whoever you entrust with a transaction and delegate to, his word in that matter is accepted, and he is your deputy. Since the guardian over those lacking capacity stands in their place, then the one you have chosen and to whom you have delegated the matter by your own choice has even greater claim to acceptance, and his word is to be considered and preferred over yours in case of disagreement.

Among them: when the one owing a right dictates to the scribe, he must fear Allah and not diminish the right he owes, neither in its amount, nor its description, nor in any of its conditions or stipulations. Rather, he must acknowledge all that is attached to the right, just as it is required when the right is owed to him by someone else. Whoever fails to do so is among those who defraud (al-mutaffifin al-bakhisin).

Among them: it is obligatory to acknowledge rights, both the apparent and the hidden, and this is among the greatest qualities of taqwa (piety), just as failing to acknowledge them undermines and diminishes piety.

Among them: guidance toward calling witnesses in sale. If it concerns debts, its ruling is the ruling of writing, as already mentioned, because writing here is the writing of testimony. If the sale is an immediate sale, it is recommended to call witnesses, and there is no fault in not writing it down, because such sales are very frequent and writing them would cause hardship.

Among them: guidance toward calling two just male witnesses. If this is not possible, or is impossible or difficult, then one man and two women. This applies to all transactions: sales, loans and their attachments, including conditions, documents and other things. It has been said: it is established that the Prophet (ﷺ) judged by a single witness together with an oath. The noble verse mentions only two men or one man and two women. The answer is that the noble verse provides guidance from Allah to His servants on preserving their rights, and therefore it cites the most complete and strongest means. It contains nothing that contradicts what the Prophet (ﷺ) stated about judgment by a witness and an oath. The principle of preserving rights at the outset guides the servant toward complete caution and safeguarding, while the principle of judging between disputants looks to the preponderant evidence and proofs according to their circumstances.

Among them: the testimony of two women stands in place of one man in worldly rights. In religious matters, such as narration of hadith and giving fatwa, a woman stands in place of a man, and the difference between these two areas is clear.

Among them: guidance toward the wisdom behind the testimony of two women being equal to one man, namely that a woman's memory is generally weaker and a man's memory stronger.

Among them: if a witness forgets his testimony and the other witness reminds him, and he then recalls it, that forgetting does not harm the testimony once it is removed by reminding, based on His saying: ﴿that if one of them errs, the other may remind her﴾. How much more so, if the witness forgets and then recalls without being reminded, since testimony rests upon knowledge and certainty.

Among them: testimony must be based on knowledge and certainty, not on doubt. Whenever the witness has doubt about his testimony, even if it is merely a strong presumption, it is not lawful for him to testify except to what he knows.

Among them: a witness may not refuse when he is called to give testimony, whether he is called to bear it or to deliver it. Upholding testimony is among the best righteous deeds, as Allah commanded it and informed of its benefit and its good outcomes.

Among them: it is not lawful to harm the scribe or the witness by making them testify at a time or in a condition that would harm them. Just as the parties to rights and the contracting people are forbidden to harm the witnesses and scribes, the scribe and the witness are likewise forbidden to harm the two contracting parties or either of them. This also indicates that if harm befalls the scribe or the witness in writing or testifying, the obligation falls from them.

Among the lessons in it: alerting that all who do good and perform acts of kindness must not be harmed or burdened with what they cannot bear. Is the reward for good anything but good? Likewise, whoever does good and performs a kindness must complete his goodness by refraining from harming, by word or by deed, the one to whom the kindness was done, for goodness is not complete without that.

Among them: it is not permitted to take payment for writing or testifying when they are obligatory, because it is a right that Allah has imposed upon the scribe and the witness, and because it amounts to harming the contracting parties.

Among them: alerting to the benefits and advantages that follow from acting upon these noble instructions, namely the preservation of rights and justice, the ending of disputes, and safety from forgetfulness and heedlessness. This is why He said: ﴿That is more equitable in the sight of Allah, more upright for testimony, and nearer to preventing you from doubt﴾. These are necessary benefits for the servants.

Among them: learning to write is one of the religious matters, because it is a means to preserving both religion and worldly life, and a cause of goodness.

Among them: whoever Allah has favoured with a blessing that people need must, as part of thanking Allah for it, bring benefit through it to the servants of Allah and meet their needs with it. The prohibition against refusing to write is grounded in the reminder to the scribe in His saying: ﴿as Allah has taught him﴾. Moreover, whoever is in his brother's need, Allah is in his need.

Among them: harming witnesses and scribes is wickedness (fusuq) on the part of the one who does it. Fusuq is leaving the obedience of Allah for His disobedience. It increases, decreases and is divided. For this reason He did not say ﴿you are wicked﴾ or ﴿you are wicked people﴾, but rather said: ﴿for it is wickedness in you﴾. The servant's wickedness corresponds to the degree to which he departs from obedience to his Lord. From His saying: ﴿Fear Allah, and Allah will teach you﴾, it is derived that the fear of Allah is a means to obtaining knowledge. Even clearer is His saying: ﴿O you who believe, if you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion (furqan)﴾, i.e., knowledge by which you distinguish realities, and truth from falsehood.

Among them: just as teaching religious matters related to acts of worship is beneficial knowledge, so too is teaching worldly matters related to transactions, for Allah has preserved for His servants the affairs of their religion and their worldly life, and His mighty Book contains the explanation of everything.

Among them: the legitimacy of securing rights by means of documentation, namely pledges and guarantees that ensure the servant obtains his right, whether the other party is righteous or wicked, trustworthy or treacherous. How many benefits there are in documentation: the preservation of rights and the ending of disputes.

Among them: the completion of documentation in pledging requires that the pledge be taken into possession. This does not mean that a pledge is valid only with possession. Rather, specifying that the pledge be in possession indicates that it may be in possession, which secures complete confidence, or it may not be, in which case it is deficient.

Among them: it is derived from His saying: {283} ﴿so pledges taken in hand﴾ that if the pledgor and the pledgee disagree about the amount of the debt for which the pledge was given, the word of the pledgee, the holder of the right, is accepted. This is because Allah made the pledge a guarantee for the debt; were his word not accepted on this matter, the pledge would not serve as security, given the absence of writing and witnesses.

Among them: it is permitted to deal without documentation and without witnesses, based on His saying: ﴿But if one of you trusts another, let the one who is trusted fulfil his trust﴾. In this case, however, one needs piety and fear of Allah, otherwise the holder of the right is exposed to risk regarding his right. This is why, in this situation, Allah commanded the one who owes the right to fear Allah and fulfil his trust.

Among them: whoever is entrusted in a transaction has done him a great kindness and has been pleased with his religion and trustworthiness. Therefore, it becomes especially binding on the one who owes the right to fulfil the trust in two respects: to fulfil the right of Allah and carry out His command, and to fulfil the right of his companion, who was pleased with his trustworthiness and placed his confidence in him.

Among them: the prohibition of concealing testimony. Whoever conceals it has sinned in his heart, which is the king of the limbs. This is because concealing testimony is like bearing false witness: it entails the loss of rights, the corruption of transactions, and repeated sin on his part and on the part of the one who owes the right. As for restricting the pledge to travel, although it is permitted both at home and on a journey, this is because of the need for it when there is no scribe or witness. The verse concludes by saying that He is All-Knowing of everything the servants do, as an encouragement to good transactions and a warning against evil ones.
